Private Label Cosmetics: White-Label Printing Solutions for Contract Manufacturers

White Label Printing Solutions for Private Label Cosmetics

The white label printing solutions market for cosmetics is booming as the industry reaches $25.8 billion by 2027. For contract manufacturers, this explosion in demand creates both opportunity and challenge: how do you efficiently label hundreds of different white label brands without drowning in setup fees and inventory chaos?

Relying on outside vendors for your white label printing solutions often means dealing with long lead times, frustrating minimum orders, and lack of control. Bringing white label printing solutions in-house with variable data digital printing puts you back in control.

Key Takeaways

  • White Label Printing Solutions Eliminate Setup Costs: Print on-demand for different clients without $150-$400 setup fees.
  • Speed and Flexibility: White label printing solutions reduce lead times from 2-3 weeks to 2-3 days.
  • Massive Savings: White label printing solutions save $100,000-$160,000 annually vs traditional printing.

What Are White Label Printing Solutions?

White label printing solutions enable contract manufacturers to produce custom-branded labels for multiple clients using a single production run. These white label printing solutions use variable data technology to swap brand names, logos, and product information automatically.

Unlike traditional printing, white label printing solutions don’t require separate plates for each unique design. This makes white label printing solutions ideal for contract manufacturers serving 20-50+ clients with different branding needs.

AspectWhite LabelPrivate Label
FormulationPre-made formulasCustom-developed
ExclusivityMultiple brandsOne brand only
Speed2-4 weeks3-6 months

Both benefit from white label printing solutions for flexible, on-demand label production.

The Challenge Without White Label Printing Solutions

Without white label printing solutions, contract manufacturers face:

  • $150-$400 setup fees per design
  • 1,000-5,000 minimum order quantities
  • 2-3 week lead times
  • Massive inventory headaches

A typical manufacturer serving the cosmetics market manages 300+ unique label designs. Without white label printing solutions, each requires separate print runs and inventory tracking.

How White Label Printing Solutions Work

White label printing solutions start with a master template containing variable fields for brand names, logos, and product data. You populate a spreadsheet with each client’s information, and the printer automatically customizes each label.

One production run using white label printing solutions can serve 20 different clients with completely different branded labels—no plate changes required.

title.rendered: FDA Cosmetic Labeling Requirements 2026: Complete Guide to Cosmetic Label Compliance & INCI Names

content.rendered:
Table of Contents

FDA Cosmetic Labeling Requirements 2026: Complete Guide to Cosmetic Label Compliance & INCI Names

Cosmetic Label Regulations 2026: FDA Requirements, Ingredient Lists & INCI Compliance

The Regulatory Landscape for Cosmetic Labels

Cosmetic labeling isn’t just about aesthetics—it’s a heavily regulated communication channel between brands and consumers. The FDA, FTC, and state regulators enforce strict requirements on what must appear on cosmetic labels, how it must be formatted, and what claims can be made.

For 2026, several factors are increasing regulatory scrutiny:

  • The Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act (MoCRA) of 2022 is now fully implemented
  • State-level “clean beauty” legislation is expanding
  • Consumer lawsuits over misleading claims are at record highs
  • Import regulations for international brands have tightened

This guide breaks down the current FDA requirements for cosmetic labels, explains INCI naming conventions, and provides a compliance checklist for beauty brands. We’ll also cover how the ArrowJet Nova 250R’s precision printing capabilities help ensure your labels meet these demanding standards.

Explore More

The Regulatory Landscape for Cosmetic Labels

Required Label Elements

Every cosmetic product sold in the United States must include these elements on its label:

1. Identity Statement (Product Name)

Requirements:

  • Must accurately describe the product
  • Must be prominent and conspicuous
  • Should indicate form (cream, lotion, serum, etc.)

Examples:

  • ✓ “Hydrating Facial Moisturizer Cream”
  • ✓ “Volumizing Mascara”
  • ✗ “Youth Serum” (vague/ambiguous)

2. Net Contents

Requirements:

  • Must appear on the principal display panel (front of package)
  • Must be parallel to the base of the package
  • Minimum type size based on package size

Format by Product Type:

  • Liquids: Fluid measure (fl oz, mL)
  • Solids/Powders: Weight (oz, g)
  • Aerosols: Net weight plus volume equivalent

Type Size Requirements:

Package SizeMinimum Type Size
≤ 5 sq in1/16 inch (1.6mm)
5-25 sq in1/8 inch (3.2mm)
25-100 sq in3/16 inch (4.8mm)
> 100 sq in1/4 inch (6.4mm)

3. Ingredient Declaration

Requirements:

  • Must appear on an information panel (can be back or side)
  • Ingredients listed in descending order by weight
  • Must use INCI (International Nomenclature of Cosmetic Ingredients) names
  • Must be conspicuous and legible

Type Size: Minimum 1/16 inch (1.6mm) for packages > 5 sq in

4. Name and Place of Business

Requirements:

  • Manufacturer, packer, or distributor name
  • Business address (street, city, state, ZIP)
  • May use distributor name if preceded by “Manufactured for” or “Distributed by”

5. Warning Statements (When Required)

Products Requiring Warnings:

Product TypeRequired Warning
Feminine deodorant sprays“Caution: For external use only”
Products containing AHASunburn alert and sunscreen recommendation
Products containing talc“Keep powder away from child’s face”
Eyelash/brow dyesProfessional use only warning
Products with high alcohol contentFlammability warning

Prohibited Label Elements

The FDA prohibits certain claims and statements:

  • Drug claims: Cannot claim to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent disease
  • Misleading claims: Cannot be false or misleading in any particular
  • Unapproved color additives: Only FDA-certified colors permitted
  • Interstate commerce of adulterated products: Products that are injurious to users

Common Violation Examples:

  • ✗ “Treats acne” (drug claim)
  • ✗ “Reduces wrinkles by 50%” (unsubstantiated claim)
  • ✗ “Cures eczema” (disease claim)
  • ✗ “Prevents skin cancer” (disease prevention claim)

INCI Naming: The Universal Language of Cosmetic Ingredients

What Is INCI?

The International Nomenclature of Cosmetic Ingredients (INCI) is a standardized system of names for cosmetic ingredients maintained by the Personal Care Products Council (PCPC). INCI names are:

  • Recognized internationally
  • Required by FDA regulations
  • Scientifically derived
  • Used on cosmetic labels worldwide

Why INCI Matters

Regulatory Compliance:
Using common names instead of INCI names is a violation. “Vitamin E” must be listed as “Tocopherol” or “Tocopheryl Acetate.”

Consumer Transparency:
INCI provides consistency so consumers can identify ingredients regardless of brand or country of origin.

Scientific Accuracy:
Common names are often ambiguous. “Almond oil” could be sweet almond or bitter almond—very different safety profiles.

Common INCI Translations

Common NameINCI Name
Vitamin ETocopherol
Vitamin CAscorbic Acid
Vitamin ARetinol
Hyaluronic AcidSodium Hyaluronate
Aloe VeraAloe Barbadensis Leaf Juice
Green TeaCamellia Sinensis Leaf Extract
Coconut OilCocos Nucifera Oil
Shea ButterButyrospermum Parkii Butter
Jojoba OilSimmondsia Chinensis Seed Oil
Rosehip OilRosa Canina Fruit Oil
Lavender OilLavandula Angustifolia Oil
Tea Tree OilMelaleuca Alternifolia Leaf Oil
Vitamin B5Panthenol
GlycerinGlycerin (or Glycerol)
AlcoholAlcohol Denat.
Witch HazelHamamelis Virginiana Water
ChamomileChamomilla Recutita Flower Extract
Argan OilArgania Spinosa Kernel Oil

Complex Ingredient Names

Many cosmetic ingredients have complex INCI names that challenge label space:

Surfactants:

  • Sodium Laureth Sulfate
  • Cocamidopropyl Betaine
  • Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate

Emulsifiers:

  • Cetearyl Alcohol (and) Ceteareth-20
  • Glyceryl Stearate SE
  • Polysorbate 60

Preservatives:

  • Phenoxyethanol (and) Ethylhexylglycerin
  • Sodium Benzoate (and) Potassium Sorbate
  • Caprylyl Glycol (and) Phenoxyethanol (and) Hexylene Glycol

Silicones:

  • Dimethicone
  • Cyclopentasiloxane
  • Trimethylsiloxysilicate

Formatting INCI Lists

Rules:

  1. Descending order by concentration (highest to lowest)
  2. Ingredients ≤1% can be listed in any order after those >1%
  3. Color additives may be listed in any order after ingredients >1%
  4. Fragrance/Parfum can be listed as a single ingredient
  5. “May contain” list for color variations

Example:

Ingredients: Water (Aqua), Glycerin, Cetearyl Alcohol, Cocos Nucifera (Coconut) Oil,
Butyrospermum Parkii (Shea) Butter, Dimethicone, Phenoxyethanol,
Tocopherol (Vitamin E), Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Juice, Fragrance (Parfum),
May Contain: Titanium Dioxide (CI 77891), Iron Oxides (CI 77491, CI 77492, CI 77499)

MoCRA 2022: New Requirements for 2026

The Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022 significantly expanded FDA authority over cosmetics. Key provisions now in effect:

1. Facility Registration

Requirement:

  • All cosmetic manufacturing facilities must register with FDA
  • Registration must be renewed every two years
  • Must update within 60 days of changes

Impact on Labeling:
Labels must now include accurate manufacturer information that matches FDA registration.

2. Product Listing

Requirement:

  • All cosmetic products must be listed with FDA
  • Must include ingredient list at time of listing
  • Must update annually or when formulation changes

Impact on Labeling:
Labels must match the ingredient list submitted to FDA exactly.

3. Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP)

Requirement:

  • FDA can establish mandatory GMP regulations
  • Must follow industry standards until regulations finalized

Impact on Labeling:
Labels must accurately reflect contents (GMP requires consistent formulation).

4. Adverse Event Reporting

Requirement:

  • Serious adverse events must be reported to FDA within 15 days
  • Must maintain records for 6 years

Impact on Labeling:
Contact information on labels must be current for adverse event reporting.

5. Safety Substantiation

Requirement:

  • Must maintain records supporting product safety
  • FDA can access these records

Impact on Labeling:
Claims must be supported by safety data (e.g., “dermatologist-tested” requires testing records).

6. Fragrance Allergen Disclosure (Coming)

Expected 2026-2027:

  • Will require disclosure of fragrance allergens on labels
  • Likely to follow EU model (26 common allergens)

Impact on Labeling:
Labels will need to identify specific fragrance allergens, not just “Fragrance (Parfum).”

State-Level Requirements

California

Proposition 65:

  • Must warn if product contains chemicals known to cause cancer or reproductive harm
  • Over 900 chemicals on the list
  • Warning format specified by law
  • Heavy penalties for non-compliance

Safe Cosmetics Act:

  • Requires reporting of ingredients linked to cancer or reproductive toxicity
  • Affects labeling indirectly (must know ingredients to report)

Washington

Toxic-Free Cosmetics Act (2025):

  • Bans specific chemicals in cosmetics
  • Requires disclosure of certain chemicals
  • Affects both formulation and labeling

New York

Disclosure Requirements:

  • Some ingredients require additional disclosure
  • Specific labeling for certain product categories

Common Labeling Compliance Mistakes

1. Ingredient Order Errors

Mistake: Listing active ingredients first, then inactive (drug format) on cosmetic products.

Correct: All cosmetics list ingredients in descending order by weight, regardless of function.

2. INCI Name Mistakes

Mistake: Using common names like “Vitamin E” or “Shea Butter” instead of INCI names.

Correct: Use Tocopherol and Butyrospermum Parkii Butter.

3. Type Size Violations

Mistake: Net contents or ingredient list in font too small for package size.

Correct: Measure carefully; FDA checks type size.

4. Drug Claims on Cosmetics

Mistake: Claims like “treats acne,” “cures eczema,” or “prevents aging.”

Correct: Use cosmetic claims: “cleanses,” “moisturizes,” “improves appearance.”

5. Missing Information Panel

Mistake: Putting all information on the front of the package.

Correct: Ingredient list and business information on an information panel (back or side).

6. International Products

Mistake: Using EU or Asian labeling formats for US market.

Correct: US has specific requirements; EU format alone isn’t compliant.

The ArrowJet Nova 250R: Precision for Compliance

Why Print Quality Matters for Compliance

Small type requirements (1/16 inch minimum) demand high-resolution printing. Blurry, illegible ingredient lists violate FDA regulations.

Nova 250R Compliance Features

1600×1600 dpi Resolution:

  • Crisp, legible text at small sizes
  • INCI names with complex characters print clearly
  • Ingredient lists remain readable even on small labels

Precise Registration:

  • Multi-color labels maintain sharp edges
  • Text doesn’t blur into graphics
  • Professional appearance supports brand positioning

Print-and-Cut Integration:

  • Precise label shapes for various package types
  • Consistent sizing batch to batch
  • Clean cuts that enhance legibility

Variable Data Capability:

  • Print different ingredient lists for product variations
  • Easily update labels when formulations change
  • Comply with MoCRA product listing updates

Substrate Versatility:

  • Print on materials that withstand cosmetic product environments
  • Oil-resistant, water-resistant options
  • Durability ensures labels remain legible through product life

Compliance Checklist for Cosmetic Labels

Before Production

  • All ingredients identified by INCI names
  • Ingredients ordered by descending weight
  • Net contents formatted correctly with appropriate units
  • Business name and address current and accurate
  • Required warning statements included
  • No prohibited drug claims present
  • Type sizes meet minimum requirements
  • Color additives listed appropriately
  • Fragrance listed as “Fragrance (Parfum)” or specific allergens

Regulatory Compliance

  • FDA facility registration current
  • Product listing submitted and accurate
  • GMP documentation maintained
  • Adverse event reporting procedures established
  • California Prop 65 warning included if required
  • State-specific requirements reviewed

Quality Control

  • Print quality legible at specified type sizes
  • Ingredient list matches submitted product listing
  • Proofread for spelling errors (especially INCI names)
  • Color consistency batch to batch
  • Label adhesion tested on actual packaging

Conclusion

Cosmetic label compliance is complex, detailed, and strictly enforced. The 2026 regulatory environment—with MoCRA fully implemented and state laws expanding—demands precision in both formulation documentation and label execution.

The foundation of compliance is accurate INCI ingredient naming, proper order of declaration, and adherence to type size and placement requirements. Violations aren’t just regulatory risks; they damage brand credibility and consumer trust.

The ArrowJet Nova 250R provides the print precision needed for compliant cosmetic labels. At 1600×1600 dpi, even complex INCI names in small type remain crisp and legible. Print-and-cut integration ensures professional presentation that reinforces compliance and brand quality.

For beauty brands, compliance isn’t a burden—it’s a competitive advantage. Accurate, professional labels signal attention to detail that extends from regulatory compliance to product quality.

title.rendered: The Real Cost of SKU Proliferation in Sachet Packaging: How to Control It (2026)

content.rendered:
Table of Contents

The Real Cost of SKU Proliferation in Sachet Packaging: How to Control It (2026)

What Is SKU Proliferation in Sachet Packaging?

SKU proliferation packaging is the rapid expansion of product variations that creates complexity and cost for brands. You started with one product. One SKU. One sachet design. Then customers asked for caffeine-free. Then sugar-free. Then travel-size packs. Then a holiday edition. Then a collaboration with that influencer.

Now you have 47 SKUs. And a sachet printing nightmare.

Every new variation means new printing plates, new inventory, new storage, new complexity. Traditional sachet printing turns SKU proliferation into a profit killer. But it doesn’t have to be this way.

This proven guide explains how multi SKU printing with digital technology eliminates the penalties of SKU management CPG operations face daily.

The Hidden Tax on Every New SKU The Traditional SKU Penalty

With rotogravure or flexographic sachet printing, each SKU carries fixed costs that don’t scale with volume:

Per-SKU Fixed Costs:

  • Gravure cylinders: $5,000-15,000 per design
  • Flexographic plates: $500-2,000 per color per SKU
  • Setup waste: 1,000-5,000 units per production run
  • Artwork prep: $200-500 for plate-ready files

The Math That Kills:

  • 10 SKUs x $8,000 average cylinder cost = $80,000 in setup costs
  • Before you print a single unit
  • Before you know if customers will buy

The Inventory Multiplication Problem

High minimum orders mean every SKU multiplies your inventory burden:

Example: 20 SKUs, 25,000-unit minimum each

  • Total inventory commitment: 500,000 units
  • At $0.50/unit = $250,000 tied up in flexible packaging short runs
  • Storage space: 2,500+ square feet
  • Obsolescence risk: If 5 SKUs fail, $62,500 in waste

This is why big CPG companies are constantly killing SKUs. The carrying costs devour profitability.

The Agility Penalty

When changing a SKU requires new plates:

  • Formula updates: New plates needed
  • Regulatory changes: New plates needed
  • Rebranding: New plates needed for every SKU
  • Seasonal variations: Prohibitively expensive

You’re locked into designs for years because changing them costs too much.

Why Brands Proliferate SKUs Anyway

Market Demand for Variety

Modern consumers expect choice in SKU proliferation packaging:

  • Flavors: Vanilla, chocolate, strawberry, unflavored
  • Sizes: Single-serve, 5-pack, 30-pack, bulk
  • Formulations: Regular, extra strength, caffeine-free, keto-friendly
  • Seasonal: Holiday editions, summer flavors, limited releases

The Long Tail Opportunity

E-commerce enables niche products:

  • Specialized diets (paleo, vegan, allergen-free)
  • Regional preferences
  • B2B customization
  • Personalized nutrition

Each niche is a potential SKU. But traditional sachet printing makes serving them unprofitable.

Competitive Pressure

When competitors launch new variants, you must respond:

  • They add a flavor
  • They partner with an influencer
  • They release a limited edition

Without affordable flexible packaging short runs, you can’t compete.

Sachet Printing: The SKU Proliferation Solution

Zero Fixed Costs Per SKU

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite uses digital inkjet technology that eliminates per-SKU setup costs for multi SKU printing:

Digital Economics:

  • Plate/cylinder costs: $0
  • Setup waste: Minimal (10-50 units)
  • Artwork changes: Digital file swap
  • Color additions: No additional cost

The New Math:

  • 10 SKUs x $0 setup = $0
  • 50 SKUs x $0 setup = $0
  • Print what you need, when you need it
Explore More

Print-on-Demand Inventory Model

Instead of stocking 25,000 units of each SKU:

  • Print 1,000 units of fast-moving SKUs weekly
  • Print 500 units of medium SKUs monthly
  • Print 100 units of slow SKUs as needed

Result: Same SKU variety, 90% less inventory.

Real-Time SKU Adjustment

When sales data shows:

  • Lemon-lime selling 3x faster → Increase print frequency
  • Tropical blend underperforming → Reduce to quarterly runs
  • Holiday edition sold out → Quick reprint without new plates

You’re optimizing your SKU management CPG mix in real-time, not guessing 6 months ahead.

Case Studies: SKU Proliferation Done Right

Case Study 1: The Electrolyte Brand with 40+ Flavors

Challenge: Sports nutrition company wanted flavor variety as a competitive differentiator but couldn’t afford 40 sets of gravure cylinders.

Traditional Reality:

  • 40 SKUs x $8,000 cylinders = $320,000 setup costs
  • 40 SKUs x 25,000 MOQ = 1,000,000 units minimum
  • Impossible for a startup

Digital Solution:

  • Launched with 40 flavors, 1,000 units each
  • Total startup cost: $20,000-30,000
  • Printed flavors based on weekly sales data
  • Killed 12 underperformers without waste
  • Doubled down on top 8 flavors

Result: 40-SKU portfolio, $0 obsolete inventory, data-driven product mix, acquired by major CPG within 2 years.

Case Study 2: The Tea Company's Seasonal Strategy

Challenge: Artisan tea brand wanted 12 seasonal blends (one per month) but couldn’t store 300,000 sachets (12 x 25,000).

Traditional Reality:

  • Storage costs: $15,000/year
  • Risk of expired product
  • Capital tied up: $150,000+

Digital Solution:

  • Print 5,000 units of current month’s blend
  • Previous month: 2,000 units (clearing remaining)
  • Next month: 1,000 units (building inventory)
  • Just-in-time production for 12 unique SKUs

Result: Zero storage costs for sachets, always-fresh product, authentic seasonal positioning, 35% higher margins.

Case Study 3: The Supplement Brand's B2B Pivot

Challenge: Nutraceutical company discovered B2B opportunity (gyms, hotels, corporate wellness) but each client wanted private label.

Traditional Reality:

  • Each private label client: $8,000-15,000 setup
  • Minimum 25,000 units per client
  • Only viable for massive chains, not mid-size

Digital Solution:

  • Private label minimum: 500 units
  • 50+ private label clients served
  • Each gets unique packaging without plate costs
  • Clients can test with small orders before scaling

Result: B2B revenue grew from 5% to 45% of total sales, 60+ active private label relationships.

The True Economics of SKU Flexibility

Cost Comparison: 20-SKU Portfolio

Cost CategoryTraditional PrintingDigital Sachet Printing
Setup costs$100,000-300,000$0
Initial inventory$250,000$25,000
Storage (annual)$12,000$1,200
Obsolescence (annual)$25,000$2,500
Total Year 1$387,000+$28,700

Assumes 20 SKUs, 25,000-unit traditional MOQ vs. 1,000-unit digital average

The ROI of SKU Agility

Beyond cost savings, flexible packaging short runs enable revenue opportunities:

Faster Time-to-Market:

  • New SKU launch: 2-3 days vs. 4-6 weeks
  • Capture trends before competitors
  • Respond to customer feedback instantly

Higher Hit Rate:

  • Test 10 concepts, scale the 3 winners
  • Kill losers early without waste
  • Improve SKU success rate from 20% to 60%

Premium Pricing:

  • Limited editions create urgency
  • Seasonal SKUs command 15-25% premium
  • Personalization adds 20-30% value

Managing 100+ SKUs: The Digital Playbook

Step 1: Categorize Your SKUs

A. Core SKUs (70% of volume)

  • High-velocity products
  • Print 2,000-5,000 units weekly
  • Stable, predictable demand

B. Seasonal/Promotional (20% of volume)

  • Limited-time offerings
  • Print 500-2,000 units per run
  • Variable timing

C. Long Tail (10% of volume)

  • Niche products
  • Print 100-500 units as needed
  • Infrequent orders

Step 2: Implement Dynamic Scheduling

Weekly Review:

  • Check inventory levels by SKU
  • Analyze sales velocity
  • Adjust print schedule

Monthly Optimization:

  • Review SKU performance
  • Identify candidates for discontinuation
  • Plan new launches

Quarterly Strategy:

  • Assess full portfolio
  • Reallocate capacity to winners
  • Test new concepts

Step 3: Leverage Variable Data

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite can print unique content on every sachet:

Batch/Lot Tracking:

  • Individual codes for traceability
  • QR codes linking to certificates
  • Expiration dates printed on-demand

Personalization:

  • Customer names on B2B orders
  • Different formulas for different segments
  • Regional variations

A/B Testing:

  • Test messaging on 500 units
  • Measure response rates
  • Scale winning messaging

Best Practices for SKU Portfolio Management

1. The 80/20 Rule Applied

80% of sales come from 20% of SKUs. With digital sachet printing:

  • Focus inventory on winners (high-velocity core SKUs)
  • Keep long tail lean (print to order)
  • Test aggressively (low cost of failure)

2. The Rule of Three

Limit active SKUs per “decision point” to 3:

  • 3 flavors (not 15)
  • 3 sizes (not 8)
  • 3 formulations (not 10)

Use multi SKU printing to rotate options seasonally rather than carrying everything.

3. Kill Criteria

Define when to discontinue an SKU:

  • Sales below X units/month for Y months
  • Margin below Z%
  • Inventory turns below W times/year

Digital sachet printing means killing SKUs doesn’t strand $50,000 in obsolete packaging.

4. Version Control

Track SKU versions:

  • Formula V1, V2, V3
  • Packaging Rev A, Rev B
  • Regulatory updates

Digital makes version transitions seamless.

Key Takeaways

  • SKU proliferation packaging doesn’t have to kill profitability
  • Traditional sachet printing adds $5,000-15,000 fixed cost per SKU
  • Digital multi SKU printing eliminates setup costs completely
  • Flexible packaging short runs reduce inventory by 90%
  • Print-on-demand enables real-time SKU management CPG optimization
  • Test 10 concepts, kill 7 losers, scale 3 winners—without waste
  • Seasonal and limited editions become profitable with short runs
  • Private label B2B becomes viable with 500-unit minimums

FAQs

What is SKU proliferation in packaging?

SKU proliferation packaging is the rapid expansion of product variations (flavors, sizes, formulations) that creates operational complexity and cost. In traditional sachet printing, each new SKU requires expensive plates or cylinders, making variety prohibitively expensive for small and mid-sized brands.

How much does each SKU cost with traditional printing?

With traditional sachet printing, each SKU carries $5,000-15,000 in fixed setup costs for gravure cylinders or $500-2,000 per color for flexographic plates. Plus 1,000-5,000 units of setup waste. Digital printing eliminates these costs entirely.

What is the minimum order quantity for digital sachet printing?

Digital sachet printing with systems like the ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite has no minimum order quantity. Print 100 units or 100,000 units—the setup cost is the same: $0. This enables true flexible packaging short runs.

How do I manage 50+ SKUs without massive inventory?

Categorize SKUs into Core (70% volume, print 2,000-5,000 weekly), Seasonal (20%, print 500-2,000 as needed), and Long Tail (10%, print 100-500 to order). This SKU management CPG strategy maintains variety while minimizing inventory.

Can I print different SKUs in the same production run?

Yes. Digital multi SKU printing allows you to print SKU A for 30 minutes, switch files, and print SKU B immediately. No plate changes, no setup time, no waste. Perfect for flexible packaging short runs.

What happens when I need to update a SKU design?

With digital sachet printing, design updates are instant. Upload the new file and the next sachet prints with the updated design. No new plates, no additional cost, no 4-6 week lead time.

  • CPG SKU Optimization Best Practices – Research on consumer goods portfolio management
  • Digital Printing for Flexible Packaging – Industry trends in multi SKU printing
  • Sustainable Packaging Solutions – Environmental benefits of print-on-demand

Conclusion

SKU proliferation packaging doesn’t have to be a cost center. With digital sachet printing, it becomes a competitive weapon:

  • Serve niche markets profitably
  • Test and iterate without massive bets
  • Respond instantly to market changes
  • Personalize at scale for premium pricing

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite transforms SKU flexibility from a luxury only big brands can afford into a tool accessible to businesses of any size. Stop fighting SKU management CPG challenges. Harness them with flexible packaging short runs.

Private Label Cosmetics: 7 Ways Digital Printing Transforms Contract Manufacturing

The White-Label Opportunity in Beauty Manufacturing

The beauty industry has fundamentally shifted. Heritage brands with decades of history now compete against agile newcomers, influencer-launched lines, and retailer house brands. This democratization has created explosive demand for contract manufacturing and white-label beauty products.

Today’s contract manufacturers serve diverse clients: indie founders testing concepts, social media influencers monetizing audiences, spas creating proprietary skincare lines, and retailers developing exclusive house brands. Each needs professional products. Each needs custom-branded labels. And each needs them produced rapidly, flexibly, and affordably.

But here’s the operational challenge: every client demands unique customization. Different brand identities. Distinct packaging designs. Varying product SKUs. Market-specific regulatory requirements. Traditional label printing—with rigid setup fees, high minimum orders, and lengthy lead times—struggles to profitably serve this fragmented, fast-moving market.

This guide explores how contract manufacturers can solve the white-label labeling challenge using modern variable data digital printing—converting what was once a production bottleneck into a genuine competitive advantage.

Understanding the Contract Manufacturing Labeling Challenge

Complexity Multiplied Across Clients

A typical beauty contract manufacturer might simultaneously support:

  • 25-50 active brand clients
  • Each client operating 5-15 individual product SKUs
  • Every SKU requiring unique branded labels
  • Frequent design iterations and new product launches
  • Varying compliance requirements across different markets

The mathematics become daunting quickly: 30 clients × 10 SKUs each = 300 unique label designs. Each design historically required separate print runs, individual inventory management, and careful version control.

Pain Points of Traditional Label Production

Setup Economics:

  • $150-$400 setup fee per unique design
  • 300 designs annually × $250 average = $75,000 in setup costs alone
  • These costs get passed to clients or absorbed as margin erosion

Volume Requirements:

  • Traditional minimums of 1,000-5,000 labels per SKU
  • Small brands forced to over-order or abandon launches entirely
  • Excess label inventory becomes a liability when formulations change

Production Timelines:

  • 2-3 weeks from order placement to delivery
  • Clients miss critical market windows and trend peaks
  • Rush production fees further erode profitability

Version Control Complexity:

  • Multiple design versions per product line
  • Obsolete inventory from formula updates or rebranding
  • Regulatory changes requiring complete label reprints

The Digital Printing Solution

What Is Variable Data Printing?

Variable Data Printing (VDP) enables production of unique information on each label using database-driven content. While conventional printing produces identical copies, VDP generates individualized labels at full production speeds.

For white-label beauty manufacturing:

  • One master template + client data file = unlimited brand variations
  • Continuous production runs with seamless brand switching
  • Instant design modifications without new printing plates
  • Each label produced on-demand as orders arrive

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R Advantage

Explore More

This production-grade variable data printer addresses the specific needs of high-changeover manufacturing environments:

Direct CSV Integration: Import client data straight from spreadsheets without middleware. Simple column mapping connects brand assets to template fields in minutes.

Regulatory-Grade Resolution: 1600×1600 dpi produces crisp, compliant ingredient lists with exceptional small-text legibility for FDA-required disclosures.

Dynamic Graphics Capability: Swap logos, brand colors, and product imagery automatically between clients. Different substrates and finishes per SKU without manual intervention.

Production Speed: Full variable data processing without per-label delays—maintain fulfillment velocity even with high customization.

Cost-Efficient Operation: Water-based pigment inks deliver lower cost-per-label than alternatives with a natural matte finish preferred by premium beauty brands.

Business Transformation Results

Before Digital Implementation:

Client onboarding required 3-4 weeks minimum: brand asset collection (1-2 days), label design (2-3 days), client approval cycles (3-5 days), printer submission (1 day), production waiting (10-14 days), plus receiving and warehousing (2-3 days).

Ongoing management meant warehousing label inventory for dozens of clients, tracking version control manually, managing expiration and obsolescence, and processing reorders on 2-3 week cycles.

Annual operational costs reached $110,000-$170,000: $50,000-$75,000 in setup fees, $25,000-$40,000 in obsolete inventory write-offs, $15,000-$25,000 in rush fees, plus $20,000-$30,000 in warehousing expenses.

After Digital Implementation:

Client onboarding compresses to 2-3 days: rapid asset collection, data template population in hours, same-day sample printing, and immediate production upon approval.

Inventory management becomes nearly zero—labels print on-demand as orders arrive. Version control lives digitally. Reorders fulfill same-day. Warehouse space requirements drop dramatically.

Annual costs fall to $15,000-$25,000: minimal operating expenses, zero setup fees, and virtually no obsolete inventory liability.

Net annual savings: $95,000-$145,000

Implementation Pathway

Phase 1: Template Development (Weeks 1-2)
Analyze existing label portfolio to identify common structures. Design 3-5 master template variations with built-in compliance frameworks.

Phase 2: Data Infrastructure (Weeks 3-4)
Create standardized client data collection forms and spreadsheet templates. Establish validation procedures ensuring regulatory compliance.

Phase 3: Equipment Integration (Weeks 5-6)
Install and configure variable data printing systems. Train operations staff and validate production quality with existing clients.

Phase 4: Pilot Migration (Weeks 7-8)
Transition 5-10 current clients to the new workflow. Run parallel operations, measure results, and gather client feedback.

Phase 5: Full Deployment (Weeks 9-12)
Migrate entire client base to digital printing. Optimize workflows, market enhanced capabilities, and document ROI achievements.

Conclusion

White-label beauty manufacturing represents a significant growth opportunity, but traditional label production creates operational friction that constrains success. Setup fees, volume minimums, and extended timelines force contract manufacturers into difficult compromises that limit client relationships.

Variable data digital printing with the ArrowJet Aqua 330R offers a superior alternative. By transforming label production from a rigid, SKU-by-SKU process into a flexible, data-driven system, contract manufacturers can serve more beauty brands with greater agility at reduced operational cost.

The transformation extends beyond efficiency metrics to genuine business advantage: faster client acquisition, minimal inventory burden, superior client satisfaction, and meaningful competitive differentiation. In private label cosmetics, operational speed and production flexibility aren’t operational luxuries—they’re the foundation of sustainable growth.

Ready to transform your contract manufacturing operation? Contact Arrow Systems for a free private label printing consultation.

title.rendered: The Minimum Order Problem: Why Small Brands Cannot Access Professional Sachet Packaging (And How Digital Changes Everything)

The Minimum Order Problem: Why Small Brands Cannot Access Professional Sachet Packaging (And How Digital Changes Everything)

You have a great product. Maybe it is a powdered greens supplement, a specialty tea blend, or a revolutionary electrolyte drink mix. You have got the formula perfected, the branding designed, and early customers who love it.

But then you hit the packaging wall.

Our minimum order is 50,000 units.

We need 100,000 sachets to justify the plate setup.

Short runs are not cost-effective with Rotogravure.

This is the minimum order problem, and it is killing small brands before they get started. But just like with custom tape, digital printing is rewriting the rules for sachet packaging.

The Economics of Traditional Sachet Printing

Why Rotogravure and Flexographic Require Massive MOQs

Traditional sachet printing methods were designed for massive CPG brands shipping millions of units. Here is why they cannot serve small brands:

Rotogravure Printing:

  • Cylinder engraving: ,000–15,000 per design

  • Setup time: 4–8 hours of press time

  • Minimum efficient run: 100,000+ sachets

  • Per-unit cost at small volumes: Prohibitively expensive

Flexographic Printing:

  • Plate costs: 00–2,000 per color

  • Setup waste: 1,000–5,000 sachets

  • Minimum order: 25,000–50,000 sachets

  • Color limitations: Additional costs for each color

The math is brutal: If you are a startup selling 500 units per month, a 50,000-unit minimum is an 8-year supply.

The Real Cost of High Minimums

Cash Flow Crisis

That 50,000-unit order? It might cost 5,000–25,000 upfront. For early-stage companies, that is:

  • Months of operating capital

  • Marketing budget that could acquire customers

  • Product development funds for line extensions

Inventory Risk

What if your design is not perfect?

  • Typo in the supplement facts

  • Regulatory compliance issue

  • Rebranding six months in

  • New competitor forces differentiation

With a 50,000-unit minimum, you are stuck with outdated inventory or eating the cost.

Storage Nightmares

50,000 sachets take up serious warehouse space:

  • Climate-controlled storage (humidity affects product quality)

  • Inventory management systems

  • Insurance and security

  • Potential for damage or expiration

Opportunity Cost

Capital tied up in sachet inventory cannot be used for:

  • Marketing and customer acquisition

  • Product development

  • Team expansion

  • Market expansion

The Digital Printing Revolution for Sachets

How Digital Changes the Economics

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite uses single-pass digital inkjet technology to print directly onto flexible sachet substrates. This eliminates the fixed costs that create minimum order requirements.

Explore More

Digital printing economics:

  • Setup costs: sh

  • Plate/cylinder costs: sh

  • Setup waste: Minimal (10–50 sachets)

  • Minimum order: 100 sachets (or even less)

The New Math

Order Size Traditional Rotogravure Digital (ArrowJet)
500 sachets -12 per unit (with setup) sh.50–1.00 per unit
5,000 sachets -4 per unit sh.30–0.60 per unit
25,000 sachets sh.80–1.50 per unit sh.20–0.40 per unit
100,000 sachets sh.30–0.60 per unit sh.15–0.30 per unit

Note: Pricing varies by specifications and substrate. Digital becomes cost-competitive at lower volumes.

Real-World Scenarios: Small Brands Winning with Digital

Scenario 1: The Supplement Startup

Profile: New collagen powder brand, launching with 3 flavors, expecting 200 orders/month

Traditional approach:

  • Order 50,000 sachets per flavor (150,000 total)

  • Cost: 5,000–75,000 upfront

  • Risk: If one flavor flops, stuck with useless inventory

Digital approach:

  • Order 1,000 sachets per flavor to start

  • Cost: ,500–3,000

  • Flexibility: Adjust flavor mix based on sales data

Result: Launched with 95% less capital, iterated based on customer feedback, doubled down on best-selling flavor.

Scenario 2: The Beverage Innovator

Profile: Electrolyte drink mix, direct-to-consumer model, testing 5 different formulations

Traditional approach:

  • Cannot afford 5 separate 50,000-unit orders

  • Forced to pick one winner without market testing

  • High risk if chosen formulation underperforms

Digital approach:

  • Print 500 sachets of each formulation

  • Send samples to 2,500 potential customers

  • Collect feedback and iterate

  • Scale the winning formula

Result: Data-driven product selection, 60% higher customer satisfaction vs. best guess approach.

Scenario 3: The Tea Blender

Profile: Artisan tea company, 12 seasonal blends, small batch ethos

Traditional approach:

  • Minimums make small-batch branding impossible

  • Forced into commodity packaging or massive inventory

  • Seasonal variations economically unviable

Digital approach:

  • Print 2,000 sachets per seasonal blend

  • 12 unique designs, no plate costs

  • Align packaging with harvest seasons

Result: Authentic small-batch positioning, 40% premium pricing vs. commodity tea, zero obsolete inventory.

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite for Sachet Production

Technical Capabilities

  • Print width: Up to 13 inches

  • Resolution: Up to 1600 × 1600 dpi

  • Inks: Aqueous pigment (food-safe options available)

  • Speed: Production rates suitable for commercial short runs

  • Substrate compatibility: PET/PE, foil laminates, paper-based materials, biodegradable films

Conclusion: Access Without Compromise

Small brands no longer need to choose between professional packaging and affordability, quality and flexibility, or short runs and good unit economics.

Digital printing with the ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite removes the barriers that kept small brands from accessing professional sachet packaging.

PackEast 2026 Wrap-Up: Key Highlights from Philadelphia's Premier Packaging Show

PackEast 2026 brought together the packaging industry’s brightest minds and most innovative technologies at the Pennsylvania Convention Center in Philadelphia, February 17–19. With approximately 7,000 attendees exploring solutions from over 400 exhibitors, this year’s show delivered on its promise as the East Coast’s premier packaging and processing trade show.

Arrow Systems, Inc. was proud to exhibit alongside our partners at the EZ Hi Tech booth, demonstrating our ArrowJet digital label printers to an enthusiastic crowd of packaging professionals, brand owners, and production managers.

What Was PackEast 2026?

PackEast is the region’s most comprehensive packaging and processing trade show for the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic markets. Held every two years, the event brings cutting-edge technology and solutions from top suppliers to CPG and life sciences companies across more than 40 vertical industries.

This year’s show introduced the new Containers & Materials Pavilion, reflecting the industry’s growing focus on sustainable packaging solutions and material innovations.

Show Overview: Stats and Highlights

  • Dates: February 17–19, 2026

  • Location: Pennsylvania Convention Center, Philadelphia, PA

  • Exhibitors: 400–500 companies

  • Expected Attendance: ~7,000 professionals

  • Industries Represented: 40+ vertical markets

  • New Feature: Containers & Materials Pavilion

The three-day event featured live technology demonstrations, educational sessions, and countless networking opportunities. Every hour spent on the show floor delivered insights into solutions for the industry’s biggest packaging and processing challenges.

Key Exhibitors and Their Innovations

Pineberry Manufacturing (Booth 1328)

Pineberry showcased an impressive lineup of automation solutions designed to streamline label production and packaging operations:

  • FlexJet Drop-on-Demand Print and Label System — combines printing and labeling in one efficient system

  • Dot Jet Printing Solutions — high-speed industrial printing with friction feeder integration

  • Friction Feeder Systems with Conveyors — automated feeding for consistent production flow

  • Erect and Flat Carton Serialization Systems — critical for pharmaceutical compliance and track-and-trace requirements

  • Pick & Place Tray Denesting System — automation for complex packaging configurations

  • Rotary Feeder Systems — versatile feeding solutions for various product types

  • Cobot MG400 System — collaborative robotics for safe, flexible automation

Afinia Label

Afinia made waves with the launch of their L701 Industrial Color Label Printer, featuring:

  • Five 150 mL ink cartridges for extended production runs

  • Full-color, photo-quality label printing

  • Direct printing to inkjet-printable die-cut labels and tag stock

  • Thousands of material and label size combinations

Their focus on bringing label production in-house continues to resonate with businesses looking to reduce lead times and increase flexibility.

ATIP

ATIP demonstrated advanced printing solutions focused on substrate versatility:

  • Expanded substrate flexibility with solvent ink support for non-porous materials

  • High-resolution tall-format printing without labels or complex multi-head setups

  • Solutions that eliminate the need for traditional label applications

AstroNova QuickLabel (EZ Hi Tech Booth)

Alongside Arrow Systems, AstroNova showcased their QuickLabel digital label printers, demonstrating high-speed, full-color label production capabilities for businesses of all sizes.

Technologies That Stood Out

Digital Label Printing Innovations

PackEast 2026 proved that digital label printing has moved firmly into the mainstream. Key innovations included:

  • Drop-on-demand printing systems offering variable data and short-run capabilities

  • Industrial-grade color label printers with expanded ink capacity for longer runs

  • Direct-to-substrate printing that bypasses traditional label materials

  • High-resolution printing delivering photo-quality results on demand

Packaging Automation Solutions

Automation was everywhere at PackEast, with exhibitors demonstrating:

  • Collaborative robots (cobots) working safely alongside human operators

  • Friction feeder systems handling products of all shapes and sizes

  • Pick-and-place systems for complex packaging requirements

  • Automated serialization systems meeting pharmaceutical and food safety standards

Product Identification and Serialization

Track-and-trace capabilities continue to be a major focus, with systems designed for:

  • Pharmaceutical compliance requirements

  • Food safety and recall preparedness

  • Anti-counterfeiting measures

  • Supply chain visibility

Industry Trends from the Show Floor

1) In-House Production Is the New Normal

Multiple vendors emphasized solutions for bringing label production in-house. Companies are tired of long lead times and minimum order quantities from traditional label suppliers. Digital printing technology now makes short runs economically viable.

2) Automation Integration Is Accelerating

Cobot systems and automated feeding solutions were prominent across the show floor. The message was clear: automation isn’t just for high-volume operations anymore. Mid-sized companies are finding ways to integrate robotics and automation into their workflows.

3) Pharmaceutical Compliance Drives Innovation

Serialization systems for pharmaceutical applications were a major focus, reflecting the industry’s need for robust track-and-trace capabilities. These systems are increasingly being adopted by food and beverage companies as well.

4) Sustainability Takes Center Stage

The introduction of the Containers & Materials Pavilion signals the industry’s commitment to sustainable packaging solutions. Expect continued innovation in recyclable materials, reduced packaging, and environmentally friendly printing processes.

5) Versatility Is King

Exhibitors emphasized multi-material printing and substrate flexibility. In today’s fast-moving market, production equipment needs to handle a wide variety of jobs without lengthy changeovers.

Arrow Systems at PackEast 2026

Arrow Systems, Inc. was proud to join our partners at the EZ Hi Tech booth for PackEast 2026. We demonstrated our ArrowJet digital label printers to hundreds of attendees interested in bringing professional label production in-house.

What We Showcased

Our ArrowJet digital label printers demonstrated:

  • High-quality color printing for product labels, packaging, and branding materials

  • Variable data capabilities for personalized and serialized labels

  • Short-run efficiency — print exactly what you need, when you need it

  • Cost-effective production — no plates, no minimums, no waste

  • User-friendly operation — easy setup and intuitive controls

Conversations on the Show Floor

The response to our demonstrations was overwhelmingly positive. Attendees were particularly interested in:

  • Reducing reliance on external label suppliers

  • Printing prototypes and samples in-house

  • Managing seasonal packaging changes efficiently

  • Complying with evolving labeling regulations

  • Controlling costs on small-batch production runs

Partnership with EZ Hi Tech

Our presence alongside EZ Hi Tech strengthened our commitment to providing comprehensive labeling solutions. The partnership allows us to offer customers not just printers, but complete labeling ecosystems including media, software, and technical support.

Looking Ahead: What’s Next for Label Printing

PackEast 2026 made one thing clear: digital label printing and packaging automation are no longer emerging trends—they’re the new standard.

As we look ahead to the rest of 2026 and beyond, we expect to see:

  • Continued advancement in digital printing speeds and quality

  • More affordable automation solutions for small and medium businesses

  • Greater emphasis on sustainable materials and processes

  • Integration of AI and machine learning into production workflows

  • Enhanced connectivity and Industry 4.0 capabilities

Final Thoughts

PackEast 2026 delivered on its promise as the East Coast’s premier packaging event. The combination of innovative exhibitors, engaged attendees, and forward-looking educational content made it an invaluable experience for anyone involved in packaging and label production.

For Arrow Systems, the show reinforced what we’ve been hearing from customers: there’s tremendous demand for flexible, affordable, high-quality label production solutions. Our ArrowJet printers are designed to meet that demand, and we’re excited to help more businesses take control of their labeling operations.

Didn’t make it to PackEast 2026? Contact Arrow Systems today to schedule a demonstration of our ArrowJet digital label printers. See firsthand how in-house label production can transform your packaging workflow.

Eliminating Wasted Inventory: The Ultimate Guide to On-Demand Box Printing (2026)

What Is On-Demand Box Printing?

On-demand case printing (also called direct-to-package printing) is the proven process of applying graphics, text, and branding directly onto corrugated cases using digital inkjet technology—without plates, without setup time, and without minimum order quantities. This revolutionary approach helps businesses eliminate box inventory completely.

Unlike pre-printed boxes ordered in bulk from converters, on-demand corrugated printing happens at the point of packaging or fulfillment. You maintain a stock of unprinted, generic boxes and transform them into branded, SKU-specific packaging moments before they’re needed.

Key technologies that enable you to reduce packaging SKU count:

  • UV-based inkjet systems offer instant curing, outdoor durability, and superior adhesion to challenging substrates
  • Water-based inkjet systems provide food-safe, low-odor decoration with excellent sustainability credentials

Both approaches eliminate box inventory and remove the traditional printing bottleneck that forces companies to over-order and over-store.

The Hidden Cost of Box Inventory

Walk into any warehouse storing corrugated packaging, and you’ll find a problem most operations have accepted as inevitable: walls of boxes. Skids upon skids of pre-printed cases, each representing frozen capital, occupied square footage, and continuous operational headaches.

The traditional packaging workflow demands forecasting. You estimate Q3 sales, order 10,000 printed boxes for a reasonable per-unit cost, and hope your predictions hold. They rarely do. Product launches flop. Seasonal demand shifts. Packaging designs become outdated. Suddenly, that $0.42 per box negotiated rate becomes much higher when you’re writing off 3,000 obsolete units.

The best solution? Just-in-time packaging printing lets you print exactly what you need, exactly when you need it. On-demand case printing isn’t science fiction—it’s the new standard for operations that refuse to let packaging dictate their inventory strategy.

Benefits of Just-in-Time Box Printing

Eliminate Obsolescence Risk

Traditional pre-printed packaging carries a 15-20% annual write-off rate. When you eliminate box inventory through on-demand printing, you reduce this waste to 0%. This proven approach saves mid-sized operations $10,000-$15,000 annually. No more MOQs and wasted space storing pre-printed boxes!

Free Up Warehouse Space

Pre-printed box inventory consumes valuable warehouse real estate. By switching to on-demand box printing, you reclaim square footage for revenue-generating activities rather than storage. No more storage shelves packed with unused boxes to be thrown out after 2 years!

Respond to Market Changes Instantly

Product designs change. Regulations update. Seasonal promotions launch. With just-in-time packaging printing, you implement changes same-day instead of waiting 2-4 weeks for new print runs. This allows for seasonal packaging and special offers to be easily offered to customers!

Reduce Total Cost of Ownership

While per-unit costs may appear higher for small runs, the total cost of on-demand case printing is lower when you factor in:

  • Zero setup fees ($800-$2,500 saved per run)
  • No obsolescence write-offs
  • Eliminated storage costs ($0.08-0.15/unit/year)
  • Reduced rush order premiums

UV vs. Water-Based Technology Comparison

Limitronic V7 (UV-Based)

The Limitronic V7 uses UV-curable inks that cure instantly under LED lamps. This creates a hardened, durable print surface that’s resistant to scratching, water, and UV exposure. Limitronic technology can be used both offline and inline on packaging lines.

Best for:

  • Outdoor or extended storage applications
  • High-risk handling environments (agriculture, industrial)
  • Quick turnaround without drying time
  • Bold graphics requiring high opacity white ink

Sustainability note: Modern UV inks have significantly lower VOCs than traditional solvent-based alternatives, though water-based systems retain the environmental edge for food-contact applications.

Explore More

Arrow OverJet Pro (Water-Based)

The Arrow OverJet Pro uses water-based pigment inks specially formulated for corrugated adhesion. These inks penetrate the board slightly, creating excellent durability while maintaining a smaller environmental footprint.

Best for:

  • Food and beverage packaging (FDA-compliant formulations available)
  • Premium consumer goods where “green” messaging matters
  • Operations prioritizing VOC reduction
  • Direct food-contact secondary packaging

The choice between UV and water-based often comes down to end-use requirements rather than print quality—both systems deliver photorealistic, full-color graphics.

Explore More

ROI Analysis: Traditional vs. On-Demand

Let’s talk numbers. A mid-sized operation running 50 SKUs might maintain $40,000-$80,000 in pre-printed packaging inventory at any given time. That’s capital that could fund equipment, marketing, or growth initiatives.

Cost Comparison Table

Cost FactorPre-Printed BulkOn-Demand Digital
Per-unit cost (100 units)$2.80 (rush)$0.85
Per-unit cost (10,000 units)$0.42$0.85
Setup cost$800-$2,500$0
Obsolescence risk15-20% annual write-off0%
Storage cost$0.08-0.15/unit/year$0
Lead time2-4 weeksSame day

The math shifts dramatically when you factor in obsolescence. A company writing off 18% of their $60,000 annual packaging spend loses $10,800 yearly to outdated inventory. On-demand case printing eliminates that waste entirely.

5 Steps to Eliminate Box Inventory

Step 1: Audit Your Current Inventory

Calculate your total packaging inventory value, square footage usage, and write-off rates. Identify which SKUs have the highest obsolescence risk (seasonal, promotional, experimental products).

Step 2: Identify Quick Wins

Start with SKUs that:

  • Have frequent design changes
  • Represent <500 units per run
  • Are seasonal or promotional
  • Have versioning requirements (regional, language, etc.)

Step 3: Select Your Technology Path

Choose UV if you need outdoor durability and immediate handling. Choose water-based if you need food contact compliance and sustainability positioning.

Step 4: Design for Digital

Update your design files for on-demand corrugated printing:

  • Verify color profiles (RGB to CMYK conversion)
  • Test barcode scannability at target resolution
  • Design for variable data if versioning is needed

Step 5: Phase Your Rollout

Start with 10-20% of your SKUs to validate workflows, train operators, and refine processes. Expand as confidence and efficiency improve.

Real-World Applications

Seasonal Packaging Without the Risk

A craft beverage company normally orders 15,000 holiday-themed boxes in October. Last year, demand exceeded projections and they sold out by December 10th—turning away sales. This year, they’re using just-in-time packaging printing: 200 boxes today, 300 tomorrow, adjusting to actual demand. No surplus. No shortage. No risk.

Regional Variants from Generic Stock

A national electronics retailer maintains one generic box SKU, printing region-specific messaging and compliance labeling at 12 distribution centers. They reduced packaging SKU count by 47 separate box SKUs and eliminated the inventory headaches that came with them.

Promotional Testing at Scale

A CPG brand wanted to test three different package designs for a new product launch. Instead of committing $15,000 to 5,000 boxes of each variant (with two-thirds destined for the dumpster), they used on-demand case printing for 200 of each, ran them to market, and let data drive the final design decision.

Sustainability Advantages

Beyond inventory efficiency, on-demand corrugated printing carries significant sustainability benefits:

  • Reduced waste: Print what you need, eliminate box inventory obsolescence
  • Lower transportation: Print at point of use, not at a converter’s facility
  • Right-sized packaging: Freedom to optimize box sizes without minimum order constraints
  • Water-based options: Arrow OverJet Pro formulations contribute to reduced VOC emissions

For companies with ESG commitments or sustainability-focused customers, just-in-time packaging printing is a tangible operational improvement that supports broader environmental goals.

Implementation Guide

Throughput Requirements: Digital throughput (50-200 feet/minute depending on resolution) suits most fulfillment operations but requires evaluation against peak demand periods.

Operator Training: Modern systems are designed for operator-friendly workflows, but expect a 2-4 week learning curve for file preparation, color management, and maintenance procedures.

Integration: Most on-demand case printing systems integrate with existing conveyor lines, WMS systems, and ERP platforms. Evaluate your current infrastructure for compatibility.

Key Takeaways

  • Eliminate box inventory to free up $40,000-$80,000 in frozen capital
  • Just-in-time packaging printing reduces obsolescence waste from 15-20% to 0%
  • On-demand corrugated printing enables same-day turnaround vs. 2-4 week lead times
  • Choose UV systems for durability, water-based for sustainability
  • Start with quick-win SKUs: seasonal, promotional, or low-volume products
  • Reduce packaging SKU count by using generic stock with variable printing
  • Calculate total cost of ownership—not just per-unit price
  • Plan for 2-4 week operator training during implementation

FAQs

What is on-demand case printing?

On-demand case printing is the process of printing graphics and branding directly onto corrugated boxes using digital inkjet technology. Unlike traditional printing that requires plates and setup, on-demand systems print instantly from digital files, allowing you to eliminate box inventory and print exactly what you need, when you need it.

How much can I save by eliminating box inventory?

Most mid-sized operations save $10,000-$15,000 annually by switching to just-in-time packaging printing. Savings come from eliminated obsolescence (15-20% of inventory value), reduced storage costs ($0.08-0.15/unit/year), and zero setup fees ($800-$2,500 per traditional run).

What is the difference between UV and water-based on-demand printing?

UV-based printing (like the Limitronic V7) uses inks that cure instantly under LED lamps. It’s best for outdoor durability and immediate handling. Water-based printing (like the Arrow OverJet Pro) uses FDA-compliant pigment inks ideal for food packaging and sustainability-focused operations.

Can on-demand printing handle high volumes?

Yes. Modern on-demand corrugated printing systems handle 50-200 feet per minute, depending on resolution. This throughput suits most fulfillment operations. For extremely high volumes, a hybrid approach using on-demand for variable/short-run SKUs and traditional for stable high-volume SKUs often works best.

How do I transition from traditional to on-demand printing?

Follow the 5-step process: (1) Audit current inventory and write-offs, (2) Identify quick-win SKUs, (3) Select UV or water-based technology, (4) Design files for digital output, (5) Phase rollout starting with 10-20% of SKUs. Most operations complete full transition within 3-6 months.

Is on-demand printing more expensive per box?

Per-unit costs for on-demand case printing are higher for large runs ($0.85 vs. $0.42 for 10,000 units) but total cost of ownership is lower. When you eliminate setup fees, obsolescence, and storage costs, on-demand typically saves 20-40% annually for operations with diverse SKU mixes.

Learn more about just-in-time packaging printing and on-demand corrugated printing:

  • corrugated packaging industry trends – Latest developments in packaging automation
  • Digital printing technology standards – Technical specifications for on-demand printing
  • Sustainable packaging initiatives – Federal sustainability guidelines for packaging operations

Conclusion

The days of warehouses full of pre-printed boxes are ending. On-demand case printing—whether via UV systems like the Limitronic V7 or water-based solutions like the Arrow OverJet Pro—gives operations the flexibility they’ve always needed and the inventory efficiency they’ve always wanted.

When you eliminate box inventory, you free up capital, reclaim warehouse space, reduce waste, and gain the agility to respond to market changes instantly. The question isn’t whether on-demand corrugated printing makes sense for your operation. It’s how quickly you can capture the competitive advantages currently locked in box inventory.

Table of Contents

Screen Printing vs Digital Inkjet on Corrugated: Which Method Wins in 2025?

The Traditional Choice: Screen Printing

Screen printing has been the workhorse of corrugated decoration for decades. The process is straightforward: create a stencil (screen) for each color, push ink through the mesh onto the board, cure, and repeat. For high-volume, single-design production runs, it’s been the default choice—and for good reason.

When you’re printing 50,000 identical boxes, screen printing delivers consistent color and low per-unit costs. The screens are durable, the ink is thick and vibrant, and the economics are well-established. Converter facilities have built entire businesses around high-volume screen printing, and the supply chain is mature.

But the world has changed. Today’s packaging landscape demands shorter runs, faster turnaround, and constant versioning. The economics that made screen printing attractive are increasingly overshadowed by its limitations.

Screen Printing’s Hidden Costs

Setup Time and Labor

Every screen print job requires screen preparation, registration, and setup. For a four-color print, you’re looking at 2-4 hours of preparation before the first acceptable box comes off the line. That time is pure overhead—unbillable, unrecoverable, and repeated for every design change.

Plate/Screen Costs

Each color requires its own screen. At $200-$500 per screen (depending on size and complexity), a four-color job incurs $800-$2,000 in setup costs before a single box is printed. Spread across 50,000 units, that’s manageable. Across 500 units, it’s prohibitive.

Minimum Order Quantities

Screen printing economics demand volume. Most converters won’t touch runs under 1,000-2,500 units. This forces brands to over-order, commit to forecasts, and absorb the costs of obsolete inventory.

Design Inflexibility

Once screens are made, changes are costly. A last-minute logo update, regulatory change, or promotional messaging shift requires new screens and new setup time. This inflexibility is increasingly out of step with fast-moving markets.

Color Limitations

Screen printing uses spot colors—pre-mixed inks applied one at a time. Achieving full-color photography or complex gradients requires process color simulation (expensive) or simply isn’t possible. Brands looking for photorealistic graphics hit a hard technical ceiling.

The Modern Alternative: Digital Inkjet on Corrugated

Digital inkjet printing applies ink directly to corrugated board using precision printheads, much like a high-speed, high-resolution office printer adapted for industrial packaging. There’s no screen creation, no setup time between jobs, and no minimum order quantity.

Two technology platforms currently lead the market:

UV-Based Digital Inkjet (Limitronic V7)

Explore more

UV systems use inks that cure instantly under LED lamps. The result is a hardened, durable print surface ready for immediate handling, stacking, and shipping.

Key characteristics:

  • Instant cure (no drying time)
  • Exceptional durability (scratch, water, UV resistant)
  • High opacity white ink capability
  • Adhesion to challenging substrates (coated boards, low-grade corrugate)
  • Smaller physical footprint (no drying tunnels)

Water-Based Digital Inkjet (Arrow OverJet Pro)

Explore more

Water-based systems use pigment inks that penetrate the board surface slightly, creating durable prints with reduced environmental impact.

Key characteristics:

  • Food-safe formulations available (FDA-compliant for direct/indirect food contact)
  • Lower VOC emissions
  • Excellent for premium consumer goods and sustainability messaging
  • Natural matte finish popular for high-end brands
  • Competitive durability for most applications

Head-to-Head Comparison

Factor Screen Printing Digital Inkjet
Setup Time 2-4 hours <15 minutes
Setup Cost $800-$2,500 $0
Minimum Order 1,000-2,500 units 1 unit
Per-Unit Cost (500 units) $3.50-$6.00 $0.85-$1.20
Per-Unit Cost (50,000 units) $0.35-$0.55 $0.65-$0.90
Color Capability Spot colors (limited) Full CMYK + white
Photographic Quality Not possible Standard
Variable Data Not possible Native capability
Design Changes New screens required File update only
Versioning Prohibitively expensive No additional cost
Lead Time 2-4 weeks Same day
Sustainability Higher waste, VOCs Options for water-based, lower waste

When Screen Printing Still Makes Sense

Digital inkjet has transformed the packaging landscape, but screen printing retains advantages in specific scenarios:

Very High Volume, Single Design
When you’re running 100,000+ identical boxes monthly with no design changes, screen printing’s lower per-unit cost eventually overcomes its setup overhead. The break-even point varies but typically falls in the 25,000-50,000 unit range for simple two-color jobs.

Specialty Inks
Metallics, fluorescents, and specialty textures are still screen printing domains. While digital is rapidly advancing, some effects remain screen-exclusive.

Extreme Thickness Requirements
For applications requiring the heaviest ink deposit (some outdoor applications, extreme durability), screen printing applies more ink per pass than digital alternatives.

When Digital Dominates

Short Runs

The economics are clear: digital wins at any volume under roughly 5,000 units for full-color jobs. Below 1,000 units, there’s no contest.

Versioning and Personalization

Digital’s native variable data capability enables:

  • Regional messaging
  • Seasonal variants
  • Promotional personalization
  • A/B testing
  • Language localization
  • SKU-specific graphics

Each of these is either impossible or cost-prohibitive with screen printing.

Fast Turnaround

When your customer demands boxes tomorrow, digital answers. Screen printing’s 2-4 week lead times through converter networks can’t compete with same-day digital production.

Full-Color Graphics

Photorealistic images, complex gradients, and brand-accurate color reproduction are digital’s home turf. Screen printing’s spot-color limitation is increasingly a deal-breaker for brands expecting retail-ready shelf appeal.

Prototyping and Testing

Before committing to 10,000 boxes, print 50. Test the market. Validate the design. Digital makes iterative development economically viable.

Real-World Decision Framework

Choose Screen Printing When:

  • Volume exceeds 25,000-50,000 units
  • Design is permanent (no changes for 12+ months)
  • Lead time of 2-4 weeks is acceptable
  • Budget prioritizes absolute lowest per-unit cost over flexibility

Choose Digital Inkjet When:

  • Volume is under 5,000 units
  • Frequent design changes are expected
  • Versioning or personalization is desired
  • Lead time pressure exists
  • Full-color graphics are required
  • Food contact compliance is needed (water-based systems)
  • Sustainability messaging matters (water-based options)

Technology Selection: UV vs. Water-Based Digital

Once you’ve decided on digital, the next decision is UV (Limitronic V7) or water-based (Arrow OverJet Pro).

Choose UV When:

  • Immediate handling is required (no dry time)
  • Durability in harsh environments matters (agriculture, industrial)
  • Outdoor exposure is likely
  • Substrates are challenging (coated boards, non-porous)
  • Maximum production speed is priority

Choose Water-Based When:

  • Food contact compliance is required
  • Sustainability is a brand or regulatory priority
  • VOC reduction matters for facility or environmental reasons
  • Premium consumer goods positioning
  • Lower total cost of ownership is preferred

Both technologies deliver excellent print quality. The choice typically comes down to end-use requirements rather than output quality.

The Hybrid Approach

Smart operations don’t have to choose exclusively. Many facilities run both methods:

  • Screen printing for the 20% of SKUs representing 80% of volume (consistent, high-volume lines)
  • Digital inkjet for the 80% of SKUs representing 20% of volume (short runs, versioning, new products)

This hybrid model captures the best of both worlds: cost efficiency at scale plus flexibility for everything else.

The 2025 Verdict

Screen printing isn’t dead—it still serves high-volume, single-design applications where flexibility isn’t required. But for an increasing share of the market, digital inkjet has become the default choice.

The combination of no setup costs, instant turnaround, full-color capability, and versioning freedom makes digital the dominant choice for:

  • Short runs
  • Fast-turn environments
  • Versioning requirements
  • Photorealistic graphics
  • Food and beverage applications

UV systems (like the Limitronic V7) address durability and speed requirements. Water-based systems (like the Arrow OverJet Pro) address sustainability and food safety needs. Between them, they cover the vast majority of modern corrugated printing applications.

The question in 2025 isn’t whether digital can replace screen printing. It’s whether your operation can afford to stay locked into the constraints of an analog process in a digital market.

Ready to evaluate digital inkjet for your operation? Arrow Systems provides sample printing, ROI analysis, and implementation guidance for both UV and water-based systems.

Memjet Technology: The Complete Guide to Digital Label Printing Innovation

Discover how Memjet’s revolutionary inkjet technology is transforming on-demand label printing and why Arrow Systems leads the industry in Duraflex, DuraCore, and VersaPass support.

Memjet technology revolutionizes digital label printing by combining the speed of flexographic presses with the flexibility of digital. Using a single-pass printhead array and water-based pigment inks, Memjet-powered printers like the ArrowJet Aqua 330R produce photo-quality color labels at up to 150 fpm — without plates, setup waste, or long lead times. This guide explains how Memjet works, why it’s ideal for short-to-medium runs, and how to choose the right Memjet printer for your business.

What is Memjet Technology?

Memjet technology is a high-speed, water-based inkjet printing technology that uses a stationary printhead spanning the full width of the media to print at production speeds up to 150 feet per minute. Unlike traditional scanning printheads, Memjet’s single-pass architecture delivers vibrant color labels in a single pass — combining production-grade speed with on-demand digital flexibility. It uses water-based pigment inks (no VOCs, no ventilation required) and achieves 1600 x 1600 dpi resolution for photo-quality output on paper, polypropylene, PET, and synthetic label stocks.

Memjet technology represents a breakthrough in high-speed, high-quality Inkjet printing. Unlike traditional thermal transfer or laser printing, Memjet uses a unique stationary printhead array that spans the entire width of the page, enabling incredibly fast print speeds without sacrificing quality.

How Memjet Works?

1. Page-Wide Printhead Array
Unlike conventional inkjet printers that move a printhead back and forth, Memjet’s stationary array covers the full media width. This design eliminates mechanical delays and enables continuous high-speed printing.

2. High-Density Nozzle Configuration
Memjet printheads contain thousands of microscopic nozzles that deliver precise ink droplets at high frequencies. This density enables photo-quality printing at production speeds.

3. Advanced Ink Chemistry
Memjet’s aqueous pigment inks provide vibrant colors, water resistance, and durability suitable for industrial labeling applications.

Frequently Asked Questions About Memjet Technology

What makes Memjet different from other inkjet technologies?

Memjet uses a single-pass printhead that spans the entire media width, printing the full page in one pass. Traditional inkjets use a scanning head that moves back and forth, making them approximately 3–5x slower than Memjet at comparable quality.

Is Memjet water-based ink durable for product labels?

Yes. Memjet uses pigment-based water inks that offer excellent water resistance, UV stability, and scratch resistance — suitable for food, beverage, cosmetic, and industrial labels.

What is the maximum print width for Memjet printers?

Most Memjet label printers support media widths up to 12.75 inches (323 mm), accommodating a wide range of label and flexible packaging applications.

Can Memjet print on synthetic materials?

Yes. Memjet printers handle paper, polypropylene (BOPP), polyethylene, PET, and other synthetics with proper ink and media compatibility.

How fast is Memjet compared to toner-based label printers?

Memjet prints at 150 fpm (45 m/min) in full color — approximately 3–5x faster than typical toner-based digital label printers.

What industries benefit most from Memjet technology?

Food and beverage, cosmetics, nutraceuticals, cannabis, chemicals, and e-commerce businesses benefit most from Memjet’s fast turnaround and high-quality short runs.

Do Memjet printers require special ventilation?

No. Because Memjet uses water-based inks without VOCs or ozone, no special ventilation is required—unlike UV or solvent inkjet systems.

What is the typical cost per label with Memjet?

Cost per label varies by coverage, but Memjet typically ranges from $0.01–0.05 per label, competitive with flexo on runs of 500–10,000 labels.

Can Memjet print variable data and barcodes?

Absolutely. Memjet supports full variable data printing including sequential numbers, barcodes (UPC, QR, Code 128), and personalized text in a single pass.

How long do Memjet printheads last?

Memjet printheads are designed for longevity, typically lasting millions of linear feet with proper maintenance and cleaning protocols.

Key Takeaways

✓  Single-Pass Speed:  Memjet prints at 150 fpm using a full-width stationary printhead

✓  Water-Based Inks:  Eco-friendly pigment inks with no VOCs or ventilation requirements

✓  Ideal for Short Runs:  Perfect for 1–10,000 label jobs with zero setup waste

✓  Photo Quality:  1600 x 1600 dpi resolution rivals offset and flexographic quality

✓  ArrowJet Integration:  ArrowJet Aqua 330R combines Memjet speed with intuitive workflow software

Conclusion

Memjet technology continues to transform the digital label printing industry with high-speed, high-quality color output. Arrow Systems stands as a leading expert across Duraflex, DuraCore, and VersaPass platforms.
