Table of Contents

Short Run vs Long Run Custom Tape: How Digital Printing Changes the Game for Small Businesses

Introduction

Custom printed water-activated tape has traditionally been a high-volume game. For years, small businesses and startups were forced to choose between ordering thousands of feet of tape they did not need or skipping branded packaging entirely. That changed with digital printing technology.

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite has revolutionized the custom tape market by making short runs economically viable. No more plate costs. No more massive minimum orders. Just professional-grade custom tape, printed on demand.

What Are Short Run and Long Run Orders?

Short Run Orders (Under 10,000 feet)

  • Typical quantities: 100 to 5,000 feet
  • Best for: Startups, seasonal promotions, testing new designs, small e-commerce businesses
  • Traditional challenge: High per-foot costs and setup fees made small orders prohibitively expensive

Long Run Orders (Over 10,000 feet)

  • Typical quantities: 10,000 to 100,000+ feet
  • Best for: Established businesses with consistent shipping volumes, wholesale operations
  • Traditional advantage: Lower per-foot cost through economies of scale

The Old Way: Why Short Runs Used to Be Impossible

Traditional flexographic printing requires physical printing plates for each color. These plates cost hundreds of dollars to produce and require significant setup time. For a short run, these fixed costs get distributed across fewer feet of tape, driving the per-foot price through the roof.

Example of traditional costs:

  1. Plate setup: $300–$500 per color
  2. Minimum order: Often 10,000+ feet
  3. Short run result: $0.50–$1.00+ per foot

This is why StickerMule and others could offer $9 for 100 feet — they were losing money on small orders to acquire customers, hoping you would reorder at volume.

The New Way: Digital Printing with ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite

Digital printing eliminates plates entirely. The ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite uses aqueous pigment inks to print directly onto water-activated gum tape in full color, with no setup costs and no minimum order requirements.

How digital printing changes the math:

– Plate setup: $0

– Minimum order: 1 roll

– Short run result: Economically viable at any quantity

Benefits of Digital Printing for Short Runs:

  1. No Plate Costs — Design changes do not cost extra. Want to test three different designs? Print 100 feet of each without paying for three sets of plates.

  2. Variable Data Printing — Print different designs on the same roll. Perfect for personalization, seasonal campaigns, or A/B testing brand messaging.

  3. Fast Turnaround — No plate production means no lead time. Print today, ship tomorrow.

  4. True On-Demand Production — Only print what you need, when you need it. No more storing rolls of outdated tape.

When to Choose Short Run vs Long Run

Choose Short Run When:

– You are a startup or small business shipping fewer than 100 packages per month

– You are testing new branding and are not ready to commit to a single design

– You have seasonal campaigns that change throughout the year

– You need samples for sales presentations or trade shows

– You want personalization (different designs for different customers or products)

– Your volume is unpredictable and you cannot forecast tape needs

Choose Long Run When:

– You ship consistently high volumes (500+ packages monthly)

– Your branding is stable and unlikely to change for 12+ months

– You have storage space and cash flow to support inventory

– You are certain of your design and do not need flexibility

– You want the absolute lowest per-foot cost (at the expense of flexibility)

Cost Comparison: Digital vs Traditional for Short Runs

Order SizeTraditional FlexoArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite Digital
100 feet$50–$400 (with plate costs)$5–$50
500 feet$200–$500$25–$100
1,000 feet$300–$600$20–$150
5,000 feet$500–$900$100–$500

Note: Prices are estimates for comparison purposes. Actual pricing varies by supplier and specifications.

The Hidden Costs of Long Runs

Many businesses focus only on per-foot cost and overlook the hidden expenses of large orders:

Storage Costs: Warehouse space for tape inventory, climate control (humidity affects gum tape quality), inventory management labor

Obsolescence Risk: Rebranding makes old tape worthless, expired adhesive reduces tape performance, design fatigue when customers see the same tape for years

Cash Flow Impact: Capital tied up in inventory, opportunity cost of that capital

Waste: Damage during storage, overordering leads to discarded tape

Real-World Scenarios

Scenario 1: The Growing E-Commerce Brand

Profile: 50 orders per month, growing 20% monthly

Old approach: Order 10,000 feet to get reasonable pricing, store for months, risk design changes

Digital approach: Order 500 feet monthly, adjust design as brand evolves, pay as you grow

Nutraceutical Label Printing: The Ultimate 2026 Guide to FDA Dietary Supplement Labeling Compliance

Table of Contents

  1. What Is Nutraceutical Label Printing and Why Compliance Matters
  2. DSHEA Compliance: The Foundation of Dietary Supplement Labeling
  3. FDA Dietary Supplement Labeling Requirements
  4. Supplement Facts Panel Requirements
  5. Common Nutraceutical Label Compliance Mistakes
  6. Nutraceutical Label Printing Solutions: The ArrowJet Aqua 330R
  7. Variable Data for Nutraceutical Labels
  8. Implementation Roadmap for FDA-Compliant Labels

  10. Key Takeaways
  11. Conclusion

What Is Nutraceutical Label Printing and Why Compliance Matters

Nutraceutical label printing is the specialized process of creating FDA-compliant labels for dietary supplements, vitamins, and nutritional products. Understanding nutraceutical label printing requirements and FDA dietary supplement labeling regulations isn’t just about avoiding regulatory issues—it’s about building consumer trust, protecting your brand, and ensuring your products can be sold nationwide.

The dietary supplement industry operates at the intersection of food and pharmaceuticals. Regulated as food under the Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act of 1994 (DSHEA), supplements have nutraceutical label printing requirements that share similarities with drug standards. This unique positioning creates a complex compliance environment where manufacturers must navigate FDA regulations, FTC advertising guidelines, and state-level requirements simultaneously.

Unlike conventional food products, dietary supplements face heightened scrutiny because consumers use them for health benefits. The FDA requires specific disclosure formats, prohibits certain claims, and mandates precise ingredient nomenclature in nutraceutical label printing. Non-compliance isn’t just a regulatory risk—it can result in product seizures, warning letters, and significant brand damage.

This comprehensive guide breaks down the essential FDA dietary supplement labeling requirements, provides actionable compliance checklists for nutraceutical label printing, and explains how digital nutraceutical label printing solutions like the ArrowJet Aqua 330R enable supplement brands to maintain compliance while responding quickly to regulatory changes.

DSHEA Compliance: The Foundation of Dietary Supplement Labeling

What Is DSHEA?

The Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act of 1994 provides the regulatory framework for dietary supplements in the United States. Under DSHEA compliance requirements:

  • Supplements are regulated as food, not drugs
  • Manufacturers are responsible for ensuring safety before marketing
  • FDA oversees dietary supplement label regulations and post-market surveillance
  • Structure/function claims are permitted with disclosures
  • Disease claims require drug approval (and are prohibited for supplements)

FDA’s Role in Supplement Labeling

The FDA doesn’t approve supplement labels before products hit the market. Instead, they conduct post-market surveillance, inspect facilities, and review labels during routine inspections. This means nutraceutical label compliance is the manufacturer’s responsibility—and mistakes can be costly.

Key FDA Oversight Areas:

  • Label accuracy and completeness
  • Prohibited disease claims
  • Adverse event reporting
  • Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) compliance
  • Ingredient safety substantiation

FDA Dietary Supplement Labeling Requirements

Required Label Elements for Dietary Supplements

Every FDA-compliant dietary supplement label must include these five essential elements:

ElementRequirementCommon Mistakes
Statement of IdentityProduct name + “Dietary Supplement”Forgetting the supplement declaration
Net QuantityWeight, volume, or unit countWrong measurement format
Supplement Facts PanelDetailed nutrient breakdownImproper formatting, missing nutrients
Ingredient ListAll ingredients in descending orderBotanical name omissions
Manufacturer InfoName, address, contactMissing required contact details

Structure/Function Claims vs. Disease Claims

Understanding the difference is critical for dietary supplement label regulations:

✅ Permitted Structure/Function Claims:

  • “Supports immune health”
  • “Promotes cardiovascular function”
  • “Helps maintain healthy joints”

❌ Prohibited Disease Claims (Require Drug Approval):

  • “Prevents cancer”
  • “Treats diabetes”
  • “Cures arthritis”

Required Disclaimer: “These statements have not been evaluated by the FDA. This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.”

Supplement Facts Panel Requirements

The 7 Essential Components

The supplement facts panel requirements are specific and non-negotiable:

  1. Serving Size – Must be realistic and customary
  2. Servings Per Container – Accurate count
  3. Calories – If present (usually 0 for supplements)
  4. Macronutrients – Total fat, carbs, protein if significant amounts
  5. Dietary Ingredients – Listed with amount and %DV when established
  6. Other Ingredients – Binders, fillers, excipients
  7. Daily Value Footnote – Reference to 2,000 calorie diet when needed

Formatting Rules for Supplement Facts Panels

Font Requirements:

  • All text must be legible (minimum 6pt)
  • “Supplement Facts” must be the largest text in the panel
  • Amounts and %DV must be clearly aligned
  • Hairlines can separate sections but aren’t required

Layout Standards:

  • Calories must appear first (if present)
  • Dietary ingredients in descending order by weight
  • Botanicals listed by common and Latin names
  • %DV mandatory when RDIs are established

Common Nutraceutical Label Compliance Mistakes

Mistake #1: Improper Supplement Facts Formatting

Many nutraceutical label printing projects fail because the supplement facts panel doesn’t meet FDA layout requirements. Common errors include:

  • Wrong font sizes
  • Improper indentation
  • Missing daily values
  • Incorrect nutrient ordering

Mistake #2: Unapproved Health Claims

Making disease claims or exaggerating structure/function benefits can trigger FDA warning letters. The best FDA dietary supplement labeling practice is conservative claims backed by substantiation.

Mistake #3: Missing Botanical Nomenclature

FDA requires both common names and Latin binomials for botanical ingredients. Listing only “green tea extract” without Camellia sinensis is a compliance violation.

Mistake #4: Incomplete Manufacturer Information

Labels must include:

  • Manufacturer or distributor name
  • Complete street address (or city/state/zip if listed in phone directory)
  • Working contact information

Mistake #5: Wrong Label Material for Product Type

Supplements have specific nutraceutical label printing durability requirements:

  • Moisture resistance for refrigerated products
  • Oil resistance for softgels
  • UV stability for products in clear containers

Nutraceutical Label Printing Solutions: The ArrowJet Aqua 330R

Why Digital Label Printing for Supplements?

The best nutraceutical label printing approach combines regulatory compliance with operational flexibility. Digital printing offers:

  • Variable data capability – Batch codes, lot numbers, expiration dates
  • Short-run economics – No minimum orders, perfect for SKUs
  • Quick turnaround – Same-day production for urgent changes
  • Regulatory agility – Update labels immediately when FDA guidance changes

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R for Supplement Labels

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R is the ideal nutraceutical label printing solution because it offers:

  • Water-based pigment inks – FDA-compliant for indirect food contact
  • High resolution – Crisp text for small supplement facts panels
  • Durability – Resists moisture, oils, and handling
  • Variable data – Print unique codes on every label

Cost FactorOutsourcedIn-House with ArrowJet
Per-label cost$0.15-$0.45$0.03-$0.08

Setup fees$100-$300$0

Proven result: A supplement brand with 25 SKUs saves approximately $12,000 annually with in-house nutraceutical label printing.

Variable Data for Nutraceutical Labels

Critical Variable Data Elements

FDA dietary supplement labeling often requires dynamic information:

  • Lot numbers and batch codes
  • Manufacturing dates
  • Expiration or “best by” dates
  • Unique serial numbers (for traceability)
  • QR codes linking to COAs

Managing Multi-SKU Operations

Supplement brands often have dozens of SKUs with different formulations. Variable data printing enables:

  • One template, unlimited variations
  • Automated batch code insertion
  • Expiration date calculation
  • Real-time label updates

Implementation Roadmap for FDA-Compliant Labels

Phase 1: Regulatory Audit (Week 1)

  • Review all product formulations
  • Verify structure/function claim substantiation
  • Audit current labels for compliance gaps

Phase 2: Label Template Design (Week 2)

  • Create FDA-compliant supplement facts panels
  • Design master templates for each product line
  • Incorporate required disclosures and disclaimers

Phase 3: Production System Setup (Week 3)

  • Install nutraceutical label printing equipment
  • Configure variable data workflows
  • Validate print quality and durability

Phase 4: Compliance Verification (Week 4)

  • Legal/regulatory review of all label designs
  • Testing for moisture, oil, and handling resistance
  • Document compliance procedures

Phase 5: Production Launch (Week 5+)

  • Print initial inventory
  • Implement lot tracking systems
  • Train production staff on FDA requirements

Nutraceutical Labeling FAQ

What font size is required for supplement facts panels?

All text in the supplement facts panel must be at least 6 point font, with “Supplement Facts” being the largest text. Most brands use 8-10 point for readability.

Can I make health claims on my supplement labels?

You can make structure/function claims (e.g., “supports immune health”) with the required FDA disclaimer. Disease claims (e.g., “prevents colds”) are prohibited without drug approval.

What is the difference between a dietary supplement and a drug?

Dietary supplements are regulated as food under DSHEA and cannot claim to treat, cure, or prevent diseases. Drugs require FDA approval and can make disease claims.

How do I format the supplement facts panel correctly?

The supplement facts panel requirements include:

  • “Supplement Facts” as the largest text
  • Serving size and servings per container
  • Calories (if present)
  • Dietary ingredients with amounts and %DV
  • Other ingredients list
  • Daily value footnote when needed

Can I print supplement labels in-house?

Yes, with the right equipment. The ArrowJet Aqua 330R uses FDA-compliant water-based pigment inks and produces durable labels suitable for nutraceutical label printing.

What are the penalties for non-compliant supplement labels?

FDA enforcement can include warning letters, product seizures, facility inspections, fines, and mandatory recalls. Brand reputation damage is often the biggest cost.

Key Takeaways

  • Understand DSHEA – Supplements are regulated as food, not drugs
  • Follow FDA Formatting Rules – Supplement facts panels have strict requirements
  • Make Compliant Claims – Structure/function only, with required disclaimer
  • List Botanicals Properly – Include Latin binomials for all plant ingredients
  • Invest in Quality Equipment – The best nutraceutical label printers offer flexibility and compliance
  • Plan for Variable Data – Batch codes, expiration dates, and lot numbers are essential
  • Document Everything – FDA expects detailed compliance records

Additional FDA Resources for Nutraceutical Label Printing

Official government resources for nutraceutical label printing and FDA dietary supplement labeling:

  • FDA Dietary Supplements Main Page – Complete guidance on dietary supplement label regulations
  • FDA Labeling Requirements for Dietary Supplements – Official nutraceutical label printing guidance
  • FTC Health Claims Guidance – Advertising compliance for supplements
  • NIH Office of Dietary Supplements – Research and education on dietary supplements

Conclusion

Nutraceutical label printing requires precision, regulatory knowledge, and the right equipment. While FDA dietary supplement labeling requirements are complex, they’re manageable with proper planning and the right nutraceutical label printing partner.

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R gives supplement brands the flexibility to maintain compliance while responding to market opportunities. In-house digital printing reduces costs, shortens lead times, and provides the agility needed in the fast-moving supplement industry.

For supplement brands ready to take control of their labeling operations, the investment in compliant nutraceutical label printing technology pays dividends in reduced risk, lower costs, and faster time-to-market.

GHS labeling (Globally Harmonized System) is an international standard for classifying and communicating chemical hazards through standardized pictograms, signal words, and safety information on product labels. Required by OSHA since 2012, GHS labels ensure consistent hazard communication across countries and industries.

GHS labels are required for any chemical shipped or used in the workplace, and the penalty for non-compliance can reach $15,625 per violation. This guide explains the six required GHS label elements, OSHA specifications for durability and size, and how to choose a GHS-compliant label printer that produces chemical-resistant, UV-stable labels for drums, bottles, and totes. Whether you’re a chemical manufacturer, distributor, or end-user, understanding GHS requirements protects your workers and your business.

What Are GHS Label Printers and Why Do You Need One?

GHS Label Printers are the best specialized printing systems designed to produce compliant chemical safety labels that meet Globally Harmonized System (GHS) standards. For chemical manufacturers, understanding how to print GHS labels in-house is easy when you have the right equipment—and it’s about protecting workers, avoiding costly fines, and ensuring your products can be sold in global markets.

The Globally Harmonized System (GHS) of Classification and Labeling of Chemicals is an internationally standardized approach to defining and communicating chemical hazards.

GHS labels serve as the critical communication link between chemical producers and end users. They provide essential safety information through standardized pictograms, signal words, hazard statements, and precautionary measures.

Whether you’re producing industrial solvents, cleaning chemicals, or specialty chemical products, GHS compliance is mandatory for market access. This comprehensive guide covers everything you need to know about GHS label compliance in 2026, including how to print GHS labels, recent regulatory updates, and cost-saving strategies.

GHS Label Printer Requirements — Durability, Materials & Technology

Durability Standards (OSHA 1910.1200)

OSHA’s Hazard Communication Standard sets clear durability expectations that standard office printers simply cannot meet:

  • Must withstand chemical exposure — resistance to solvents, acids, and bases
  • Must resist UV light and outdoor weather for outdoor storage applications

OSHA Hazmat Label Requirements for GHS Label Printing

The Hazard Communication Standard (HCS 2012)

OSHA’s Hazard Communication Standard aligns with GHS requirements but includes specific provisions for the U.S. market:

Key OSHA Requirements:

  • All shipped hazardous chemical containers must have GHS labels
  • Workplace labels must be legible and prominently displayed
  • Labels must be written in English (additional languages permitted)
  • Pictograms must have a red border on a white background
  • Signal words must be in bold text

Recent 2026 Regulatory Updates

Chemical manufacturers should be aware of these recent changes to GHS label regulations:

  • Enhanced requirements for small container labeling

Real-World Success: Cleartech Industries, a valued Arrow Systems customer for over 10 years, recently expanded their finishing capabilities with our equipment. This demonstrates the long-term reliability and ROI of our GHS label printing solutions.

GHS Label Durability Requirements

Chemical safety labels must withstand harsh environments:

  • Chemical exposure: Resistance to solvents, acids, bases
  • Moisture: Waterproof and humidity-resistant
  • UV exposure: Fade-resistant for outdoor storage
  • Abrasion: Readable after handling and shipping
  • Temperature: Stability from -40°F to 150°F

The most effective solution: Pigment-based inkjet printing on synthetic substrates (BOPP, PET) provides superior durability compared to laser or thermal transfer methods.

5 Common GHS Label Compliance Mistakes to Avoid

Mistake #1: Incorrect Pictogram Selection

Many manufacturers select GHS pictograms based on general hazard categories rather than specific classification criteria. Each pictogram has precise triggering criteria—using the wrong one can result in OSHA compliance violations and safety risks.

Mistake #2: Missing Precautionary Statements

Precautionary statements must match the hazard classification level. Generic statements or incomplete P-statements (P264, P280, etc.) are common OSHA hazmat label violations.

Mistake #3: Illegible Small Container Labels

Containers under 100ml present unique chemical label compliance challenges. The solution: Use pull-out labels, fold-out labels, or tag-style labels that maintain full GHS compliance while fitting small surfaces.

Mistake #4: Outdated Safety Data Sheets

GHS labels and Safety Data Sheets (SDS) must align perfectly. Changes to one require updates to the other within 3-6 months depending on jurisdiction.

Mistake #5: Using the Wrong Printer Technology

Standard office printers lack the durability needed for chemical environments. Only GHS Label Printers with pigment-based inks can produce compliant, long-lasting labels.

GHS Label Printers: The ArrowJet Aqua 330R Solution

How to Print GHS Labels with Pigment Ink Technology

Water-based pigment inks offer critical advantages for GHS label compliance:

  • Lightfastness: 12+ month outdoor durability
  • Chemical resistance: Withstands common industrial chemicals
  • Water resistance: BS5609 Section 3 marine grade compliance
  • Smear resistance: Immediate handling durability
  • Low VOC: Safer for indoor production environments

Variable Data for Multi-SKU Chemical Operations

Chemical manufacturers often manage hundreds of SKUs with varying chemical label requirements:

  • Concentration percentages
  • Hazard classifications
  • Language requirements
  • Batch numbers and lot codes

Variable data printing enables single-template workflows where one design file + data spreadsheet = unlimited SKU variations. Change a chemical concentration or update a formula? Update the data file, not the artwork.

GHS Label Design Best Practices

Maximizing Legibility for GHS Labels

  • Font size: Minimum 6pt for body text, 8pt+ recommended
  • Contrast: High contrast between text and background
  • Whitespace: Adequate spacing around pictograms
  • Layout: Logical flow from hazard to precaution

Color Requirements for Chemical Labels

  • Pictogram borders: Red (Pantone 485 or equivalent)
  • Signal words: Black text on white background
  • Supplementary information: Can use additional colors
  • Background: White preferred, other colors acceptable with sufficient contrast

Multi-Language Considerations

For global chemical distribution, GHS labels often require:

  • Dual-language labeling (English/Spanish common in North America)
  • Regional hazard classification differences
  • Country-specific regulatory statements

Variable data printing handles multi-language how to print GHS labels for chemical products requirements efficiently—print English labels for domestic shipments, Spanish labels for export, all from the same template.

Your GHS Label Printing Implementation Roadmap

Phase 1: Hazard Classification Audit (Week 1)

  • Review all chemical formulations against GHS criteria
  • Identify required pictograms and hazard classes
  • Document precautionary statement requirements

Phase 2: Label Design and Template Creation (Week 2)

  • Develop compliant GHS label templates for each hazard class
  • Establish variable data fields for SKU-specific information
  • Create secondary templates for small containers (<100ml)

Phase 3: Production System Setup (Week 3)

  • Install pigment-based inkjet GHS label printer
  • Validate print quality against durability requirements
  • Train operators on GHS-specific printing procedures

Phase 4: Compliance Validation (Week 4)

  • Review sample labels against OSHA/GHS requirements
  • Conduct durability testing (chemical exposure, abrasion, UV)
  • Document compliance procedures for audit purposes

Phase 5: Full Production Transition (Week 5+)

  • Phase out outsourced label inventory
  • Implement lot code and date tracking
  • Establish label quality control procedures

GHS Labeling Resources and References

Stay informed about the latest developments in GHS label requirements:

  • OSHA Hazard Communication Standard (HCS)
  • United Nations GHS Portal
  • CDC NIOSH Chemical Safety
  • EPA Chemical Substance Safety

GHS Label Printer FAQ: Common Questions Answered

Q: What is GHS labeling and who needs it?

A: GHS (Globally Harmonized System) labeling is required by OSHA for any hazardous chemical manufactured, shipped, or used in the workplace. All chemical producers, distributors, and employers handling hazardous chemicals must comply — including downstream users who transfer chemicals into secondary containers.

 

Q: What are the six required GHS label elements?

A: The six required elements are: (1) Product Identifier — chemical name or code matching SDS Section 1; (2) Signal Word — ‘Danger’ or ‘Warning’; (3) Hazard Pictograms — visual symbols in red diamond border; (4) Hazard Statements — standardized risk descriptions; (5) Precautionary Statements — P-codes for prevention, response, storage, and disposal; and (6) Supplier Information — name, address, and telephone number.

 

Q: What is a GHS label printer?

A: A GHS label printer is a specialized printing system designed to produce chemical safety labels that comply with GHS standards. These printers use durable pigment-based inks and synthetic substrates to create labels that withstand harsh chemical environments while displaying required hazard pictograms, signal words, and precautionary statements — unlike standard office printers which lack the necessary chemical and UV resistance.

 

Q: How to print GHS labels that are OSHA compliant?

A: To print OSHA-compliant GHS labels: (1) Use a pigment-based inkjet printer for durability; (2) Print on synthetic substrates (BOPP, PET, or polypropylene); (3) Include all six required GHS elements; (4) Ensure pictograms have red borders on white backgrounds at minimum 10mm × 10mm; (5) Use minimum 6pt font for body text; (6) Include supplier contact information; (7) Validate labels against OSHA’s Hazard Communication Standard 1910.1200.

 

Q: How long do GHS labels need to last?

A: GHS labels must remain legible throughout the entire use period of the chemical, including exposure to the chemical itself, UV light, weather, temperature extremes, and normal handling. For outdoor-stored drums this typically means 12–24 months of chemical and UV exposure resistance minimum.

 

Q: Can I print GHS labels in-house?

A: Yes. With the right printer (pigment inkjet or thermal transfer) and durable synthetic label stock, you can produce OSHA-compliant GHS labels in-house at $0.04–$0.12 per label compared to $0.25–$0.85 outsourced. Most chemical manufacturers recover the investment within 12–18 months.

 

Q: What is the minimum size for GHS pictograms?

A: GHS pictograms must be at least 10mm × 10mm (approximately 0.4″) on the label. Larger containers require proportionally larger pictograms — on a standard 55-gallon drum label, pictograms are typically 25–50mm. Pictograms that are too small to be clearly visible from a normal viewing distance are a compliance violation.

 

Q: What label material is best for chemical drum GHS labels?

A: Polyester (PET) or polypropylene (BOPP) with a permanent aggressive adhesive provides the best chemical resistance and durability for drum labeling. For drums stored outdoors, add an overlaminate for additional UV and abrasion protection. Avoid paper-based labels on chemical containers — they degrade quickly under chemical splash.

 

Q: Do secondary workplace containers need GHS labels?

A: Yes. Any container holding a hazardous chemical in the workplace must have a GHS label — or at minimum a workplace label with the product identifier and hazard information. Exemptions exist only for containers that will be used immediately and by the person who transferred the chemical.

 

Q: What are the OSHA penalties for non-compliant GHS labels?

A: As of 2026, OSHA can fine up to $15,625 per serious violation and $156,259 per willful or repeat violation for GHS non-compliance. Penalties apply per container — a shipment of 100 non-compliant drums could generate $1.5M in fines.

 

Q: Can I use color laser printers for GHS labels?

A: Color laser printers work for indoor applications with limited chemical exposure, but inkjet with pigment inks or thermal transfer typically offers better durability for chemical and outdoor exposure. For BS5609 marine-grade compliance required for international chemical shipping, only pigment inkjet or UV inkjet systems qualify.

 

Q: How do I choose the right GHS label size?

A: Minimum label sizes vary by container: small bottles (3–100ml) require pull-out or fold-out labels with all six elements; 1–5 gallon containers typically use 4″ × 6″ labels; 55-gallon drums use 8.5″ × 11″ or larger. The key requirement is that all six GHS elements must be legible at the chosen size using a minimum 6pt font.

 

Q: How much does a GHS label printer cost?

A: GHS label printers range from $15,000 to $50,000 depending on features and production volume. The ArrowJet Aqua 330R offers industrial-grade GHS label printing at a mid-market price point, with most manufacturers recovering their investment within 12–18 months through reduced per-label costs and eliminated minimum order requirements.

Key Takeaways: How to Print GHS Labels Successfully

✓  Six Required Elements:  Product ID, Signal Word, Pictograms, Hazard Statements, Precautionary Statements, Supplier Info

✓  Durability Critical:  Labels must survive the container’s entire use lifecycle including chemical, UV, and abrasion exposure

✓  Pictogram Size:  Minimum 10mm × 10mm dimension required — larger containers need proportionally larger pictograms

✓  Best Printer Technology:  Pigment inkjet or thermal transfer on synthetic stock (BOPP, PET) for maximum compliance durability

✓  Penalty Risk:  Up to $15,625 per serious violation and $156,259 per willful violation for GHS non-compliance

Why GHS Label Printers Are Essential for Chemical Compliance

GHS label compliance is non-negotiable for chemical manufacturers, but it doesn’t have to be a bottleneck or cost center. Investing in the right GHS Label Printers and learning how to print GHS labels in-house with pigment-based inkjet technology provides:

  • Immediate cost savings: 60-80% reduction in per-label costs
  • Regulatory agility: Same-day label updates when formulations change
  • Quality control: Consistent, durable labels that withstand harsh environments
  • Scalability: Handle hundreds of SKUs without inventory complexity

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R delivers industrial-grade GHS label production capabilities without industrial-scale infrastructure requirements. For chemical operations ready to take control of their labeling compliance, the business case is compelling—and the operational benefits extend far beyond cost savings.

The Hidden Costs of Outsourced Cannabis Label Printing

If you’re running a cannabis operation—whether a cultivation facility, dispensary, or infused product manufacturer—you already know that labels are a non-negotiable expense. What you might not realize is how much money you’re leaving on the table by continuing to outsource your cannabis label printing production.

The typical outsourced cannabis label workflow looks like this: design your labels (or pay a designer), send files to a converter, wait 2-3 weeks for production, pay for shipping, receive your labels, discover a compliance error or design tweak needed, repeat the entire process.

Meanwhile, you’re writing checks for setup fees, plate charges, minimum order quantities, and rush fees when inventory runs low.

This article breaks down the real cost of outsourced cannabis label printing versus in-house cannabis label printing production—and provides a framework for determining when bringing cannabis label printing in-house makes financial sense for your operation.

Figure 1: Outsourced vs In-House Cannabis Label Printing Comparison

The True Cost Breakdown: Outsourced vs. In-House

Outsourced Label Costs (What You’re Paying Now)

Cost Category Typical Range Notes
Setup/Plate Fees $150-$400 per order Charged every time, even for reorders with minor changes
Minimum Order Quantity 1,000-5,000 labels Forces over-ordering; obsolete inventory when regulations change
Per-Label Cost (1,000 qty) $0.15-$0.45 Decreases with volume, but you’re locked into large orders
Per-Label Cost (5,000 qty) $0.08-$0.25 Better unit cost, but capital tied up in inventory
Shipping $25-$75 per order Adds up with frequent reorders
Rush Fees 25-50% surcharge When you run low and need labels fast
Design Revision Costs $50-$200 per change New plates for every tweak
Obsolete Inventory 10-20% annual waste Regulations change; designs evolve; strains rotate

Real-World Example: A mid-size cultivator running 12 strains, ordering 2,500 labels per strain quarterly:

  • Annual label volume: 120,000 labels
  • Per-label cost: $0.18 average

  • Shipping: $50 × 12 orders = $600
  • Rush fees (estimated 4x/year): $1,200

Beyond Cost: The Operational Advantages

ROI calculations focus on dollars, but the operational benefits of in-house printing often matter more than the financial savings:

1. Eliminate Lead Times

Outsourced labels: 2-3 weeks minimum
In-house cannabis label printing: Same-day production

When a new strain passes testing and needs to ship tomorrow, in-house printing means you don’t miss the window.

2. End Minimum Order Quantities

Need 200 labels for a limited strain release? Print 200 labels. No more ordering 2,500 to get a reasonable price and storing 2,300 in a warehouse.

3. Instant Design Changes

Regulatory update requires new warning language? Design change approved at 2 PM? Updated labels are printing by 3 PM. No setup fees. No delays.

Run 12 strains? That’s 12 label SKUs minimum. With variable data printing on the Aqua 330R, one design template + data file = unlimited strain variants.

Stop tying up capital in cannabis label printing inventory. Print as needed, preserve cash for other priorities.

In-house label printing isn’t for everyone. Consider these factors:

Strong Candidates for In-House:

  • Annual label volume exceeds 30,000 units
  • Frequent design changes or regulatory updates
  • Multiple strains/SKUs requiring versioning
  • Seasonal or limited-edition products
  • Quality control concerns with outsourced cannabis label printing
  • Need for same-day turnaround capability
  • Desire to bring packaging in-house as competitive advantage

Outsourcing May Still Make Sense If:

  • Annual volume under 20,000 labels

Implementation Roadmap

Conclusion

The decision to bring cannabis label printing in-house is fundamentally a math problem with operational implications. For operations printing 30,000+ labels annually, the financial case is compelling—often delivering payback in 12-18 months with ongoing annual savings of $10,000-$30,000+.

But the numbers only tell part of the story. The real value is operational flexibility: same-day turnaround, no minimum orders, instant design changes, and the ability to version labels for every strain and SKU without cost penalties.

The Rise of Sustainable Packaging: Why Water-Activated Tape is Taking Over in 2025

Introduction

The packaging industry is undergoing a sustainability revolution. Single-use plastics are being phased out. Consumers are demanding eco-friendly alternatives. And regulators worldwide are tightening packaging waste laws.

At the center of this transformation is an unexpected hero: water-activated tape (WAT). Once considered old-fashioned, this simple kraft paper tape is now the darling of sustainable packaging. And thanks to digital printing technology like the ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite, custom-branded water-activated tape is more accessible than ever.

Explore More

The Problem with Plastic Packaging Tape

Plastic pressure-sensitive tape (the clear or brown tape most people use) has dominated packaging for decades. But it comes with significant environmental costs.

Environmental Impact of Plastic Tape

Non-Recyclable Contamination:
Plastic tape must be removed from cardboard boxes before recycling. If left on, it contaminates the cardboard recycling stream, often causing entire batches to be landfilled.

Microplastic Pollution:
When plastic tape breaks down, it does not biodegrade — it fragments into microplastics that persist in the environment for centuries.

Petroleum Dependence:
Most plastic tape is made from polypropylene, a petroleum-derived plastic that contributes to fossil fuel consumption.

Limited Recyclability:
Even recyclable plastic tape often lacks the infrastructure for actual recycling and ends up in landfills or incinerators.

The Numbers

  • Over 1.3 billion pounds of packaging tape are used annually in the US alone

  • Less than 5% of plastic tape is effectively recycled

  • Each roll of plastic tape has a carbon footprint 3–4x higher than paper alternatives

Why Water-Activated Tape Is the Sustainable Solution

Water-activated tape, also known as gummed tape or kraft paper tape, offers a fundamentally different environmental profile.

100% Biodegradable and Compostable:

Water-activated tape is made from kraft paper with a starch-based adhesive. Both components are plant-derived materials, fully biodegradable within weeks to months, safe for home and industrial composting, and non-toxic if they enter waterways.

Curbside Recyclable:

Unlike plastic tape, water-activated tape can be left on cardboard boxes during recycling. The paper fibers and adhesive break down in the pulping process, causing no contamination. This means no need to remove tape before recycling, higher recycling rates for corrugated boxes, and less labor in waste management.

Renewable Resources:

Kraft paper comes from trees — a renewable resource when managed responsibly. Most water-activated tape manufacturers use FSC-certified paper sources, recycled content options (up to 100% recycled), and sustainable forestry practices.

Reduced Material Usage:

Water-activated tape forms a permanent bond with cardboard fibers, requiring only a single strip for secure sealing. Compare this to plastic tape, which often requires multiple strips for security, additional reinforcement tape for heavy boxes, and H-taping technique using significantly more material.

Material efficiency:

One strip of WAT = 3–4 strips of plastic tape in holding power.

The Branding Challenge: Why Sustainability Needed Digital Printing

or years, sustainable packaging came with a branding trade-off. Plastic tape could be easily printed with logos and designs, but water-activated tape traditionally required expensive flexographic printing with high minimum orders.

This meant many businesses had to choose:

  • Option A: Eco-friendly tape with no branding

  • Option B: Branded plastic tape that hurts the environment

Neither option served businesses that wanted both sustainability and professional presentation.

Digital Printing Bridges the Gap

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite changes this equation completely. This digital inkjet printer uses aqueous (water-based) pigment inks to print directly onto water-activated tape in full color.

Why Aqueous Inks Matter

Traditional solvent-based inks contain volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that emit harmful fumes during printing, require special ventilation and disposal, and contribute to air pollution.

Aqueous inks used in the ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite use water as the primary carrier, emit minimal VOCs, are safer for workers and the environment, and produce vibrant, durable prints on kraft paper.

The Sustainability Stack

When you combine water-activated tape with digital aqueous printing, you get:

  1. Biodegradable substrate (kraft paper)

  2. Plant-based adhesive (starch gum)

  3. Water-based inks (no solvents)

  4. On-demand production (no waste from overruns)

  5. No plate manufacturing (reduced industrial waste)

This is truly sustainable custom packaging.

Consumer Demand for Sustainable Packaging

The market is speaking loudly.

Consumer Preferences

  • 74% of consumers are willing to pay more for sustainable packaging

  • 60% say packaging sustainability affects their purchase decisions

  • 50% have switched brands based on environmental practices

Business Response

  • 82% of companies have sustainable packaging goals for 2025

  • Major retailers (Amazon, Walmart, Target) have packaging sustainability mandates

  • B2B customers increasingly require sustainability credentials from suppliers

Regulatory Pressure

  • Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) laws expanding globally

  • Plastic bans and restrictions in dozens of countries

  • Packaging waste reduction targets in the EU and beyond

Cost Reality: Is Sustainable Tape More Expensive?

The perception persists that eco-friendly means expensive. But the math has changed.

Traditional Cost Comparison

FactorPlastic TapeWater-Activated Tape
Material costLowerSlightly higher
Tape needed per box2–4 strips1 strip
Actual cost per boxsh.08–0.15sh.06–0.12

When you factor in reduced material usage, costs are comparable — and sometimes water-activated tape is cheaper.

Digital Printing Cost Comparison

Old Flexographic Method

  • Plate costs: 00–500 per color

  • Minimum order: 10,000+ feet

  • Small business barrier: High

New Digital Method (ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite)

  • Plate costs: sh

  • Minimum order: 100 feet

  • Small business barrier: None

Sustainable branded packaging is now accessible to businesses of all sizes.

Real-World Adoption Stories

E-Commerce Subscription Box

Challenge: Monthly subscription box service wanted plastic-free packaging but needed branded tape for unboxing experience.
Solution: Switched to digitally printed water-activated tape using the ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite.
Results: Eliminated 2,400 pounds of plastic tape annually, customer satisfaction increased, and cost per package decreased by 12%.

B2B Industrial Supplier

Challenge: Required to achieve 50% sustainable packaging by 2025.
Solution: Replaced plastic tape with reinforced water-activated tape printed with handling instructions and branding.
Results: Achieved sustainability goal 18 months early, reduced tape-related complaints, and won new contracts.

Artisan Food Producer

Challenge: Needed to convey premium quality and environmental values through packaging.
Solution: Short runs of custom water-activated tape with seasonal designs.
Results: Stronger brand alignment, increased social media mentions, and zero inventory waste.

The Future of Sustainable Packaging Tape

Key trends accelerating adoption:

  1. Advanced Inks – More vibrant colors, better durability, bio-based formulations

  2. Automation Integration – Smarter dispensers, lower labor costs

  3. Circular Economy Design – Optimized for recycling and composting

  4. Regulatory Momentum – Plastic bans and carbon pricing favor sustainable options

How to Transition to Sustainable Tape

  1. Assess Your Volume – Understand current usage and seasonality

  2. Evaluate Branding Needs – Custom vs stock, design flexibility

  3. Choose the Right Tape Type – Non-reinforced, reinforced, or custom printed

  4. Select Application Method – Manual, electric, or integrated systems

  5. Source Responsibly – FSC paper, aqueous inks, credible suppliers

Conclusion: The Sustainable Choice Is Now the Smart Choice

Water-activated tape has evolved from a niche eco-product to a mainstream packaging solution. Digital printing technology has removed the barriers that once limited access to custom-branded sustainable tape.

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R Lite represents a new era — where sustainability, affordability, and professional branding converge. Businesses no longer need to compromise environmental values for marketing impact.

The future of packaging is here. And it is printed with water-based inks on kraft paper.

The Ultimate Guide to Bottle Labels: Everything You Need to Know

Bottle labels are adhesive-backed graphics applied to glass, plastic, or metal containers to identify products, display branding, provide regulatory information, and communicate essential details to consumers. Bottle labels come in various types including pressure-sensitive labels, shrink sleeves, and cut-and-stack formats—each suited to different bottle shapes, materials, and durability requirements.

Bottle labels do more than identify your product—they’re your silent salesperson on the shelf. Whether you’re labeling wine bottles, juice containers, cosmetics, or chemical drums, choosing the right label material, adhesive, and finish determines how your product performs in retail environments, withstands moisture, and communicates your brand. This guide covers bottle label types, materials, design considerations, and printing options from digital short runs to high-volume flexographic production.

Introduction

Bottle labels are more than just pieces of paper or plastic stuck onto bottles. They serve as the face of the product, conveying vital information, attracting customers, and differentiating the brand in a crowded marketplace. Whether you’re in the food and beverage industry, pharmaceuticals, or cosmetics, understanding the intricacies of bottle labeling is crucial. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know about bottle labels.

The Basics of Bottle Labels

What are Bottle Labels?

Bottle labels are adhesive stickers or tags applied to bottles to provide information about the product inside. They can include brand names, logos, ingredients, instructions, and other essential details.

Types of Bottle Labels

  • Wrap-around Labels: Cover the entire circumference of the bottle.
  • Pressure-sensitive Labels: Easy to apply and stick to the bottle with pressure.
  • Shrink Sleeve Labels: Wrap around the bottle and shrink when heat is applied.
  • In-mold Labels: Integrated into the bottle during the manufacturing process.

Materials Used in Bottle Labels

Paper Labels

Paper labels are cost-effective and versatile, suitable for many products. They can be coated or uncoated, depending on the desired finish.

Plastic Labels

Plastic labels are durable and resistant to moisture and chemicals, making them ideal for products like beverages and cleaning supplies.

Foil Labels

Foil labels add a premium look with their metallic finish, often used for luxury products like wines and spirits.

Bottle Label Materials

Paper Labels

  • Coated Paper: Vibrant colors, wine/spirits, dry environments
  • Uncoated: Natural/organic look, textured feel
  • Parchment: Specialty/premium positioning
  • Limitations: Not waterproof, may wrinkle with condensation

Film Labels (Vinyl/Synthetic)

  • BOPP (Biaxial PP): Most popular, moisture/chemical resistant, clear or white
  • Vinyl: Conformable for curved surfaces, outdoor durability
  • PET/Polyester: Premium, rigid, excellent clarity
  • Advantages: Waterproof, won’t tear, survives temperature changes

Specialty Materials

  • Metallized: Premium/cosmetic look
  • Textured: Linen, embossed, tactile
  • Dissolvable: Sustainability/specialty
  • Plant-Based: Eco-friendly options

Designing Bottle Labels

Essential Design Elements

Creating an effective bottle label involves several key elements:

  • Brand Name and Logo: The most prominent part of the label.
  • Product Information: Ingredients, usage instructions, and other relevant details.
  • Visuals: Images or graphics that represent the product.

Color Psychology in Labels

Colors evoke emotions and can influence purchasing decisions. For example, green often indicates natural or organic products, while red can stimulate appetite.

Typography and Fonts

Choosing the right fonts is essential for readability and brand identity. Serif fonts can convey tradition and reliability, while sans-serif fonts are modern and clean.

Design Best Practices

Hierarchy of Information:

  1. Brand Name: Largest, most prominent
  2. Product Name: Clear, readable
  3. Visual/Graphics: Color, imagery
  4. Required Info: Ingredients, warnings, net contents
  5. Supporting: QR codes, certifications, social proof

 

Technical Considerations:

  • Safety Zone: Keep critical text 0.125″ from edges
  • Bleed: Allow 0.125″ extra for cutting
  • Barcodes: Minimum 1.5″ x 1″ for reliable scanning
  • Font Size: Minimum 6pt body text, 4pt for fine print

Why Choose ArrowJet Aqua 330R for Bottle Labels?

Increased Efficiency: With its high-speed printing capability of 90 feet per minute, the ArrowJet Aqua 330R enables label converters to handle large volumes quickly, reducing turnaround times and increasing productivity.

Enhanced Print Quality: The printer’s high resolution of 1600 x 1600 dpi ensures that every label is produced with exceptional clarity and vibrancy. This high-quality output enhances the overall appearance of labels, which can lead to higher customer satisfaction and repeat business.

Versatile Application: The ArrowJet Aqua 330R’s ability to print on various materials and sizes means that label converters can offer a broader range of products to their clients. Cost Savings: The printer’s efficient ink usage and minimal waste help to lower production costs. The use of aqueous pigment inks, which are often less expensive and more environmentally friendly than solvent-based inks, contributes to overall cost savings while maintaining high-quality results.

Regulatory Compliance: With Swiss compliant inks, the ArrowJet Aqua 330R ensures that labels meet stringent environmental and safety standards. Competitive Edge: The combination of speed, quality, and regulatory compliance allows label converters to offer premium products and services. This competitive edge can attract new clients and retain existing ones, boosting business growth and profitability.

Eco-friendly Materials

Sustainable Printing Practices

Vintage and Retro Styles

Factors Influencing Costs

Material choice, printing method, design complexity, and order volume all influence the cost of bottle labels.

Plan your budget by considering both initial design and production costs and long-term label needs.

FAQs

What are bottle labels made of?

Bottle labels are typically made of paper (for dry/durable uses) or synthetic films like BOPP, vinyl, or PET (for moisture/chemical resistance). The label face material bonds to a backing liner via adhesive.

What label material is best for bottles that get wet?

BOPP (biaxially-oriented polypropylene) film labels are the best choice for beverage, bath, and outdoor products because they’re fully waterproof, won’t tear, and resist condensation.

What's the difference between paper and vinyl labels for bottles?

Paper labels cost less and print vibrantly but aren’t waterproof and can tear. Vinyl/film labels are waterproof, more durable, and conform better to curved surfaces but cost more.

How do I choose the right size label for my bottle?

Measure your bottle’s circumference and decide your coverage area. Leave 0.5-1″ gap for overlap on wrap-around labels. Test with paper templates before printing.

Can I print bottle labels myself?

Yes. For small quantities (under 500), desktop label printers work. For professional results at 500+ labels, invest in a digital label printer or use a label printing service.

What's better: roll labels or sheet labels for bottles?

Roll labels are standard for commercial production with automated labelers. Sheet labels work for hand-application or very small quantities. Roll format is more cost-effective at scale.

Do I need waterproof labels for refrigerated products?

Yes. Products in refrigerated or cold environments will get condensation. Use BOPP or polyester film labels with permanent adhesive—not paper labels.

Can I get clear labels for a "no-label" look?

Yes. Clear BOPP or PET labels create a premium “printed on bottle” appearance. Use white ink behind elements or screen important text directly on the bottle color.

✓  Best Film:  BOPP for general use, vinyl for conformability, PET for premium

✓  Sizing:  Always measure actual bottle; leave 0.5″ overlap on wrap labels

✓  Type:  Pressure-sensitive for most, shrink sleeves for 360° coverage

✓  Cost Tip:  Digital printing economical at 500-5,000 labels; flexo beyond 50K

Conclusion

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R is a versatile, high-performance printer that meets the diverse needs of bottle labeling. Its advanced features ensure that labels are not only visually appealing but also durable and suitable for various environments. Whether it’s for custom wine labels, daycare bottle labels, baby bottle labels, custom water bottle labels, or beer bottle labels, the ArrowJet Aqua 330R delivers exceptional results.

Table of Contents

Flexible Packaging: Types, Materials, Applications, and Benefits

Flexible packaging refers to any package or container made of easily yielding materials — such as paper, plastic film, foil, or combinations thereof — that can be bent, folded, or shaped to fit contents. Unlike rigid packaging (bottles, jars, cans), flexible packaging conforms to product shape, offering superior space efficiency, lighter weight, and lower shipping costs.

Flexible packaging is the fastest-growing segment in packaging, now representing over 30% of the $1 trillion global packaging market. From stand-up pouches and flat bags to shrink sleeves and films, flexible formats offer brands unmatched versatility, sustainability benefits (less material per unit), and consumer convenience features like resealable zippers. This guide covers flexible packaging types, materials, ideal applications, and how digital printing is transforming short-run flexible packaging economics.

Flexible packaging refers to packaging made from materials that can easily change shape—such as plastic films, paper, aluminum foil, or laminates. Unlike rigid packaging, it adapts to the product it contains, making it versatile, lightweight, and cost-effective. Today, flexible packaging dominates industries ranging from food and beverages to pharmaceuticals and cosmetics because of its durability, printability, and strong barrier properties that preserve product freshness.

In this comprehensive guide, we’ll explore the overview of flexible packaging, the main types, materials used, its applications across industries, and the advantages driving its global adoption.

Overview of Flexible Packaging

Flexible packaging is designed to bend, fold, or reshape while still protecting the product inside. It includes bags, pouches, liners, tubes, wraps, and laminated rolls. The adaptability of these formats makes them ideal for both everyday consumer goods and specialized industrial products.

Brands prefer flexible packaging because it:

  • Uses fewer raw materials than rigid packaging.

  • Lowers shipping costs thanks to lightweight design.

  • Provides high-quality printing surfaces for logos and graphics.

  • Improves shelf appeal by allowing creative designs and resealable options.

Equally important, barrier properties such as resistance to moisture, oxygen, light, and contaminants help extend product shelf life—an essential factor for perishable goods.

1. Flexible Pouches

One of the most popular packaging formats worldwide, flexible pouches are available in flat, stand-up, spouted, and resealable styles. Stand-up pouches with gusseted bottoms are especially attractive on retail shelves.

  • Applications: Snacks, frozen foods, coffee, pet food, beverages, lotions, pharmaceuticals, and industrial liquids.

2. Bags and Sachets

Simple yet versatile, bags and sachets serve both single-use and retail purposes. From ketchup packets to shopping bags, they dominate convenience packaging.

  • Materials: LDPE, HDPE, coated paper, biodegradable polymers.

  • Applications: Grocery and fashion bags, food sachets, pharma samples, and household goods.

3. Rolls and Laminated Films

Flexible packaging rolls are used in form-fill-seal machines to create wrappers and pouches. Laminated films combine multiple layers for durability and protection.

  • Materials: Multilayer laminates with foil and polymers.

  • Applications: Candy bars, snacks, confectionery, agrochemicals, and pharma wrappers.

4. Wraps and Stretch Films

Thin wraps and films protect fresh produce and perishable goods. Stretch films also bundle and palletize shipments, reducing logistics damage.

    • Materials: LDPE, LLDPE, BOPP, PVC.

    • Applications: Meat, cheese, fresh produce, shipping pallets.

5. Tubes

Flexible tubes provide controlled dispensing, making them a favorite in personal care packaging.

  • Materials: Laminated plastic films, aluminum-based laminates.

  • Applications: Toothpaste, gels, lotions, adhesives, and pharmaceutical creams.

6. Specialty Flexible Packaging

Specialty formats include vacuum-sealed pouches, biodegradable films, compostable laminates, and vacuum metalized films (VMPET). These are designed for high-barrier or eco-friendly applications.

    • Applications: Organic food packaging, eco-conscious brands, pharmaceuticals, and high-value products.

Applications in Different Industries

Food and Beverage Industry

Flexible packaging is the backbone of food packaging. It preserves taste, aroma, and freshness while offering resealable convenience.

  • Examples: Chips, nuts, frozen veggies, dairy, coffee, sauces, and ready-to-eat meals.

  • Why it matters: Protects from moisture and oxygen, reducing food waste.

Pharmaceuticals

In pharma, safety and sterility are non-negotiable. Flexible packaging such as laminated pouches, blister packs, and sachets helps maintain product integrity.

Personal Care and Cosmetics

Advantages of Flexible Packaging

Why is flexible packaging overtaking rigid formats? The answer lies in its unique advantages:

  1. Lightweight and space-saving – Reduces transport costs and carbon footprint.

  2. Durability – Resistant to punctures and tears.

  3. Versatility – Customizable in size, shape, and design.

  4. Extended shelf life – Protects against oxygen, moisture, and UV light.

  5. Cost-effective – Lower material use and reduced logistics costs.

  6. Convenience – Easy to open, resealable, and portion-friendly.

  7. Sustainability – Recyclable and compostable options are increasing.

  8. Branding potential – High-resolution printing for maximum shelf appeal.

Frequently Asked Questions — Flexible Packaging

Q: What is flexible packaging?

A: Flexible packaging is any package made of pliable materials — plastic film, paper, or foil — that can be bent or folded, including bags, pouches, wraps, and films. It contrasts with rigid containers like bottles, jars, or cans. The most common examples are stand-up pouches, flat sachets, shrink film, and laminated rolls.

Q: What are the advantages of flexible packaging over rigid?

A: Flexible packaging uses up to 70% less material per unit, weighs 85% less for shipping (reducing freight costs), offers better shelf appeal through 360° graphics, and typically costs less per unit than rigid alternatives. It also provides consumer convenience features like resealable zippers and easy-open tear notches that rigid packaging cannot match.

Q: Is flexible packaging recyclable?

A: Multi-layer flexible packaging is challenging to recycle due to mixed material structures. New mono-material structures (all polyethylene or all polypropylene) are specifically designed for recyclability. Look for the How2Recycle label or check local drop-off programs — many grocery stores accept PE film for recycling.

Q: What is the difference between pouches and bags?

A: ‘Pouch’ typically refers to a pre-formed, often gusseted bag with structural stability — particularly stand-up pouches. ‘Bag’ is a general term for any flexible container, often pillow-style without gussets. In industry usage, pouches are usually considered more premium with more complex sealing and finishing options.

Q: Can I print directly on flexible packaging?

A: Yes. Digital inkjet printers like the ArrowJet Aqua 800M and Hybrid Pro M can print on roll-fed flexible packaging materials including PE, PP, and paper-based flexible substrates — ideal for short runs (500+ units), prototypes, and variable data. Substrates must be corona-treated or primer-coated for proper ink adhesion.

Q: What is the minimum order quantity for flexible packaging?

A: Traditional flexographic printing requires minimum orders of 25,000–50,000 units due to plate costs and setup. Digital printing reduces minimums to 500–2,000 units with no plate costs, making it economically viable for small brands, seasonal editions, and new product launches.

Q: What coatings are needed for printing on flexible packaging?

A: Substrates need corona treatment or primer coating for ink adhesion. Water-based pigment inks require specially coated films for proper bond strength. UV inks adhere to a wider range of materials but have food-contact limitations. Always request print-ready (corona-treated) film stock from your supplier.

Q: What materials are used for flexible food packaging?

A: The most common materials for food flexible packaging are PET/PE laminates, BOPP/CPP structures, and PET/ALU/PE foil laminates for high-barrier applications. Mono-PE structures are increasingly used for sustainable recyclable food pouches. The choice depends on the specific barrier requirements — moisture, oxygen, UV, or grease.

Q: How is flexible packaging different from rigid packaging?

A: Flexible packaging conforms to product shape and can be folded, squeezed, or rolled up. Rigid packaging maintains a fixed shape regardless of contents. Flexible is lighter, cheaper per unit, and more sustainable but offers less crush protection than rigid formats. Most food categories have shifted from rigid to flexible over the past 20 years.

Q: What is a stand-up pouch and why is it popular?

A: A stand-up pouch is a flexible bag with a gusseted bottom that allows it to stand upright on retail shelves. It’s popular because it combines the shelf presence of rigid packaging with the cost and weight advantages of flexible formats. Stand-up pouches are widely used for coffee, pet food, snacks, supplements, and cannabis products.

Key Takeaways

✓  Definition:  Pliable materials (film, paper, foil) that conform to product shape vs. rigid containers

✓  Popular Types:  Stand-up pouches, flat bags, Mylar, shrink film, tubes — each with specific use cases

✓  Materials:  PE, PP, PET, BOPP — often multi-layer structures for enhanced barrier properties

✓  Key Benefits:  Lower cost, 85% lighter shipping, sustainability advantages, 360° branding surface

✓  Digital Printing:  Enables short runs (500+ units) with no plate costs and fast turnaround for flexible packaging

The Future of Flexible Packaging

The future of flexible packaging lies in sustainability and innovation. With rising environmental concerns, companies are shifting to biodegradable polymers, paper laminates, and recyclable pouches. Smart packaging technologies—such as QR codes, freshness indicators, and interactive labels—are also emerging.

Global demand is projected to rise steadily, especially in food, beverages, and healthcare. Brands that embrace eco-friendly flexible packaging will not only meet regulatory requirements but also win consumer loyalty.

Conclusion

Flexible packaging has become an essential part of modern packaging strategies. Its versatility, barrier properties, lightweight design, and branding opportunities make it indispensable across industries. From food and beverage packaging to pharmaceuticals and cosmetics, its impact is undeniable.

Looking forward, sustainable flexible packaging solutions will dominate, as brands and consumers alike prioritize environmental responsibility. By embracing innovative materials and eco-conscious designs, businesses can stay ahead in this rapidly evolving market.

What Is Mylar? Uses, Thickness & Printability Explained (Ultimate 2026 Guide)

Mylar is a brand name for biaxially-oriented polyethylene terephthalate (BoPET) — a stretched polyester film known for its exceptional strength, chemical stability, and barrier properties. Invented by DuPont in the 1950s, Mylar has become the generic term for all BoPET films used in packaging, electronics, and industrial applications.

Mylar is a strong, flexible polyester film used primarily for food storage, flexible packaging, and protective barriers. Available in thicknesses from 2 to 14 mil (0.002″ to 0.014″), Mylar bags offer superior oxygen and moisture barriers compared to standard plastic — making them ideal for long-term food storage, cannabis packaging, and electronics protection. This guide covers Mylar types, thickness selection, and how to print professional labels and designs directly on Mylar packaging.

Mylar bags are everywhere today  from coffee packaging to pet treats, snacks, supplements, cannabis packaging, nutraceutical pouches, and even emergency food storage. Yet despite their popularity, many brands and converters still ask:

“What exactly is Mylar, what thickness do I need, and how do I print it?”

If that sounds like you, you’re in the right place.

This guide breaks down Mylar in simple, business-friendly language while giving you the deep technical accuracy your converters, production teams, and brand managers expect.

Let’s dive in.

What Is Mylar?

Mylar is a brand name for biaxially-oriented polyethylene terephthalate (BoPET), a strong polyester film known for its durability, barrier protection, heat resistance, and smooth print surface.

In simpler terms?
 Mylar is the ultra-tough, food-safe, shiny (or matte) plastic film used to make most modern flexible packaging  especially resealable bags and stand-up pouches.

Why Mylar Became the Packaging Standard

Mylar is trusted across industries because it offers:

  • Exceptional oxygen and moisture barrier performance

  • High tensile strength (it doesn’t tear easily)

  • Heat-seal compatibility

  • Lightweight construction

  • Smooth, ink-friendly surface

  • Long shelf-life stability

It checks every box brands care about: product protection, branding potential, and reliable performance.

Where Is Mylar Used? 10 Major Applications

Mylar is one of the most versatile substrates on earth. You’ll find it in:

1. Custom Mylar Bags & Pouches

The #1 use case — from food to wellness products.

2. Coffee & Tea Packaging

Oxygen barrier = preserved aroma.

3. Cannabis & CBD Packaging

Child-resistant + scent-proof performance.

4. Snack & Confectionery Packaging

5. Pet Food & Treat Bags

6. Powdered Supplements & Protein Pouches

7. Long-Term Food Storage

Preppers love Mylar for a reason.

8. Electronics & Component Packaging

Anti-static protection.

9. Medical & Pharmaceutical Packaging

10. Industrial Films & Insulation

Because Mylar is exceptionally stable across temperature ranges.

  • Often combined with foil layer for enhanced oxygen barrier
  • Suitable for nuts, dried goods, powders, and ready meals

  • Child-resistant compatible closures
  • Smell-proof barrier properties
  • UV-resistant options for light-sensitive products
  • Typically 6–8 mil with resealable zipper closures

 

Electronics-Grade Mylar

  • ESD (electrostatic discharge) protection
  • Ultra-high purity film
  • 2–5 mil for static shielding bags and component packaging

 

Medical / Pharmaceutical Mylar

  • ISO 13485 certified manufacturing available
  • Sterilizable grades for medical device packaging
  • Tamper-evident compatible seals

Is Mylar Good for Printing? Understanding Printability

The short answer?

Yes — Mylar is excellent for printing, especially with modern digital inkjet technology.

But print success depends on three factors:

1. Surface Treatment (Corona or Chemical)

Untreated Mylar is too smooth for ink adhesion.
 Processors treat it to increase surface energy, making ink bond tightly.

2. Ink Compatibility

Mylar works with:

  • Pigment inkjet inks (best for durability & lamination)

  • UV-curable inks (great for labels, not ideal for food contact)

  • Solvent/eco-solvent inks (depends on food safety)

  • Flexo inks (industry standard for large volumes)

  • Gravure inks (for extremely high-volume runs)

Food, beverage, and nutraceutical brands increasingly prefer water-based pigment inkjet because it offers:

  • Excellent rub resistance

  • Food-grade compliance

  • Compatibility with lamination, pouching, sealing

  • Vibrant colors

3. Heat Sensitivity

Because Mylar films can distort under extreme heat, print engines must maintain precise temperature control.

This is where high-end systems like the ArrowJet Aqua series outperform basic inkjet printers.

Why Digital Inkjet Is Dominating Mylar Packaging in 2026

Modern inkjet systems deliver what traditional flexo and gravure simply cannot:

  • Short Runs without financial penalties

  • Micro-versioning for flavors, batches, SKUs, and regions

  • Personalization at scale from influencer drops to limited editions

  • Lightning-fast turnarounds to keep up with fast-moving markets

  • Zero plate costs, eliminating delays and cutting waste

This combination has made inkjet the preferred choice for converters focused on premium flexible packaging.

Pros of Digital Inkjet for Mylar Films

Digital inkjet offers a set of advantages uniquely suited to the challenges of printing onto Mylar, especially when paired with pigment-based, food-safe inks:

✔ Ideal for Small to Medium Production Volumes

Inkjet empowers converters to run 500 bags in the morning and 5,000 in the afternoon—without changing hardware or printing plates.

✔ Ultra-Fast Job Changeovers

Switch SKUs, flavors, languages, or artwork with a click. Inkjet workflow is built for multi-SKU environments.

✔ Zero Plates = Lower Costs for Short Runs

Every new design printed flexographically adds cost. Inkjet eliminates plates entirely, making short runs extremely profitable.

✔ Perfect for Seasonal, Promotional & Limited-Edition Packaging

Holiday editions, collaboration drops, event packaging these projects thrive with inkjet’s flexibility.

✔ High-Resolution, Photo-Realistic Print Quality

Modern inkjet heads deliver sharp text, rich blacks, vibrant colors, and photographic detail that stand out on shelves.

✔ Works Exceptionally Well With Pigment Inks

Pigment inks are the gold standard for Mylar bags because they offer:

  • Superior durability

  • Excellent rub and water resistance

  • Stability during lamination and heat sealing

  • Fade-free performance in long storage cycles

This makes inkjet an even stronger choice for food, supplements, and cannabis applications.

Best Use Cases for Digital Inkjet Mylar Printing

Digital inkjet is the top-performing solution for converters serving high-growth packaging categories:

1. Custom Mylar Bags for Supplements

Perfect for vitamin blends, protein powders, pre-workouts, nutraceuticals, and sample-size trial packs.

2. Cannabis & CBD Packaging

Mylar bags dominate this segment because of their durability, oxygen barrier, and premium feel. Inkjet allows rapid SKU changes for strains, flavors, and compliance updates.

3. Coffee Pouches

Print small-batch roasts, origin-specific blends, or seasonal drops without minimum order headaches.

4. Limited Editions & Promotional Packaging

Brand collaborations, influencers, seasonal promos, or short-term campaigns thrive with inkjet’s flexibility.

5. Prototype & Sampling Runs

Designers and brand owners can test multiple variants quickly—critical for startups and new product development.

What About Hybrid Printing? The Best of Both Worlds

Hybrid printing is becoming one of the fastest-growing printing methods in flexible packaging and Mylar production — and for good reason.

Instead of choosing between digital and flexo, hybrid technology allows converters to use both on the same press, unlocking benefits neither platform can deliver alone.

How Hybrid Printing Typically Works

  • Flexo handles the high-coverage, repeatable parts
     – Solid background colors
     – Flood coating
     – White ink layers
     – Varnish or primers

  • Digital handles the dynamic, changeable parts
     – Variable data
     – SKU variations
     – Seasonal editions
     – Short-run campaigns

Why This Matters for Converters

Hybrid printing significantly reduces cost while improving operational speed:

  • Flexo prints the “cheap-to-produce” static area.

  • Digital prints only the variable or SKU-specific segments.

  • No need to waste digital ink on large backgrounds.

  • No need to create a flexo plate for every SKU.

The result?
 Lower production cost, faster time to market, and far more flexibility.

This system combines full flexo capability with high-resolution digital inkjet printing, giving converters the power to scale Mylar bag production like never before.

Why ArrowJet Hybrid Pro M+ Is a Game-Changer

Explore More

This is not a “digital press with a flexo station” — it’s a fully integrated hybrid press.
 You can run:

  • Flexo → Digital → Flexo

  • Flexo-only

This adaptability allows converters to build workflows around cost, ink usage, SKU complexity, and turn-around time.

  • Laminated films

  • Flexo coating

     

  • Cold foil

     

  • Die-cutting

     

  • Slitting

     

  • Rewinding

Meaning converters can move from blank film → finished roll → pouching line with minimal touches.

6. Lowest Cost Hybrid Production in Its Class

With flexo doing heavy lifting on ink coverage and digital handling design variations, converters can enjoy:

  • Faster job setup

     

  • Minimal waste

 ✔ Want to eliminate outsourcing

If your customers constantly request new flavors, limited editions, or rapid redesigns, this system is a strategic advantage.

Frequently Asked Questions — What Is Mylar?

Is Mylar the same as polyester?

Yes. Mylar is DuPont’s brand name for biaxially-oriented polyethylene terephthalate (BoPET), which is a type of polyester film. All Mylar is polyester, but not all polyester is Mylar — the same way all Xerox machines are photocopiers but not all photocopiers are Xerox.

Is Mylar food safe?

Yes, FDA-compliant food-grade Mylar meets 21 CFR 177.1630 standards for direct food contact. Always verify your supplier provides food-grade certification with the specific lot you purchase.

What thickness Mylar should I use for food storage?

For long-term food storage (5+ years), use 6–7 mil Mylar bags with oxygen absorbers. For short-term or retail packaging, 4–5 mil provides adequate protection for most dried goods.

Are Mylar bags smell-proof?

Yes, properly sealed Mylar bags (6+ mil) with aluminum foil layers are highly effective at containing odors — making them popular for cannabis, coffee, and strong aromatic products.

Can you microwave Mylar bags?

No. Mylar is not microwave-safe and can melt or release chemicals when heated. Transfer food to microwave-safe containers before heating.

How long does food last in Mylar bags?

With proper sealing and oxygen absorbers, low-moisture foods can last 10–25 years in Mylar bags. Typical shelf life ranges from 5–10 years for most dried goods under proper storage conditions.

What's the difference between Mylar and aluminum foil?

Mylar is a polyester plastic film often laminated with aluminum foil. Pure foil offers better barrier properties but tears easily. Mylar provides strength and flexibility with excellent barrier when foil-laminated — giving you the best of both materials.

Can I print white ink on Mylar?

Most standard inkjet printers cannot print white ink. For white printing on Mylar, use UV printers with white ink capabilities, hybrid systems with a dedicated flexo white unit, or choose pre-printed Mylar stock with white base.

What is the best printer for Mylar bags?

For short to medium runs, the ArrowJet Aqua 800M (digital inkjet) is the top choice for food-safe, high-quality Mylar bag printing. For high-volume production at scale, the ArrowJet Hybrid Pro M combines digital and flexo for the lowest cost per unit.

What inks are safe for food-contact Mylar packaging?

Water-based pigment inks compliant with Swiss Ordinance or FDA standards are the safest for food-contact Mylar packaging. Avoid UV-curable and solvent inks unless a tested barrier lamination is applied between ink and food contact surface.

✓  Thickness Matters:  4–5 mil for retail, 6–7 mil for long-term storage, 8+ mil for maximum protection

✓  Food Safe:  FDA-compliant grades available for direct food contact (21 CFR 177.1630)

✓  Printable:  Digital inkjet works well for short runs; coated Mylar required for ink adhesion

✓  Best Uses:  Food storage, cannabis packaging, electronics protection, chemical containment
