Table of Contents

Top 5 Digital Label Printers of 2026

The top 5 digital label printers of 2026 are: (1) ArrowJet Aqua 330R for overall value, (2) Epson C7500G for photo quality, (3) Primera LX3000 for budget-conscious buyers, (4) Afinia L901 for growing businesses, and (5) TrojanLabel T2-C for enterprise volumes. Each excels in different categories from entry-level desktop units to high-speed production systems.

As label printing changes, digital label printers have become important tools for businesses. They help create high-quality labels quickly and efficiently.

By 2026, digital printing technology will improve a lot. We have found the top 5 digital label printers that are leading the industry. These printers have advanced features, excellent print quality, and flexibility for different uses. They are the best choice for businesses that want to stay ahead of the competition.

In this article, we will review the Top 5 Digital Label Printers of 2026:

  1. ArrowJet Aqua 330R
  2. ArrowJet Hybrid Pro M
  3. ArrowJet Aqua 800M
  4. ArrowJet Nova 250R
  5. ArrowJet VDP

Let’s explore each model in detail. We will highlight the key features, benefits, and possible uses that make them unique in 2026.

Detailed Rankings

#1 ARROWJET AQUA 330R — “Best Overall”

  • Print Speed:  150 fpm (unmatched in water-based inkjet)
  • Max Width:  12.75 inches
  • Technology:  Single-pass Memjet with water-based pigment
  • Why It Wins:  Production speed matches industrial UV systems at half the price, with eco-friendly water-based inks
  • Ideal For:  Print shops, co-packers, manufacturers needing 500+ labels/day
  • 2026 Update:  New Fiery Impress software integration, expanded substrate library

 

#2 EPSON C7500G — “Best for Photo Quality”

  • Print Speed:  30 fpm
  • Max Width:  8.4 inches
  • Technology:  PrecisionCore pigment inkjet
  • Why It Ranks High:  Unmatched color accuracy and image reproduction
  • Ideal For:  Premium cosmetics, wine, gourmet food, photography
  • 2026 Update:  Enhanced white ink option, faster drying times

 

#3 PRIMERA LX3000 — “Best Entry-Level”

  • Print Speed:  15 fpm
  • Max Width:  8 inches
  • Technology:  Dye-based inkjet
  • Why It Ranks:  Lowest cost of entry for professional results
  • Ideal For:  Small businesses, startups, offices under 100 labels/day
  • 2026 Update:  Improved color management software

 

#4 AFINIA L901 — “Best for Growing Businesses”

  • Print Speed:  60 fpm
  • Max Width:  8.5 inches
  • Technology:  Memjet water-based dye
  • Why It Ranks:  Bridges gap between desktop and production
  • Ideal For:  Businesses scaling from hundreds to thousands of labels
  • 2026 Update:  New industrial duty cycle rating

 

#5 TROJANLABEL T2-C — “Best for Enterprise”

  • Print Speed:  200+ fpm
  • Max Width:  13 inches
  • Technology:  UV inkjet
  • Why It Ranks:  Industrial speed and durability
  • Ideal For:  Large manufacturers, high-volume converters

1. ArrowJet Aqua 330R: Revolutionizing Digital Water-Based Inkjet Printing

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R is a digital inkjet printer. It is known for its fast speed and high print quality.

This printer uses Memjet’s DuraFlex technology. It is perfect for businesses that need precise printing with water-based pigment inks. It can produce high-resolution output at speeds of up to 150 feet per minute. This ensures high productivity while keeping print quality high.

Key Features

  • Colors: CMYK, ensuring vibrant and accurate color reproduction.

     

  • Print Speed: Offers two speed options—90 feet per minute or 150 feet per minute, depending on the required print resolution.

     

  • Resolution: The printer works at 90 feet per minute and achieves 1600 x 1600 dpi for clear printing. At 150 feet per minute, it keeps a resolution of 1600 x 954 dpi. This allows for faster output while still providing high quality.

     

  • Max Printing Width: Capable of printing on media up to 12.75 inches wide, allowing flexibility for various label and packaging applications.

     

  • Ink: Uses water-based pigment inks, making it an eco-friendly solution while providing durable, fade-resistant prints.

Applications

The ArrowJet Aqua 330R is perfect for industries like food and beverage, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics where high-quality, vivid labels are essential. Its fast speed and high resolution make it ideal for both short-run and high-volume production environments.

2. ArrowJet Hybrid Pro M: The Ultimate All-in-One Digital with Inline Flexo station

The ArrowJet Hybrid Pro M is a modern hybrid label printer. It uses digital inkjet technology and flexographic finishing. This combination provides great flexibility and efficiency.

This system allows businesses to handle a wide range of printing jobs, integrating both digital and traditional flexographic processes in a single pass. With options for UV and water-based inks, the Hybrid Pro M is built to meet diverse printing needs, delivering high-quality output at high speeds.

Key Features

  • Hybrid Technology: Combines digital inkjet printing with flexographic finishing, offering a complete solution that enhances both productivity and print quality.

  • Colors: CMYK digital inkjet printing, ensuring consistent, vibrant color reproduction.

  • Print Speed: High-speed label production ensures maximum efficiency for both short-run and long-run jobs.

  • Finishing Options: Integrated UV coating, lamination, and die-cutting, streamlining the entire label printing and finishing process in one machine.

  • Substrates: Compatible with a wide variety of substrates, from flexible packaging materials to labels, making it versatile for different industries.

  • Ink: Can use either UV-based or water-based inks, allowing for flexibility depending on the specific application and environmental considerations.

Optional Features

  • Prime and Varnish Flexo Station: Allows for pre-print priming and post-print varnishing, enhancing label durability and appearance.

  • Inline Rotary Slitter or Lamination: Provides in-line slitting or lamination capabilities, enabling seamless finishing without the need for separate machinery.

  • High-Speed Gap and BM Sensor: Ensures accurate print positioning and tracking, maintaining precision even at high speeds.

  • RIP Software: Advanced RIP software for precise color management and workflow automation.

  • Inline NIR Dryer Module: Integrated Near Infrared (NIR) Dryer Module for rapid ink drying, enabling faster production without compromising print quality.

Applications

The ArrowJet Hybrid Pro M is ideal for businesses that demand high customization and flexibility in their printing operations. Whether producing luxury goods packaging, healthcare labels, or industrial labels, this hybrid printer offers a seamless workflow by integrating both printing and finishing in a single system. The optional features make it adaptable to various specific production needs, ensuring reduced production time and enhanced efficiency.

3. ArrowJet Aqua 800M: 25" Wide Web Inkjet Solution for Flexible Packaging

The ArrowJet Aqua 800M is the ultimate solution for wide-format flexible packaging printing, offering unmatched versatility and performance. This printer is designed for companies looking to take their flexible packaging production to the next level with enhanced speed, precision, and efficiency. The Aqua 800M has a maximum print width of over 25 inches. It is ideal for businesses that need large-format printing on different packaging materials.

Key Features

  • Dual Carriage – CMYK Single Printhead with Modular Design: Ensures maximum flexibility and easy maintenance while delivering high-speed printing with vivid color output.

  • MemJet’s DuraFlex® Technology: Offers high-resolution printing with incredible speed, allowing for 1600 x 1600 dpi at full production capacity.

  • Water-Based Pigment Inks: Eco-friendly and durable, the water-based inks ensure long-lasting, fade-resistant prints while being environmentally safe.

  • Maximum Printing Width: Supports media up to 25.39 inches wide, making it ideal for larger packaging formats, providing greater design possibilities.

  • Inline Flexo Stations for Priming and Varnishing: Allows for inline priming and varnishing, ensuring your packaging stands out with a premium finish and enhanced durability.

  • Inline Rotary Slitter: Integrated rotary slitting capabilities, streamlining production by allowing precise cuts and reducing the need for additional equipment.

Applications

The ArrowJet Aqua 800M is perfect for companies working with flexible packaging, food packaging, cosmetic wraps, and industrial labeling. Its wide web printing capabilities make it a great choice for industries that need large formats and high-volume production. It delivers consistent, high-quality results.

4. ArrowJet Nova 250R: Full-Color Label Printer with Inline Laser Cutter

The ArrowJet Nova 250R is a groundbreaking solution that combines full-color digital printing with inline laser cutting, delivering unmatched efficiency for label and sticker production. Featuring the latest advancements in Memjet inkjet technology and laser die-cutting, this system allows businesses to print and cut labels in a single streamlined process.

 

Key Features

  • Full-Color Printing with Memjet Technology: Delivers 1600 x 1600 dpi resolution for vibrant, high-quality prints, ensuring that every label meets professional standards.

  • Inline Laser Die-Cutting: Equipped with a high-power 125W laser, capable of full-cut, half-cut, perforation, marking, and scribing in a single pass. The cutting area spans 8.8″ (225mm) wide, with unlimited length, ensuring flexibility for different label sizes.

  • Print and Cut Functionality: Users can print and cut full-color labels or stickers inline, with the option to use the system as a standalone printer or cutter. The cut to part function is perfect for cut-out stickers.

  • Enhanced Laser Power: Now offering up to 150W laser power, improving cutting speed and precision for more demanding applications.

  • In-Line Slitting and Dual Rewinders: Features in-line slitting and dual rewinders for enhanced finishing options, streamlining the workflow and maximizing productivity.

  • Auto Job Changeover with Barcode Reader: The system’s intuitive software allows for single-click print and cut operation, and can be upgraded with a barcode reader for automatic job switching, enabling efficient, continuous production.

  • Versatile Functionality: The ArrowJet Nova 250R can operate as both a printer and cutter, or separately as a flexible packaging printer or laser cutter, making it adaptable to various production needs.

Applications

The ArrowJet Nova 250R is designed for companies needing high-efficiency label printing and cutting. Its versatility makes it ideal for label converters, in-house production, and packaging solutions. With the ability to handle various cutting modes and auto job changeovers, it’s perfect for producing custom labels, stickers, and even flexible packaging at scale.

5. ArrowJet VDP: The Premier Solution for High-Speed Variable Data & Custom Embellishments

The ArrowJet VDP is the ultimate solution for businesses looking to implement high-speed variable data printing (VDP) with custom embellishments. Built with Kyocera printhead technology, this versatile printer offers flexibility, high performance, and precision for a wide range of variable data applications, including barcodes, QR codes, sequential numbering, and customized text. It seamlessly integrates with traditional presses or can function as a standalone printer, offering unmatched versatility in label production.

Key Features

  • Variable Data Printing: Capable of printing barcodes, QR codes, sequential numbers, and variable text, making it perfect for industries requiring customization at scale.

  • Modular Design: The ArrowJet VDP can be integrated into traditional press setups or used independently, offering cost-effectiveness and operational flexibility.

Advanced Capabilities

  • Spot and Tactile Varnishing: Provides additional customization options, enhancing the appearance and durability of the labels.

  • Cold Foiling: Enables the addition of metallic accents to labels, creating a premium finish.

  • High-Contrast White Ink: Ensures excellent print quality on dark or colored substrates.

  • Security Inks: Offers anti-counterfeiting features, making the ArrowJet VDP ideal for industries such as pharmaceuticals and luxury goods.

Applications

The ArrowJet VDP is a perfect fit for businesses involved in security printing, personalized marketing, and product labeling. Its ability to handle variable data printing at high speeds, along with its advanced embellishment features, allows for the production of eye-catching, customized labels that meet the highest industry standards.

The ArrowJet VDP enhances business capabilities by providing a low-investment, high-productivity solution that reduces plate usage and flexo production costs. With its ability to integrate into traditional presses or act as a standalone unit, it offers businesses the flexibility to meet the growing demands of variable data and customized printing.

Table of Contents

Short-Run Label Printing: What Every Converter Needs to Know in 2026

Short-run label printing refers to producing label quantities from one unit up to approximately 1,000 labels—quantities too small for traditional flexographic printing to be economically viable. Digital label printing technology enables profitable short-run production by eliminating plate costs, setup waste, and minimum order requirements, making it economical to print just the amount needed, when needed.

Short-run label printing has transformed from a money-losing necessity into a profitable niche for converters and a game-changer for brands. Digital technology now makes runs of 50-500 labels economically viable—opening opportunities for seasonal products, prototypes, variable data campaigns, and just-in-time manufacturing. This guide explains why converters are investing in short-run capabilities, the technology required, pricing strategies, and how to calculate ROI for adding short-run services to your business.

Introduction: The Shift to Short-Run Isn’t a Trend—It’s a Transformation

If you’ve been in the label business for any length of time, you’ve seen the signs.

SKUs are multiplying. Consumer preferences are evolving faster than ever. Brands are demanding smaller, more customized print runs. And timelines? They’re getting tighter by the day.

Welcome to 2026—the era of short-run label printing.

What once was considered a niche or specialty service has now become an essential part of a converter’s toolkit. And here’s the real kicker: short-run printing doesn’t compete with traditional flexo or offset setups—it complements them beautifully. It enables converters to serve more clients, fulfill faster turnarounds, reduce waste, and even open new revenue streams through prototyping and regionalized SKUs.

In this blog, we’ll explore:

  • Why short-run label printing is gaining ground in 2026
  • How converters can integrate it into their current operations
  • The growing demand from brands and startups
  • Real-world strategies to shift from prototype to production
  • Why the ArrowJet Bolt is making headlines as the fastest digital label solution on the market

Let’s get started.

What Is Short-Run Label Printing (And Why Now)?

Short-run label printing refers to the production of low-volume print jobs, often with quick turnaround times and high customization. Unlike traditional methods that require long setups and high minimum order quantities, short-run jobs can be produced on-demand with minimal waste.

According to Smithers Pira, the global market for digital print in packaging is expected to hit $31.6 billion by 2026, driven largely by shorter run lengths, SKU proliferation, and demand for personalization. Converters who adapt will not only survive—they’ll thrive.

Short-run printing is ideal for:

  • Prototypes and mock-ups
  • Seasonal or promotional SKUs
  • Product launches and rebrands
  • Regional language or compliance variations
  • Personalized or serialized labels

Why Short-Run Doesn’t Replace Flexo—It Complements It

Flexo is still king when it comes to long runs and standard designs, but in today’s dynamic packaging environment, it has its limitations.

Here’s how short-run digital printing fits into the bigger picture:

  • Fills the gaps between large runs—no more waiting to batch jobs
  • Speeds up prototyping—brands can test designs in-market before scaling
  • Handles last-minute changes with agility
  • Reduces plate and setup costs for smaller batches
  • Supports variable data printing for personalization or traceability

Think of short-run as your agile pressroom assistant, allowing your flexo lines to focus on high-efficiency production, while short-run presses take care of speed, flexibility, and experimentation.

From Prototype to Production: How Brands Are Using Short-Run in 2026

Modern brands are designing, testing, and launching products at unprecedented speeds. With consumer tastes constantly shifting, brands no longer want to commit to 100,000 labels before validating a product in-market.

Instead, they want:

  • 100 labels for a product photoshoot
  • 500 units for a soft launch on a retail shelf
  • 3,000 pieces with variable QR codes for a limited promotion
  • Real-time feedback from customers before scaling

Short-run printing makes all of this possible.

And when it’s time to scale, converters can switch to traditional presses for high-volume production—armed with proof that the product performs.

Why Converters Need to Embrace Short-Run Printing Now

Market Forces:

  • SKU Proliferation:  Brands launching more SKUs in smaller quantities
  • Personalization:  Variable data and regional campaigns require shorter runs
  • Speed-to-Market:  Brands need labels in days, not weeks
  • Sustainability:  Reduce over-print waste and obsolete inventory

 

Business Benefits:

  • New Revenue Stream:  Capture jobs previously rejected
  • Customer Retention:  Be the one-stop shop for all run lengths
  • Higher Margins:  Digital short-run often commands premium pricing
  • Differentiation:  Not every converter offers true short-run capability

Why Converters Are Adding Short-Run

The biggest myth around short-run printing? That it’s only for small converters or niche markets.

In reality, large and mid-sized converters are now actively investing in digital short-run systems to:

  • Expand their client base
  • Offer prototypes and quick-turn samples
  • Serve fast-moving startups and DTC brands
  • Unlock premium pricing for customized, short-quantity labels

A 2024 FINAT Radar Report found that over 60% of European label converters plan to increase their investment in digital printing technologies by 2026, citing flexibility and speed as the top drivers.

The takeaway? Waiting is riskier than evolving.

Technology for Short-Run Printing

What Is a Digital Label Printer?

A digital label printer is a device that produces custom labels directly from digital files without the need for printing plates, screens, or dies. Digital Label Printers for 2026: Trends, Features, and What to Look For

A digital label printer is a press that produces adhesive labels directly from digital files without printing plates, enabling on-demand production from single labels to thousands. Digital label printers use inkjet or toner technology to print variable data, graphics, and barcodes in a single pass—eliminating setup time and minimum order requirements associated with traditional flexographic printing.

Digital label printers have revolutionized packaging by bringing production in-house, reducing lead times from weeks to hours. Unlike traditional printing that requires expensive plates and long setup, digital systems print any quantity instantly—making them ideal for short runs, variable data, and just-in-time manufacturing. This guide explains how digital label printers work, the different technologies available (inkjet vs. toner vs. UV), and what to consider when investing in a system for your business in 2026.

The world of digital label printing is evolving at a remarkable pace, and as we step into 2026, it’s clear that innovation is driving this industry forward. Whether you’re a small business owner, a label converter, or an enterprise in food, beverage, cosmetics, or pharmaceuticals, staying updated on the latest trends and features is essential to staying competitive.

In this blog, we’ll dive into the latest trends in digital label printing, explore the features that businesses are prioritizing, and highlight how digital label printers are reshaping the market.

Why Digital Label Printing Is Booming in 2026

Gone are the days when traditional printing methods could keep up with the demands of modern businesses. The shift to digital label printing is driven by a need for efficiency, flexibility, and sustainability.

Top Drivers Behind the Shift:

  1. Customization Needs: Businesses demand highly personalized labels to cater to niche markets.
  2. Short-Run Production: With a focus on reducing inventory and waste, companies are opting for short-run, on-demand printing solutions.
  3. Eco-Friendly Printing: With increasing awareness about sustainability, water-based and eco-compliant inks are becoming the norm.
  4. Cost-Effectiveness: Digital solutions eliminate the need for plates and setup costs, reducing expenses for short and medium runs.
  5. Rapid Turnaround Times: Brands want their products on shelves faster, making high-speed digital printing a must.

Trending Topics in Digital Label Printing

1. Sustainability and Eco-Friendly Inks

2026 will be the year of green printing solutions. Businesses are choosing printers that use water-based pigment inks compliant with global health standards like Nestlé Guidance or Swiss Ordinance. This trend aligns with brands striving to reduce their carbon footprint while meeting regulatory requirements.

2. Variable Data Printing (VDP)

VDP is making waves in industries like pharma, food, and security printing, where serialization, barcodes, QR codes, and anti-counterfeit solutions are in demand. Digital label printers with VDP capabilities enable businesses to print unique data on every label without slowing down production.

3. Inline Print-and-Cut Solutions

Companies are looking for seamless workflows, and inline printing and cutting systems are simplifying operations. Machines like the ArrowJet Nova 250R combine high-speed printing with precision laser cutting, saving time and resources.

4. High-Resolution Printing

With increasing emphasis on brand aesthetics, 1600 x 1600 dpi resolution is becoming the benchmark for premium label printing. Whether it’s a wine label or cosmetics packaging, businesses want vibrant, detailed prints that capture attention. Our Water based Inkjet Printers deliver 1600 x 1600 dpi with speed up to 150 meters per minute

5. Automation and Smart Features

In 2026, automation isn’t just a perk—it’s a necessity. Features like remote monitoring, predictive maintenance, and AI-based job scheduling are transforming production lines.

Features to Look for in a Digital Label Printer in 2026

If you’re considering investing in a digital label printer, here are the must-have features that align with current trends:

1. Speed and Efficiency

Look for printers capable of handling high-speed production without compromising quality. Machines like the ArrowJet Aqua 330R print at speeds up to 195ft/min, perfect for meeting tight deadlines.

2. Customizability

With brands diversifying product lines, printers must accommodate unlimited customization. Whether it’s printing multiple SKUs or personalized labels, flexibility is a game-changer.

3. Sustainability

Eco-conscious brands prefer printers that support water-based pigment inks, which are safe for food and pharmaceutical applications.

4. Durability and Versatility

Printers with robust build quality and compatibility with materials like paper, film, PET, and Flexible packaging ensure long-term usability.

5. Variable Data and Security Printing

Advanced features like serial number printing, anti-counterfeit measures, and QR code generation are crucial for industries like pharmaceuticals and cosmetics.

6. Cost-Saving Technologies

From eliminating plate costs to reducing material wastage, digital printers must offer a high ROI. The ability to print short runs with no minimum order is highly valued.

7. Ease of Use

Intuitive user interfaces, cloud-based job management, and minimal maintenance requirements ensure that printers are accessible to operators of varying skill levels.

How Digital Label Printers Are Transforming Industries

From food and beverages to pharmaceuticals, digital label printing is reshaping the way businesses operate.

  • Food and Beverage: High-quality, vibrant labels with regulatory compliance are now possible with digital printers.
  • Pharmaceuticals: VDP ensures accurate serialization and tamper-proof labeling for safety and compliance.
  • Cosmetics: Luxury brands leverage digital printing for unique, eye-catching designs that reflect premium quality.
  • Wine and Spirits: High-resolution printing ensures labels stand out on crowded shelves.

2026 Trends in Digital Label Printing

 Top Trends:

  1. Sustainability Focus  Water-based inks replacing UV and solvent systems for eco-friendly packaging
  2. Hybrid Systems  Digital + finishing inline (printing, laminating, die-cutting in one pass)
  3. AI-Powered Color Management  Automated color matching and ICC profile optimization
  4. Cloud-Based Workflow  Remote job submission and print queue management
  5. Food-Safe Inks  FDA-compliant water-based pigments for direct food contact
  6. Wider Print Widths  Standard moving from 8″ to 12-13″ for flexible packaging

What’s Next for Digital Label Printing in 2026?

The industry is heading toward greater automation, enhanced sustainability, and versatile solutions. Expect to see more hybrid printers combining analog and digital technologies, innovations in inline finishing, and advancements in smart printing technologies powered by AI and IoT.

Meet ArrowJet Bolt: Your Printing Powerhouse!

Ready to supercharge your production line? Enter the ArrowJet Bolt – designed for unmatched speed, quality, and reliability. FAQs

Q: What is a digital label printer and how does it work?

A: A digital label printer produces adhesive labels directly from computer files using inkjet or toner technology, eliminating the need for printing plates. It prints graphics, text, and barcodes in a single pass on roll-fed label stock.

Q: What’s the difference between inkjet and laser label printers?

A: Inkjet sprays liquid ink onto media (better for color and photos), while laser uses toner powder fused with heat (better for text and durability). Inkjet offers better substrate flexibility; laser offers lower cost per page.

Q: Can digital label printers handle waterproof labels?

A: Yes. Printers using pigment-based inks (rather than dye-based) produce waterproof, smudge-proof labels suitable for beverages and outdoor use.

Q: What software do I need for digital label printing?

A: Most printers include basic software, but professional RIP (Raster Image Processing) software like Caldera, Wasatch, or the included Fiery Impress provides better color management, variable data handling, and workflow automation.

Q: How long do digital label printer printheads last?

A: Printhead life varies by technology: thermal inkjet lasts 1-3 years; piezoelectric lasts 3-5 years+ with proper maintenance. Cost ranges from $500-2,000 per head replacement.

Q: Can I print foil or special effects with digital label printers?

A: Basic digital printers handle CMYK only. For foil, spot UV, or embossing, you need specialty systems or offline finishing equipment.

Key Takeaways

✓  What it is:  Direct-to-label printing without plates or setup

✓  Best For:  Short runs, variable data, fast turnaround needs

✓  Technologies:  Water-based inkjet (eco), UV inkjet (durable), toner (economy)

✓  2026 Trends:  Sustainability, hybrid finishing, AI color management

✓  ROI Point:  Cost-effective at 500+ labels/month vs outsourcing

Conclusion

As we venture further into 2026, Digital label printers are no longer just tools—they are strategic assets that drive business growth. By keeping up with the latest trends and investing in the right features, businesses can unlock cost savings, operational efficiency, and unmatched flexibility.

Whether you’re upgrading your current setup or exploring digital label printing for the first time, now is the perfect time to embrace the future. Ready to transform your labeling game? Let’s make 2026 your year of success!

How to Print Custom Mylar Bags in 2026 | Full Guide for Brands & Converters

Custom Mylar Bags Market Will Hit $33.2 Billion by 2028 — Here’s How to Win Now.

The demand for custom Mylar bags has exploded. Consumer product brands across food, snacks, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, and cannabis are shifting from rigid packaging to flexible, lightweight, and customizable Mylar pouches. According to industry reports, over 72% of brands say premium printed pouches directly influence customer purchase decisions, and nearly 65% of converters are upgrading their digital presses to accommodate short-run and high-mix Mylar jobs in 2026.

If you’re a brand or converter, mastering custom Mylar bag printing is now a competitive necessity. But Mylar isn’t like paper or BOPP. It requires the right substrates, ink technology, curing system, and finishing workflow for durable, food-safe, and compliant results.

This guide breaks down everything you need to know — including what Mylar is, why it dominates the flexible packaging world, and how to print custom Mylar bags with the ArrowJet Aqua 800M, the leading 2026 digital solution for Mylar and pouch applications.

What Is Mylar?

Mylar is a biaxially-oriented polyester film, technically known as BoPET (Biaxially Oriented Polyethylene Terephthalate). It was originally trademarked by DuPont and has become synonymous with high-barrier, heat-resistant, and durable flexible packaging.

Key Attributes of Mylar Film

Property

Why It Matters

High Barrier Protection

Extends shelf life; resists oxygen, light, and moisture.

Thermal Stability

Great for heat-sealing and stand-up pouch manufacturing.

Strength & Puncture Resistance

Withstands shipping and retail handling.

Lightweight

Reduces logistics costs.

Printable Surface

Compatible with advanced inkjet and digital printing systems.

Why Mylar Is the Standard for 2026 Packaging

As consumer expectations rise and brands shift toward flexible, sustainable solutions, Mylar packaging has quickly become the gold standard for 2026. Its unique combination of durability, barrier protection, printability, and customization makes it the preferred choice for both established brands and fast-growing micro-businesses.

Rising Demand for Sustainable Flexible Packaging

With sustainability becoming a core purchasing factor, Mylar stands out for its lightweight structure, reduced material waste, and recyclability options. Brands benefit from lower shipping costs, smaller carbon footprints, and packaging that supports modern eco-friendly initiatives—all while maintaining exceptional product protection.

Perfect for Small-Batch, High-Customization Markets

Today’s consumers expect personalized, limited-edition, and niche product variations. Mylar bags make this possible thanks to their excellent print compatibility and cost-effective short-run production, especially with digital presses like the ArrowJet series. Whether it’s seasonal SKUs, influencer collaborations, private-label products, or subscription box items, Mylar allows brands to move fast without compromising quality.

Versatile for Nearly Every Product Category

From powders and snacks to supplements, cosmetics, coffee, and liquids, Mylar’s superior barrier properties protect against moisture, oxygen, UV exposure, and contamination. This extends shelf life, keeps products fresh, and maintains brand integrity across diverse industries, F&B, nutraceuticals, beauty, and beyond.

Ideal for E-Commerce and D2C Brands

Direct-to-consumer businesses require packaging that is lightweight, protective, aesthetically premium, and quick to produce. Mylar checks every box. It ships well, holds its shape, and offers a large printable surface for bold branding. With fast digital printing, D2C brands can launch products in days instead of months.

The Packaging of Choice Across Fast-Growing Industries

Because of these advantages, Mylar bags have become the preferred solution for CPG brands, cannabis companies, private-label manufacturers, boutique businesses, and micro-brands. They deliver a powerful combination of:

  • High-end visual impact

  • Low minimum order flexibility

  • Strong barrier protection

  • Quick turnaround for new launches

In 2026 and beyond, Mylar continues to lead because it supports what the modern market demands: speed, sustainability, freshness, and flawless branding.

Premium Shelf Appeal

Consumers buy with their eyes—and Mylar delivers unmatched visual impact.

  • High-resolution graphics, vivid colors, and photorealistic prints elevate product presentation.

  • Metallic finishes, soft-touch laminates, gloss, matte, and holographic effects make products stand out.

  • Mylar’s smooth surface provides a premium feel that resonates with modern branding expectations.

In competitive retail and e-commerce environments, Mylar packaging helps brands differentiate instantly.

Increasing Regulatory Packaging Requirements

Industries such as nutraceuticals, food, beverages, and cannabis now face stricter labeling and packaging compliance than ever before.

Brands need packaging that supports:

  • Clear ingredient lists and dosage information

  • Tamper-evident and child-resistant features

  • Durable, smudge-proof, and food-safe ink systems

  • Compliance with FDA, FSSAI, Health Canada, and state-specific regulations

Custom Mylar bags—combined with pigment-based digital printing—deliver long-lasting, high-clarity labels that withstand moisture, heat, and handling.

How to Print Custom Mylar Bags (Step-by-Step Guide)

Below is the complete professional workflow used by converters and packaging manufacturers producing custom Mylar bags at scale. Whether you’re printing for food, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, or cannabis, this guide covers the essential steps for achieving premium, compliant, and durable Mylar packaging.

Step 1: Choose the Right Mylar Substrate

Selecting the correct Mylar film is the foundation of high-quality pouch production. Each substrate offers unique barrier properties, print characteristics, and sealing performance depending on the product being packaged.

Most Common Mylar Films

  • MET-PET (Metalized Polyester) – Offers the highest barrier against oxygen, moisture, and UV exposure; widely used for snacks, supplements, and long-shelf-life products.

  • PET (Polyester) – Supports clear viewing windows, ideal for premium food and cosmetic packaging where product visibility matters.

  • Multi-Layer Laminates (PET/AL/PE, PET/PET/PE, etc.) – Provide premium protection for sensitive products, combining strength, flexibility, and superior barrier ratings.

What to Look For When Selecting Mylar Films

  • Heat-Seal Compatibility: Ensures airtight, durable pouch sealing.

     

  • Barrier Ratings (MVTR, OTR): Determines shelf life and protection levels.

     

  • Lamination Performance: Critical for multi-layer structures requiring stability and durability.

     

  • Print-Receptive Coatings: Guarantees proper ink adhesion, sharpness, and smudge resistance.

Converters using the ArrowJet Aqua 800M benefit greatly from its ability to run a wide variety of Mylar-based films. Its advanced pigment inkjet chemistry and precise media transport system are engineered specifically to handle the challenges of flexible packaging substrates, ensuring clean edges, accurate ink laydown, and exceptional color consistency.

Step 2: Prepare Artwork for Mylar Printing

Proper artwork preparation ensures accurate color, sharp detail, and correct alignment during pouch forming. Files should be created at high resolution with appropriate bleed allowances and clearly marked seal areas, gussets, zippers, and tear notches.

Because Mylar films can stretch slightly during forming, using the converter’s exact pouch template is essential to maintain design accuracy.

Step 3: Print the Mylar Film

Printing is performed on the flat Mylar web before lamination. Modern digital presses such as the ArrowJet Aqua 800M are engineered to handle PET and MET-PET films with precise ink laydown, high resolution, and consistent color output.

Pigment-based aqueous inks are preferred for Mylar because they provide excellent adhesion, durability, and compatibility with downstream lamination and heat sealing.

Step 4: Laminate the Printed Film

Lamination protects the printed layer and provides the final barrier and mechanical properties required for packaging. Depending on the application, common structures include PET/PE for general use, MET-PET/PE for high-barrier pouches, and PET/AL/PE for long shelf-life products.

Lamination enhances moisture and oxygen resistance, improves puncture strength, and protects graphics from abrasion during filling, transport, and retail handling.

Step 5: Slit and Rewind the Laminated Web

After lamination, the web is slit into precise roll widths suitable for pouch-making equipment. Accurate slitting ensures clean edges, stable rolls, and consistent alignment during conversion, reducing waste and improving seal integrity.

Step 6: Pouch Conversion (Bag Making)

The laminated rolls are then converted into finished Mylar bags using pouch-making machines. This stage includes folding, heat sealing, gusset formation, zipper or valve insertion, and tear-notch creation. Stable laminates and heat-resistant inks are critical at this stage to maintain seal strength and compliance.

Step 7: Finishing and Customization

Optional finishing features enhance branding and functionality. These may include matte or gloss effects, spot varnish, embossing, custom window shapes, QR codes, and variable data such as batch numbers. Digital printing enables these enhancements even in short runs.

Step 8: Quality Control and Compliance

Before shipment, finished Mylar bags undergo quality checks including seal integrity testing, barrier performance verification, durability testing, color consistency checks, and regulatory label verification. This ensures the packaging meets food safety, labeling, and industry standards.

Step 9: Delivery of Finished Mylar Bags

Approved bags are packed and delivered to brands. Many converters now offer on-demand Mylar printing, allowing brands to order smaller quantities with faster turnaround, supporting agile product launches and inventory control.

Why Digital Printing and Mylar Are the Future of Flexible Packaging

Digital printing eliminates plate costs, reduces setup time, and enables rapid production of customized Mylar packaging. It is particularly cost-effective for short to medium runs and supports personalization, variable data, and faster time-to-market.

Why the ArrowJet Aqua 800M Is Ideal for Custom Mylar Bags

The ArrowJet Aqua 800M is purpose-built for wide-web flexible packaging, including PET, MET-PET, and multilayer Mylar films. Its pigment-based ink system is designed for food-safe applications and delivers strong adhesion, resistance to heat and abrasion, and compatibility with lamination and pouch forming.

For converters entering or expanding in the Mylar packaging market, the system offers production-level speeds, low operating costs, and reliable performance across a wide range of pouch formats.

FAQs

What is Mylar made of?
Mylar is made from biaxially oriented polyester film (BoPET), known for its strength, clarity, and high barrier protection.

Can you print directly on Mylar bags?
Yes. Digital pigment inkjet systems designed for PET and MET-PET films can print directly on Mylar before lamination.

Are Mylar bags food-safe?
They are food-safe when printed with compliant inks and laminated using approved materials.

What is the best printer for custom Mylar bags in 2026?
Production-level digital systems like the ArrowJet Aqua 800M are designed specifically for Mylar and flexible packaging applications.

title.rendered: How to Ensure Food-Safe Printing for Pouches & Bags

content.rendered:

How to Ensure Food-Safe Printing for Pouches & Bags (2026 Guide for Brands & Converters)

Food brands today face more pressure than ever. Consumers want clean labels, safe packaging, and complete transparency. Regulators are tightening standards. Retailers expect longer shelf life and higher durability. And through all this, one factor often gets overlooked until it becomes a problem: the safety of your printed packaging.

Whether you’re producing snack pouches, coffee bags, nutraceutical sachets, pet food packaging, or stand-up pouches, ensuring food-safe printing is non-negotiable. The inks, substrates, and finishing steps you choose directly impact compliance, migration levels, shelf stability, and brand reputation.

This guide breaks down everything you need to know about safe printing for food packaging explained in a simple, brand-friendly way.

Why Food-Safe Printing Matters

Imagine spending thousands launching a new product only to face a recall because the ink failed migration testing. Unfortunately, this scenario is more common than you think.

Food packaging printing must meet both regulatory standards and real-world durability demands. If inks migrate through the packaging layer or transfer during heat sealing, they can contaminate the food leading to safety hazards and legal implications.

Food-safe printing ensures:

  • Compliance with global regulations (Swiss Ordinance, FDA, EU 1935/2004, Nestlé guidance, etc.)

  • Shelf-life protection from fading, rub-off, and abrasion

  • Consumer trust through cleaner, safer packaging

  • Stronger retail appeal with high-quality print

  • Sustainability alignment with low-migration, low-VOC inks

Key Regulations You Must Understand

Food safety rules differ by region, but most countries align to three core frameworks:

1. Swiss Ordinance (SR 817.023.21)

The most recognized global benchmark for low-migration inks.
 Brands often ask suppliers, “Are your inks Swiss Ordinance compliant?” because it’s considered a gold standard for food-safe printing.

2. FDA Regulations (Indirect Food Contact)

For the U.S., inks and coatings must comply with FDA guidelines for indirect food contact, meaning they may touch the packaging but not the food itself.

3. EU Framework Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004

In Europe, materials must not transfer substances that:

  • Endanger human health

  • Change food composition

  • Alter the food’s taste or odor

What Makes Printing Truly Food-Safe?

To print safe packaging for pouches and bags, you must control three areas:

1. Use Low-Migration, Food-Safe Inks

Not all inks are created equal. Many conventional inks contain photoinitiators, solvents, or additives that can migrate into food.

Look for inks that are:

  • Pigment-based (better stability during lamination)

  • Low-migration / low-VOC

  • Swiss Ordinance compliant

  • Designed for flexible packaging substrates

  • Compatible with laminations, heat sealing, and retort processes

Example:
 ArrowJet Inks engineered specifically for food-grade flexible packaging offer exceptional rub resistance, chemical stability, and zero-migration performance. These pigment inks are Swiss compliant, making them ideal for Mylar, PET, PE, and multilayer pouch structures.

2. Select the Right Printing Technology

The printing method you choose affects ink adhesion, migration levels, and durability.

Below is a simple breakdown:

Digital Inkjet Printing

Best for: short runs, customization, and fast turnaround.
 Benefits:

  • No plates

     

  • Lower waste

     

  • Ideal for Mylar and multi-layer films

     

  • Perfect for variable data and SKU changes

     

  • Works well with pigment inks

Digital is rapidly becoming the go-to option for 2026 and beyond, especially with advanced presses like the ArrowJet Aqua 800M or ArrowJet Aqua 330R.

Flexographic Printing

Best for: large volumes and consistent long runs.
 Benefits:

  • Cost-effective for high-volume jobs

     

  • Compatible with many food-safe ink sets

     

  • Can run solvent, UV, or water-based inks

Gravure

High-quality but expensive; used mainly for global FMCG brands.

Hybrid (Digital + Flexo)

The fastest-growing trend.
 Converters use:

  • Flexo for white ink, solids, backgrounds

     

  • Digital for versioning, personalization, or quick-change SKUs

This ensures cost savings without sacrificing flexibility.

3. Choose Food-Safe Substrates & Lamination

Even if your ink is food-safe, the substrate must also be compatible.
 Most pouches use combinations like:

  • PET

  • MET-PET

  • PE

  • BOPP

Ensure your print system supports:

  • High ink adhesion

  • Superb lamination bond strength

  • Heat sealing without ink transfer

  • Barrier performance consistency

Modern inkjet systems are designed to print directly on these films with precision drop placement and minimal heat impact critical for thin films.

4. Control Migration Through Proper Lamination

For most food pouches, ink never touches the food it is buried under a laminate layer.
 This requires choosing the right laminates and adhesives.

Ensure that your lamination:

  • Locks in pigment

  • Prevents ink transfer

  • Withstands retort or high-heat sealing

  • Maintains adhesion during shipping and storage

Pigment inks typically perform better than dye inks because they resist heat, water, and abrasion.

5. Test, Test, Test: Quality Control Is Everything

To guarantee food safety, perform these tests regularly:

  • Migration tests (overall + specific)

  • Ink adhesion tests

  • Seal-strength test

  • Rub resistance

  • Drop test / pouch integrity test

  • Heat-resistance test

  • Shelf-life simulation

Modern digital presses like the ArrowJet Aqua 800M are built to pass these tests with consistent results thanks to precision ink laydown and advanced pigment chemistry.

6. Maintain a Clean, Controlled Production Environment

Food-safe printing doesn’t stop at ink selection.

Keep in mind:

  • Use dedicated storage for inks and coatings

  • Avoid contamination during substrate handling

  • Clean printheads, rollers, and laminators regularly

  • Ensure operators follow GMP (Good Manufacturing Practices)

  • Keep clear batch records for traceability

These steps increase compliance and prevent costly recalls.

7. Work With Trusted, Compliant Technology Partners

One of the easiest ways to ensure food-safe printing is to work with manufacturers who already meet strict safety standards.

For example:
The ArrowJet line of aqueous pigment presses is engineered specifically for food packaging with:

  • Swiss Ordinance compliant inks

  • High adhesion on films

  • Strong lamination compatibility

  • Low migration formulation

  • Superb print speed and quality

Systems like the ArrowJet Aqua 800M and 330R are built for converters who want to scale food-grade flexible packaging in 2026 and beyond.

8. Document Everything (For Audits & Retail Compliance)

Brands and retailers increasingly ask for certification proofs.
 Keep documentation for:

  • Ink compliance statements

  • MSDS sheets

  • Migration test results

  • Lot numbers

  • GMP practices

  • Production logs

A well-maintained compliance folder protects your brand and streamlines retailer onboarding.

Final Thoughts: Safe Printing Is Smart Printing

Food-safe printing for pouches and bags isn’t optional; it’s the foundation of responsible packaging. By choosing the right inks, substrates, technology, lamination, and quality controls, brands can deliver packaging that is beautiful, durable, and compliant.

Whether you’re a startup launching your first pouch line or a large converter scaling digital production, investing in food-grade, low-migration printing safeguards your product and your reputation.

Mylar Bags for Long-Term Food Storage: The Complete 2026 Guide for Survivalists, Food Brands & Home Preppers

When it comes to protecting food for 10, 20, or even 30 years, no packaging format is searched, trusted, and recommended as widely as Mylar bags. Whether you’re a homesteader building emergency reserves, a food brand needing shelf-stable packaging, or a survival prepper planning for long-term storage  Mylar remains the gold standard.

In 2026, demand for “Mylar bags long-term food storage” has surged thanks to rising global interest in preparedness, supply-chain uncertainties, and consumer preference for safer, more durable packaging solutions.

This guide explains what Mylar bags are, why they work so well, how to use them correctly, what sizes/thicknesses to choose, and how oxygen absorbers extend shelf life — plus expert tips many blogs miss.

What Are Mylar Bags? (And Why They’re Used for Food Storage)

Mylar is a polyester film (PET) that has been metalized with aluminum to create a barrier material that is:

  • Heat-sealable

  • Lightproof

  • Moisture resistant

  • Oxygen resistant

  • Flexible yet durable

  • Shelf-stable for decades

The combination of PET + Aluminum creates one of the strongest barrier laminates used in food and pharmaceutical packaging.

Why Mylar Is Ideal for 10–30 Year Food Storage

  • Blocks 99.99% of light

  • Prevents oxygen penetration

  • Protects from humidity

  • Limits nutrient loss

  • Prevents mold & spoilage

  • Stops insects and pests (when sealed correctly)

  • Suitable for dry, low-oil foods

This makes Mylar bags the preferred choice for emergency food stockpiling, survival kits, and long-term pantry storage.

Best Foods to Store in Mylar Bags Long-Term

Mylar works best for dry foods with low moisture and low oil content, including:

Foods That Can Last 20–30 Years

  • White rice

  • Wheat berries

  • Rolled oats

  • Dry beans

  • Lentils

  • Pasta

  • Quinoa

  • Barley

  • Freeze-dried fruits & vegetables

Foods That Last 5–10 Years

  • Brown rice (higher oil content)

  • Nuts & seeds

  • Powdered milk

  • Whole wheat flour

  • Dehydrated foods

Foods NOT Recommended

Wet foods
High oil foods
Brown sugar (clumps)
Soft dehydrated fruits (retain moisture)

Choosing the Right Mylar Bag Thickness: 3.5 Mil vs 5 Mil vs 7 Mil

The thicker the bag, the stronger the barrier and long-term durability.

Thickness

Best For

Lifespan

Pros

3.5 Mil

Short-term pantry storage

3–5 years

Cheaper, flexible

5 Mil

Standard long-term storage

10–20 years

Strong, puncture-resistant

7 Mil

Survival food & rough transport

20–30 years

Maximum protection

5 Mil is the most common, while 7 Mil is the premium choice for preppers and emergency food manufacturers.

How Oxygen Absorbers Work (The Secret to 30-Year Shelf Life)

Mylar alone isn’t enough.

To achieve real long-term food storage, combine Mylar bags with oxygen absorbers (OAs) — small packets filled with iron powder that suck oxygen from the sealed environment.

Correct Oxygen Absorber Sizes

Use the following chart for accurate absorption:

Bag Size

Oxygen Absorber Needed

1 Quart

100cc

1 Gallon

300cc–500cc

2 Gallon

1000cc

5 Gallon

2000cc

Always seal immediately after opening the OA packet — exposure reduces effectiveness in minutes.

How to Use Mylar Bags for Long-Term Food Storage (Step-by-Step)

Step 1: Choose the Right Bag

Pick the size and thickness based on the food type and how often you plan to open it.

Step 2: Add Dry Food

Fill the bag with foods that are fully dehydrated and low in oil.

Step 3: Insert Oxygen Absorber

Push the OA into the center of the food for faster activation.

Step 4: Seal the Bag

You can seal with:

  • Heat sealer (best)

  • Clothing iron

  • Hair straightener

  • Impulse sealer

Seal 95% of the top → push out remaining air → seal the last 5%.

Step 5: Store in a Cool, Dark Location

Ideal conditions:

  • 50–70°F (10–21°C)

  • Low humidity

  • Away from sunlight

How Long Can Food Really Last in Mylar Bags?

Here are real-world, expert-backed shelf-life estimates:

Food

Shelf Life in Mylar + O2 Absorber

White rice

30 years

Beans

25+ years

Wheat berries

30+ years

Rolled oats

20–25 years

Pasta

20 years

Lentils

20 years

Powdered milk

10–15 years

Freeze-dried food

30+ years

With proper sealing, many foods last twice as long as in vacuum-sealed bags or rigid containers.

Mylar Bags vs Vacuum Sealing (Which Is Better?)

Feature

Mylar Bags

Vacuum Seal Bags

Oxygen removal

✔ Good

Cost

✔ Yes

Mylar is the only real long-term storage solution.
 Vacuum bags are better for short-term pantry storage or meats in the freezer.

Mistakes to Avoid When Storing Food in Mylar Bags

Using Mylar without oxygen absorbers
Storing high-moisture or oily foods
Not sealing bags fully
Leaving air pockets inside
Reusing oxygen absorbers
Storing bags near rodents or sharp edges

Avoiding these mistakes ensures your food stays safe and maintains nutrition for decades.

What Makes a High-Quality Mylar Bag?

When purchasing Mylar bags in 2026, focus on:

  • Food-safe certification

  • BPA-free materials

  • True aluminum metallization (not cheap plastic)

  • Consistent thickness (5–7 mil)

  • Strong bottom seals

  • Durable gusset options for bulk storage

Premium Mylar bags also provide better odor protection, higher tear strength, and more reliable oxygen barriers.

FAQs

Do Mylar bags need to be stored inside buckets?

Not required—but highly recommended for rodent protection.

Can you reuse Mylar bags?

If cut carefully and re-sealed, yes. But barrier quality weakens over time.

Are Mylar bags safe for food?

Yes — when made from food-grade PET and aluminum.

Do oxygen absorbers make the bags shrink?

A slight tightening is normal and proves the seal is working.

Final Thoughts: The Most Reliable Method for Long-Term Food Storage

If you’re serious about prepping, survival food storage, or emergency readiness, Mylar bags paired with oxygen absorbers remain the #1 industry recommendation.

They offer:

  • 30-year shelf life

  • Superior barrier protection

  • Lightweight, flexible storage

  • Safe, long-lasting preservation

Whether you’re storing 10 lbs of rice or creating long-term emergency kits, Mylar is the most dependable and affordable solution available today.

Arrow Systems, Inc. Announces the Launch of the ArrowJet MTS-48 A Breakthrough in Membrane Switch & Industrial Overlay Printing

Arrow Systems, Inc. is proud to announce the launch of the ArrowJet MTS-48, a next-generation UV LED membrane switch printer engineered specifically for high-precision sub-surface and second-surface printing. Purpose-built for applications such as membrane switches, overlays, nameplates, instrument panels, and industrial user interfaces, the ArrowJet MTS-48 is designed to deliver exceptional adhesion, long-term durability, and superior print clarity for even the most demanding production environments.

Compact yet industrial in performance, the ArrowJet MTS-48 introduces a powerful new standard for OEM manufacturers, converters, and electronics producers looking to elevate the quality, lifetime performance, and reliability of their functional graphic components. The system features 3–6 Ricoh Gen6 printheads, up to 1200 dpi resolution, and production speeds of up to 580 ft²/hr, making it one of the most efficient and precise printers in its category. Its advanced UV LED curing, robust 4-zone vacuum flatbed, and compatibility with large sheet sizes enable seamless handling of polycarbonate, polyester, PC/PET blends, rigid vinyl, acrylic, co-polyesters, and other industry-standard substrates used in industrial interfaces.

A major highlight of the new platform is Arrow’s PolyFlex PC UV LED inkset, engineered specifically for membrane switch and overlay durability. These inks offer strong adhesion on polycarbonate and membrane films, high opacity, chemical and abrasion resistance, and the flexibility required for multi-layer, embossed, and actuating switch structures. The inks are PSA-resistant to prevent lift and smearing—critical for laminated interfaces—and meet GE Lexan® and Valox® PTX specifications, ensuring consistent long-term performance across industrial, automotive, medical, and appliance applications.

Speaking on the launch, Mr. Shaan Patel, Director of Arrow Systems, Inc., shared his excitement about what this new platform means for the global manufacturing community.
 “The ArrowJet MTS-48 represents a major leap forward for converters and OEMs who rely on precision, durability, and reliability in their Membrane switch production,” said Patel. “For years, the industry has been forced to compromise between speed and quality. With the MTS-48, we’ve eliminated that compromise. We wanted to build a system that not only prints beautifully but stands up to real-world environments: automotive dashboards, medical equipment, industrial controls, aviation panels, places where failure is not an option.”

The ArrowJet MTS-48 delivers up to three years of lightfastness, 1500 hours of weathering resistance with minimal change, and print durability validated through rigorous cross-hatch adhesion and environmental testing. These performance metrics make it an ideal choice for mission-critical products that must withstand constant use, UV exposure, and harsh industrial conditions.

Patel further emphasized the company’s long-term vision for the technology:
 “Our goal at Arrow Systems has always been to bridge the gap between innovation and real manufacturing needs. The MTS-48 is more than a printer it’s a production solution that empowers manufacturers to streamline workflows, expand design possibilities, and deliver higher-value products to their customers. We see this technology shaping the next era of membrane switch production globally.”

The new system supports a wide range of applications, including automotive dashboards, HVAC control interfaces, industrial machine panels, medical keypads, consumer electronics user interfaces, fitness equipment controls, and aviation cockpit instruments. Its versatility, combined with industrial-grade performance, positions the ArrowJet MTS-48 as a transformational addition to the membrane switch and overlay printing sector.

With the launch of the ArrowJet MTS-48, Arrow Systems, Inc. continues its commitment to advancing digital print technology through innovation, precision engineering, and customer-driven design.

Weed Mylar Bags: The Complete 2026 Guide (Storage, Safety, Branding & ArrowJet Printing)

Cannabis packaging has transformed rapidly  and weed Mylar bags are now the industry’s #1 choice for flower, edibles, concentrates, and pre-rolls. As brands push for premium shelf appeal, faster turnarounds, and state-compliant packaging, Mylar bags paired with ArrowJet digital printing technology have become the new standard.

This guide covers everything: what weed Mylar bags are, their benefits, types, compliance rules, and why the ArrowJet platform is quickly becoming the preferred solution for custom cannabis pouch printing.

What Are Weed Mylar Bags?

Weed Mylar bags are high-barrier pouches made from PET or MET-PET (metalized polyester) designed to keep cannabis fresh, odor-proof, UV-protected, and shelf-stable.

Why the cannabis market depends on Mylar:

  • Blocks moisture and oxygen

     

  • Locks in aroma (smell-proof)

     

  • Prevents UV degradation

     

  • Offers superior durability

     

  • Customizable for branding + state compliance

Today, over 80% of retail cannabis packaging uses Mylar and the Demand grows yearly.

Benefits of Weed Mylar Bags for Cannabis Brands

1. Maximum Freshness & Terpene Preservation

Mylar has one of the lowest oxygen transmission rates available, keeping cannabinoids and terpenes protected.

2. Smell-Proof Barrier Performance

A critical compliance factor. Mylar prevents terpene-rich aromas from escaping.

3. UV Light Protection

Light exposure breaks down THC. Mylar blocks nearly 100% of UV rays.

4. Highly Customizable for Branding

This is where ArrowJet printers enter the spotlight.
 Brands now print:

  • THC/CBD percentages

  • Batch IDs

  • Compliance icons

Mylar bags have become a marketing billboard for cannabis brands.

5. Child-Resistant Options for Compliance

Lightweight, low-cost, and fast to produce.

Highest demand. Available in matte, gloss, soft-touch, holographic.

Smell Proof Mylar Bags: The Ultimate Guide for Odor-Blocking Packaging in 2026

If you’ve ever opened a package and instantly caught a strong scent—fresh coffee, herbs, spices, or cannabis—you already understand why smell proof Mylar bags are booming across nearly every consumer industry today.

Brands need packaging that locks in aroma, prevents odor leakage, and protects freshness, all while looking sharp on retail shelves. And there’s no material that does it better than Mylar.

In this guide, we’ll break down why smell proof Mylar bags work, how they’re made, who uses them, and how businesses can customize them for maximum shelf appeal and product protection.

What Are Smell Proof Mylar Bags?

Smell proof Mylar bags are specialized barrier pouches made with PET (polyethylene terephthalate) and often layered with aluminum foil. These layers create a near-impenetrable barrier that prevents oxygen, moisture, and odor molecules from escaping.

Think of them as small, flexible vaults—not letting anything in or out unless the user opens the seal.

Why they’re called “smell proof”

Because they use:

  • High-density metalized layers

  • Heat-sealed seams

  • Ultra-tight closures like zip locks or child-resistant zippers

These features trap even the strongest aromas.

Why Smell Proof Mylar Bags Are in High Demand

From 2024–2026, the global demand for smell proof packaging is Projected to grow at over 8.7% CAGR as more brands shift from rigid containers to lightweight, flexible packaging.

The biggest drivers include:

  • Cannabis legalization

     

  • Direct-to-consumer shipments

     

  • E-commerce odor compliance

     

  • Food preservation & freshness control

Mylar’s multi-layer composition gives brands a single solution for long-term freshness + safety + branding.

How Do Smell Proof Mylar Bags Work?

Here’s what makes them so effective:

1. Multi-Layer Barrier Protection

Most smell proof Mylar bags contain:

  • PET outer layer

  • Aluminum foil middle layer

  • PE inner layer

Together, these block:

  • Odor particles

  • Light

  • Humidity

  • Oxygen

  • UV exposure

No smell leaks out—and no air seeps in to degrade the product.

2. Airtight Zippers or Heat Seals

Smell proof packaging uses reinforced closures like:

  • Press-to-close zippers

  • Child-resistant sliders

  • Tamper-evident heat seals

These ensure the bag stays completely sealed until opened.

3. Thick Material (3.5–7 mil)

Thicker film = better odor retention + better strength.

Top Industries That Use Smell Proof Mylar Bags

1. Cannabis & Hemp Packaging

This is the #1 market.
 Smell proof Mylar bags keep:

  • Terpenes locked in

  • Odors discreet

  • Products compliant with regulations

Premade and custom-printed pouches are widely used for:

  • Flower

  • Edibles

  • Concentrates

  • Pre-rolls

2. Coffee & Tea Brands

Aroma is everything.
 Mylar keeps beans fresh by preventing oxidation and retaining essential oils.

3. Spices, Herbs & Seasonings

Mylar prevents:

  • Aroma loss

  • Moisture absorption

  • Flavor fade

Perfect for gourmet and bulk spice packaging.

4. Pet Treats & Supplements

Smell proof packaging prevents strong odors from leaking in transit or retail shelving.

5. Snack Foods & Dehydrated Goods

Brands use Mylar for:

  • Jerky

  • Nuts

  • Freeze-dried foods

  • Trail mixes

The tight seal keeps products crunchy and fresh.

Benefits of Smell Proof Mylar Bags for Brands

1. Absolute Odor Control

Perfect for applications where aroma must be preserved or hidden.

2. Long Shelf Life

Mylar extends product life by blocking oxygen and moisture—two major causes of spoilage.

3. Lightweight & Cost Efficient

Compared to jars or tins, Mylar bags:

  • Reduce shipping costs

  • Take up less warehouse space

  • Lower material expenses

4. Fully Customizable

Brands can design:

    • Gloss, matte, or metallic finishes

       

    • Child-resistant closures

       

    • Stand-up or flat pouches

       

    • Resealable or single-use bags

5. Eco-Friendly Options Available

Newer Mylar structures use:

  • Recyclable layers

     

  • Reduced plastic content

     

  • Water-based inks

Custom Printed Smell Proof Mylar Bags (Branding Advantage)

In 2026, custom-printed pouches have become a top retail differentiator.

Premium digital presses like the ArrowJet line enable:

  • Vivid color reproduction

  • Edge-to-edge graphics

  • Quick turnaround

  • Zero plate costs

  • SKU flexibility

This allows brands to create:

  • Limited editions

  • Seasonal designs

  • Variant-specific packaging

Perfect for cannabis strains, coffee origins, and gourmet blends.

Are Smell Proof Mylar Bags Safe for Food?

Yes—high-quality Mylar bags are:

  • Food-grade

  • BPA-free

  • FDA compliant

  • Safe for direct or indirect food contact

As long as they’re purchased from certified suppliers, they meet safety standards for edible products.

How to Choose the Best Smell Proof Mylar Bags

When sourcing Mylar bags, consider the following:

1. Thickness

3.5 mil – general retail
 5 mil – cannabis, coffee
 7 mil – long-term storage

2. Layer Composition

Look for PET + ALU + PE for maximum odor control.

3. Closure Type

Standard zipper
 Child-resistant zipper
 Heat-seal

4. Size

From 1g to full pound sizes depending on application.

5. Printing Options

Digital printing for small runs
 Flexo for large volumes
 Hybrid printing for best of both worlds

Why Smell Proof Mylar Bags Are the Future of Packaging

As brands expand into e-commerce and compliance becomes stricter, demand will continue rising.

These bags provide:

  • Maximum freshness

  • Superior odor-blocking

  • Strong branding potential

  • Cost-effective packaging

Whether you’re packaging herbs, superfoods, snacks, or cannabis, smell proof Mylar bags offer unmatched protection and presentation.

Final Thoughts

Smell proof Mylar bags aren’t just trendy—they’re now essential for businesses wanting safe, compliant, and premium-quality packaging that protects both aroma and brand reputation.

Mylar Bags for Freeze Drying: The Ultimate Guide for Long-Term Food Storage

Freeze drying has exploded in popularity both among homesteaders and commercial food businesses looking to extend shelf life without compromising nutrition. But freeze-dried food is only as good as the packaging that protects it.

Enter Mylar bags: the gold standard for long-term food preservation.

If you’re trying to decide whether Mylar is right for your freeze-drying workflow or you want to understand which Mylar bags offer the best protection, this guide breaks down everything you need to know.

What Are Mylar Bags and Why Are They Used for Freeze Drying?

Mylar is a brand name for biaxially-oriented PET (BoPET) film an ultra-strong, lightweight, and barrier-rich material engineered to block oxygen, moisture, UV light, and odors.

For freeze-dried foods, this is crucial.

Once moisture is removed, the biggest threat to food shelf life is oxygen and light exposure, both of which can degrade nutrients, color, flavor, and texture.

Why Mylar Is the Best Choice for Freeze-Dried Food Storage

Superior oxygen barrier
Moisture-proof and vapor-tight
Light and UV resistant
Durable and puncture-resistant
Works with oxygen absorbers
Safe for food contact

Mylar doesn’t just preserve food, it extends shelf life to 10–30+ years when used correctly.

How Freeze Drying Works And Where Mylar Fits In

Freeze drying removes water from food using a process called sublimation, where ice turns directly into vapor.

The steps look like this:

  1. Food is frozen.

     

  2. A vacuum pulls out moisture.

     

  3. The remaining product is shelf-stable—but extremely sensitive to air.

This is where Mylar bags shine.

Freeze-dried foods absorb moisture quickly. Even brief exposure can ruin a batch. Mylar bags act as a moisture-blocking vault, locking oxygen absorbers inside and keeping food safe for decades.

Best Mylar Bag Thickness for Freeze-Drying

Choosing the right thickness is key for long-term storage.

Thickness

Best For

Pros

Cons

3.5 mil

Short-term storage, snacks

Lightweight, inexpensive

Not ideal for long-term pantry storage

5 mil

Most home users

Great balance of cost + durability

May puncture with sharp foods

7–8 mil

Long-term storage (10–30 years)

Maximum protection, premium quality

Higher cost but worth it

>10 mil (industrial)

Bulk or commercial use

Extreme durability

Harder to heat seal

Most freeze dry enthusiasts prefer 5–7 mil Mylar bags for everyday use.

Choosing the Right Sizes for Freeze-Dried Food

Mylar bags come in multiple sizes—useful depending on the storage goal:

  • 1-quart bags → fruits, snacks, single meals

  • 1-gallon bags → bulk grains, rice, pasta, vegetables

  • 2-gallon bags → larger family-size portions

  • Stand-up pouches → retail-ready freeze-dried products

  • Ziplock Mylar → resealable, best for short-term pantry use

Pro tip: For true long-term storage, always heat seal zip-top Mylar after final packaging.

Do You Need Oxygen Absorbers?

Freeze-dried food must be paired with Oxygen absorbers (OAs) to prevent spoilage.

Recommended oxygen absorber sizes:

  • 300cc for quart Mylar bags

     

  • 500cc–800cc for 1-gallon bags

     

  • 2000cc for 2-gallon bags

Why OAs are essential:

  • Prevent oxidation

     

  • Stop microbial growth

     

  • Preserve fats from going rancid

     

  • Keep food fresh long-term

Remember: Oxygen absorbers start working immediately once exposed to air. Keep them sealed until the moment you pack.

How to Package Freeze-Dried Food in Mylar Bags (Step-by-Step)

1. Start with fully freeze-dried food

Any remaining moisture invites mold or spoilage.

2. Fill the Mylar bag

Leave a few inches of space at the top.

3. Add oxygen absorbers

Place them directly on the food don’t open more than you can use in 10 minutes.

4. Heat seal the bag

Use an impulse sealer, flat iron, or heat sealer.

5. Label everything

Include:

  • Food name

  • Date of storage

  • Weight or batch ID

6. Store in a cool, dark, dry place

Ideal storage temperature: 60–70°F (15–21°C).

Shelf Life: How Long Do Freeze-Dried Foods Last in Mylar Bags?

With proper sealing and storage:

  • Low-fat foods (vegetables, fruits, grains): 20–30+ years

  • Moderate-fat foods (meat, dairy): 10–15 years

  • High-fat foods (nuts, avocado, oils): 2–5 years

Mylar does not protect against fat oxidation, which is why higher-fat foods naturally have shorter shelf lives.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Even the best bag won’t save you from bad packaging practices.

Mistake: Leaving air gaps in the bag

Always heat seal completely.

Mistake: Not using enough oxygen absorbers

Under-packing OAs leads to partial protection.

Mistake: Using low-quality Mylar

Cheap bags often have weak seams or poor barrier layers.

Mistake: Storing bags in hot areas

Heat accelerates food degradation.

Mylar Bags vs Vacuum Sealing for Freeze-Dried Food

Feature

Mylar Bags

⭐⭐

Best for

Long-term storage

Winner for freeze-dried food: Mylar, every time.

Who Uses Mylar Bags for Freeze Drying?

Home Freeze Dryers

Families preserving:

  • Fruits

  • Vegetables

  • Full meals

  • Emergency food kits

Commercial Freeze-Dry Brands

For:

  • Packaged snacks

  • Freeze-dried candies

  • Camping meals

  • Premium pet treats

Preparedness & Survival Stores

Long-term kits
 Bulk freeze-dried staples
 Disaster preparedness foods

Final Thoughts: Are Mylar Bags Worth It for Freeze-Drying?

Absolutely.

If your goal is decades-long shelf life, food safety, and nutrient retention, Mylar is simply unmatched. When combined with oxygen absorbers and proper sealing, Mylar bags protect freeze-dried food from the three biggest enemies:

  • Oxygen

  • Moisture

  • Light

Whether you’re prepping for emergencies, building a food business, or stocking your home pantry, Mylar bags are the most reliable, cost-effective packaging solution for freeze-dried foods.
