Mylar Bags for Hydrated Food: The Complete Guide for 2026 Storage & Packaging

If you’re storing hydrated meals, ready-to-eat foods, emergency rations, camping meals, or gourmet wet ingredients, you’ve probably noticed one challenge:

How do you keep moisture-rich food fresh, safe, and shelf-stable without sacrificing flavor or texture?

Enter Mylar bags, the gold standard in modern food packaging.

Traditionally known for long-term dry food storage, Mylar is now becoming the #1 choice for packaging hydrated and semi-moist foods thanks to advancements in barrier films, heat sealing technology, and food-safe digital printing.

This guide breaks down everything you need to know about benefits, shelf life, safety, sealing tips, and the best Mylar materials for moisture-rich foods.

What Are Mylar Bags?

Mylar is a brand name for BoPET (Biaxially Oriented Polyethylene Terephthalate) a strong, flexible, heat-resistant film.

When converted into pouches, it offers:

  • Extreme oxygen barrier

  • Excellent moisture resistance

  • Light protection

  • Chemical stability

  • High heat-seal strength

This combination makes it ideal not only for dry beans and rice
but also for hydrated, partially hydrated, and semi-moist foods.

Can You Store Hydrated Food in Mylar Bags?

Yes—if you use the right grade and follow proper sealing practices.

Modern food companies and meal-prep brands widely use Mylar bags for:

Hydrated & Ready-to-Eat Foods

  • Soups

  • Curries

  • Chili

  • Rice bowls

  • Pasta dishes

Semi-Moist & High-Aw Moisture Items

  • Beef jerky (moist varieties)

  • Cooked vegetables

  • Hydrated fruit slices

  • Prepared grains

  • Meal kits

Hydration-Preserved Foods

  • Rehydrated freeze-dried meals

  • Protein-rich hydrated foods

  • Gourmet meal blends

  • Infant food refills (non-shelf-stable, refrigerated)

Important Note on Hydrated Food Safety

Hydrated food has high water activity (Aw), which supports microbial growth.
 This means:

Mylar alone does NOT make hydrated food shelf-stable.

You must pair the pouch with one of the following:

  • Retort processing

  • Pasteurization or sterilization

  • Refrigerated distribution

  • Frozen storage

For shelf-stable hydrated meals (like army MREs), manufacturers use:

Retort Mylar Bags (PET/Aluminum/CPP multilayer films)

These can withstand 121°C (250°F) sterilization and create a commercial vacuum seal.

Why Mylar Bags Are Ideal for Hydrated & Semi-Moist Foods

1. Superior Oxygen Barrier

Oxygen exposure is one of the fastest ways hydrated foods spoil or change flavor.

Premium Mylar films offer:

  • OTR as low as 0.0003 cc/m²/day

  • Odor and aroma retention

  • Oxidation protection for fats, oils, and meats

This keeps hydrated meals tasting fresher, longer.

2. Moisture Retention (No Drying Out)

Unlike basic plastic pouches, Mylar:

  • Prevents water from evaporating

  • Maintains food texture and tenderness

  • Preserves sauces, juiciness & moisture balance

Perfect for meals like biryani, pasta, curries, and cooked vegetables.

3. Light Protection for Nutrient Stability

UV exposure breaks down:

  • Vitamins

  • Proteins

  • Natural colors

  • Healthy fats

Aluminum-layered Mylar offers full light-blocking, ideal for sensitive hydrated meals.

4. Heat-Seal Strength for Liquid Foods

Hydrated food packaging must withstand:

  • Pressure

  • Temperature changes

  • Handling during shipping

Mylar’s high tensile strength + strong heat seals prevent leaks and tears.

5. Custom Printing for Premium Food Brands

Digital printing on Mylar bags allows:

  • Waterproof pigment ink graphics

  • Food-safe printing (FDA-friendly & Swiss compliant inks like ArrowJet Inks)

  • Matte, glossy, or metalized finishes

  • Short-run or large-scale production

Brands selling prepared meals, ready-to-eat pouches, keto meals, protein meals, etc. can now print:

  • Nutrition labels

  • High-quality product images

  • QR codes

  • Batch & expiry data

  • Brand storytelling

Types of Mylar Bags for Hydrated Foods

1. Standard PET/PE Mylar Pouches

For semi-moist foods requiring refrigeration or freezing.

Best for:
Prepped meals
Hydrated fruits & vegetables
Gourmet food kits

2. Retort Mylar Bags (for Shelf-Stable Hydrated Meals)

Multi-layer films such as:

PET / ALU / Nylon / CPP

These are built for thermal sterilization and are used in:

  • MREs

     

  • RTE curries

     

  • Saucy pasta meals

     

  • Rice bowls

     

  • Ready-to-eat Asian meals

Benefits:

  • Survives 121°C retort sterilization

     

  • Creates hermetic, shelf-stable packaging

     

  • Multi-year storage life

3. High-Barrier Mylar Stand-Up Pouches

For premium presentation on shelves.

Ideal for:

  • Gourmet wet foods

  • Marinated vegetables

  • Refrigerated ready meals

  • Meal-prep businesses

How Long Can Hydrated Food Last in Mylar Bags?

Food Type

Mylar Type

Storage Condition

Shelf Life

Hydrated vegetables

PET/PE

Refrigerated

3–7 days

Hydrated fruits

PET/PE

Refrigerated

5–10 days

Saucy meals

Retort

Ambient

12–36 months

Meat-based meals

Retort

Ambient

12–24 months

Prepared grains

Retort

Ambient

8–18 months

Hydrated freeze-dried meals

Standard Mylar

Ambient

12–24 months

Shelf life varies by formulation, pH, Aw, sterilization, and packaging seal quality.

How to Seal Hydrated Food in Mylar Bags (Correct Process)

Step 1: Choose the right Mylar grade

 

  • Retort grade for shelf-stable meals

     

  • Standard grade for refrigerated / frozen foods

Step 2: Fill the pouch carefully

 

Leave 1–1.5 inches of headspace.

Step 3: Remove air

 

  • Vacuum sealing is ideal

     

  • Nitrogen flushing for large food batches

Step 4: Heat-seal properly

 

Seal temperature range: 350°F–400°F (177–204°C)
 Use:

  • Impulse sealers

     

  • Band sealers

     

  • Hot-bar sealers

Step 5: Test the pouch

 

Check for:

  • Seal strength

     

  • Leakage

     

  • Delamination

     

  • Pressure resistance

Best Practices for Branding Hydrated Food Mylar Bags

Use food-safe digital inks

Pigment-based, compliant inks (e.g., ArrowJet Inks) prevent:

  • Smudging

  • Leaching

  • Color fading during heat processes

Add reclosable zippers if portioned

For meal-prep or baby food products.

Opt for clear windows only if product is light-stable

Add QR or NFC for premium experience

Brands use it for:

  • Recipes

  • Heating instructions

  • Nutrition analysis

Why Mylar Is the Future of Hydrated Food Packaging

With the rise of:

  • Meal-prep businesses

  • RTE (ready-to-eat) convenience foods

  • Camping and survival meals

  • Gourmet globally-inspired meal kits

  • Pet food hydration packs

…the industry needs packaging that is:

  • Safe

  • Hygienic

  • Durable

  • Printable

  • High-barrier

Mylar checks all the boxes and continues to evolve with digital printing and advanced film structures.

Conclusion

Mylar bags are one of the most reliable, versatile, and safe packaging options for hydrated, semi-moist, and RTE foods. Whether you’re a food brand, manufacturer, meal-prep company, or survival meal producer, Mylar offers unmatched:

  • Barrier protection

  • Shelf stability

  • Custom branding

  • Safety

  • Convenience

Pair the right Mylar grade with proper thermal processing, and you can achieve commercial shelf stability and premium product presentation that customers trust.

This milestone is especially meaningful as it showcases how modern digital printing technology, specifically the ArrowJet Aqua 330R from Arrow Systems, Inc., has helped elevate local manufacturing standards to world-class levels.

At the awards ceremony in Georgetown, the atmosphere was filled with celebration as leaders from across industries gathered to recognize top-performing organizations. Among them was Mr. Sheik Rowling Khan, Founder and CEO of Lansen Label, who stepped forward to receive the trophy with visible pride. Reflecting on the achievement, Mr. Khan shared that this recognition is more than just an award, it is a validation of the hard work, discipline, and passion that his team brings to the label manufacturing sector every day.

“This award is a testament to the dedication and discipline of our entire team,” he said. “Safety and quality are the pillars of Lansen Label, and the ArrowJet Aqua 330R has been instrumental in helping us deliver world-class results with uncompromised consistency. Using ArrowJet technology has elevated not just our output but also the confidence our customers have in our processes. We are proud to bring advanced digital printing standards to Guyana.”

For Lansen Label, the transition to advanced digital production with the ArrowJet Aqua 330R marked a turning point. The Printer’s high-resolution, pigment-based, food-safe printing capabilities allowed the company to deliver cleaner, safer, and more consistent labels. This improvement in production reliability directly strengthened their occupational health and safety practices, one of the core evaluation criteria of the National Quality Awards. With more efficient workflows and reduced manual handling, the company could ensure a safer manufacturing environment while simultaneously raising the standard of print quality for its customers.

Mr. Shaan Patel, Founder and CEO of Arrow Systems, Inc., celebrated the news with enthusiasm, acknowledging the strong partnership between the two companies. “We are extremely proud of Lansen Label and this incredible milestone,” he said. “Their commitment to quality, safety, and innovation aligns perfectly with what the ArrowJet Aqua 330R was designed for. Seeing the technology empower businesses like Lansen Label in emerging markets reinforces our mission to make world-class digital printing accessible globally. We look forward to supporting their growth and leadership in Guyana and the Caribbean region.”

Beyond the award, Lansen Label continues to embrace an ambitious vision: to transform Guyana into a regional hub for high-quality label and flexible packaging production. Mr. Khan has repeatedly emphasized his goal of enabling local and regional brands to access premium, globally competitive packaging without the long lead times or high costs typically associated with importing. The company aims to support SMEs, empower manufacturers, and strengthen the region’s packaging ecosystem through innovation, efficiency, and safety-driven practices.

The National Quality Award stands not just as a symbol of recognition, but as a testament to what is possible when vision, technology, and commitment come together. Lansen Label’ success demonstrates that world-class manufacturing can be built right here in Guyana and this achievement is only the beginning of their journey toward regional and global influence.

Both partners believe that Poland will become one of Europe’s strongest digital printing hubs. In the coming months, Arrow Systems and Wolff Poligrafia will roll out an ambitious joint roadmap that includes nationwide demonstrations, technical workshops, live production showcases, and on-site integration programs to help converters transition smoothly into digital.

Krzysztof Wolff adds: “With the Arrow Systems portfolio of machines we’re not just supplying equipment but also possibilities for obtaining new sales opportunities, new markets and what is equally important, together with savings.

With Arrow’s technology, Wolff Poligrafia’s market strength, and Poland’s rapidly modernizing packaging sector, this partnership stands to redefine digital label and pouch printing across the region. In an engaging conversation, Mr. Shaan Patel, Director at Arrow Systems, Inc., and Mr. Spyros Lavranos, Head Business Executive at BUSINESSWARE, shared their insights on why this partnership matters and how it will reshape the region’s print landscape. 

“One of the core strengths of this collaboration is the depth of expertise BUSINESSWARE brings to the table” , Said Mr. Shaan Patel said, “BUSINESSWARE brings more than fifteen years of experience in Memjet technology and digital printing, along with strong expertise in materials and application workflows, providing a solid technical foundation for supporting converters across Greece and Cyprus.”

This long-standing technical competence makes BUSINESSWARE the ideal partner to introduce ArrowJet’s advanced solutions to the region.

Mr. Spyros Lavranos highlighted, “The markets in Greece and Cyprus show increasing demand for cost-efficient production, regulatory-compliant materials and stable digital workflows, making ArrowJet’s water-based pigment technology a strong fit for current and emerging converter needs.”

The evolving dynamics of the market, noting how converters in Greece and Cyprus are increasingly shifting to short-run, on-demand, customized production. According to recent industry data, digital label printing volume in Southern Europe has grown by over 15% annually, fueled by SME expansion, private-label growth, and rising consumer expectations around brand differentiation. Mr. Shaan added.

Shaan emphasized, Our Arrow Systems’ flagship technologies including the ArrowJet Hybrid Series and the ArrowJet 800M wide-web digital press are built precisely to support this transition.

Spyros provided an on-ground perspective, calling this partnership “timely and necessary,” especially as local converters demand faster output, safer materials, and more efficient workflows. 

He emphasized that regulatory pressure for safer packaging is rising rapidly. With food and beverage products accounting for more than half of the region’s label production, Swiss-compliant water-based pigment inks have become essential rather than optional. Spyros underscored how ArrowJet technology aligns with this shift, offering unmatched print safety without compromising sharpness, durability, or speed.

The conversation also highlighted the strengths of Arrow Systems’ hardware lineup, starting with the ArrowJet Hybrid Series, which integrates inline priming and varnishes a major advantage for converters seeking streamlined production. Shaan noted how this feature removes multiple manual steps from the workflow, reduces waste, and creates consistency across long and short runs alike. 

Spyros agreed, adding that such automation is exactly what converters in Greece and Cyprus need, especially since many operate in compact facilities with high-pressure production schedules.

Both leaders also spoke about the transformative potential of the ArrowJet 800M, a 25-inch wide-web pigment inkjet system designed for industrial-scale flexible packaging and specialty print applications. Spyros highlighted how this single platform opens doors to entirely new revenue opportunities, allowing converters to expand into pouches, sachets, and large-format packaging markets previously limited by equipment constraints. The ability to print wide, fast, and with water-based pigment technology places the ArrowJet 800M in a category of its own for converters looking to scale profitably.

Shaan emphasized that this partnership is not just about introducing new equipment it’s about creating a future-ready ecosystem. With rising demand for variable data printing, personalization, and fast turnaround times, converters need tools that deliver both agility and compliance. ArrowJet systems offer high-resolution output, durable pigment-based performance, and a workflow designed for modern market demands. 

During our discussions, it became clear that Arrow Systems is not simply a machine manufacturer but a company deeply focused on materials, coatings and overall cost reduction for converters, offering a complete ecosystem rather than a single piece of equipment.

BUSINESSWARE also operates a dedicated Service and Support Center in Cyprus, ensuring converters across the region receive fast, reliable technical assistance and ongoing operational guidance.

“With Arrow Systems, we are not just expanding our product portfolio. We are expanding what’s possible for converters in our region. These technologies will help businesses innovate, compete, and grow.”

In closing, Mr. Spyros expressed his enthusiasm for what lies ahead, “With Arrow Systems, we are not just expanding our product portfolio, we are expanding what’s possible for converters in our region. These technologies will help businesses innovate, compete, and grow.”

Mr. Shaan Patel echoed this optimism, “This partnership marks the beginning of a new era for digital printing in Greece and Cyprus. We are committed to empowering converters with the tools they need to thrive.”

Together, Arrow Systems and Businessware aim to equip converters in Greece and Cyprus to operate at global production standards while unlocking stronger margins and diversified revenue streams. As part of the collaboration, the two companies plan to organize technical presentations and informational sessions to introduce the ArrowJet platform and its capabilities to the local market.

As this collaboration takes shape, both companies are confident that converters in Greece and Cyprus will experience a new benchmark in speed, safety, quality, and performance. This distribution partnership stands as a bold step forward in bringing advanced digital printing technology to two rapidly growing markets setting the stage for long-term innovation and sustainable business growth.

Sid Sistemas de Impresión in Spain Installs ArrowJet Aqua 330R and DPR Taurus to Bolster Label Production

Arrow Systems, Inc., in collaboration with its authorized Spanish dealer Katun Corporation, is proud to announce the installation of the ArrowJet 330R high-resolution digital label press and DPR Taurus Laser Finisher at Sid Sistemas de Impresión Diseño gráfico y web, located in Calamocha and Calatayud, Spain.

This milestone represents a new era of digital production for Sid Sistemas, empowering the company with next-generation print technology built for precision, compliance, and scalable growth in high-demand industries.

At the heart of this installation is the ArrowJet 330R’s advanced water-based pigment inkjet engine, capable of delivering a true 1600 × 1600 dpi resolution. Powered by Swiss-compliant, food-safe inks, the system enables Sid Sistemas to confidently serve food, pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetics brands markets that increasingly demand regulatory clarity, migration-safe inks, and traceable supply chains.

With global studies showing that over 68% of food and pharmaceutical brands now prioritize compliant digital packaging and 41% are switching to water-based technologies to reduce chemical risk, the ArrowJet platform positions Sid Sistemas at the forefront of safety-driven label production.

The press’s high durability pigment formulation also ensures resistance to moisture, chemicals, and UV exposure critical for premium consumer labels that must look flawless from warehouse to shelf.

Speaking on the installation, Mr. Shaan Patel, Director at Arrow Systems, Inc., shared, “This is more than an equipment placement. It’s a long-term investment into the future of safe, high-resolution, environmentally responsible label production. Sid Sistemas now has the power to deliver full-color, 1600 dpi output using water-based pigment inks that meet Swiss Ordinance standards. It opens the door to food, pharma, and specialty markets where print precision and compliance are non-negotiable. We are excited to support their vision and proud to partner with Katun Corporation in expanding cutting-edge solutions across Spain.”

For Mr. Santiago, Director at Sid Sistemas de Impresión, the choice was clear after evaluating the rapidly shifting needs of the market. “We knew we needed technology that wasn’t just modern, but future-proof,” he explained. “The ArrowJet 330R impressed us immediately with color accuracy, the crispness of the short run output, and the security of water-based, food-safe inks aligned perfectly with our direction. We serve clients in food packaging, cosmetics, beverages, nutraceuticals, and we are seeing demand rise sharply. With the ArrowJet and Taurus solution, we can cut lead times, improve consistency, and open new revenue streams with small-batch, high-mix, fast-turnaround jobs. This installation is the beginning of a bigger transformation for our business.”

With the Spanish label market growing at an estimated 6.5% annually, and consumer categories like nutraceuticals and premium cosmetics rising even faster 9.2% and 7.8% respectively. Sid Sistemas now has the technology to capitalize on some of Europe’s fastest-expanding segments.

The integrated Taurus laser finisher further streamlines production with precision die-cutting, allowing Sid Sistemas to offer both short-run and mid-volume jobs without the delays or tooling costs of traditional finishing workflows.

Representing the regional partnership, the Sales Manager of Katun Corporation added, “Our commitment has always been to deliver world-class solutions that help elevate our customers’ capabilities. The collaboration with Arrow Systems on this project reinforces that mission. With ArrowJet’s compliant pigment inks and unmatched print clarity, Sid Sistemas is now positioned to serve regulated sectors with complete confidence. We are honored to support this upgrade and excited for what it means for the Spanish label market.”

One of the decisive factors behind Sid Sistemas’ investment was Arrow Systems’ renowned 24×7 global support model, providing continuous access to expert technicians, remote diagnostics, color management assistance, and rapid-response service. This ensures maximum uptime essential for businesses handling mission-critical production for food, pharmaceutical, and medical clients.

As Mr. Patel emphasized: “Technology is only as good as the support behind it. Our 24×7 service commitment ensures Sid Sistemas can run confidently, day and night. We don’t just install machines we build long-term partnerships.”

This installation marks a powerful step forward for Sid Sistemas de Impresión as the company expands into high-value markets such as food packaging, pharmaceuticals, nutraceuticals, beverages, personal care, and cosmetics. With the ArrowJet platform, the business is now well-equipped to deliver premium-quality, regulatory-compliant labels while opening profitable new revenue streams driven by fast turnaround, high-resolution output, and zero-compromise safety.

As Arrow Systems’ authorized dealer in Spain, Katun plays a key role in supporting digital transformation for label and packaging converters.

With facilities in Calamocha and Calatayud, the company is committed to delivering fast, premium, and innovative solutions to brands across multiple sectors. Step Inside Innovation: Arrow Systems New Experience Center Opens in Ontario, Canada.

If there’s one thing the printing industry thrives on, it’s innovation and Arrow Systems, Inc. has just taken that spirit to a whole new level. The company has officially opened its state-of-the-art Experience Center in Burlington, Ontario (5100 S Service Rd #15, Burlington, ON L7L 6A5, Canada), inviting brands, converters, and creative professionals to explore the next generation of digital label and packaging technology.

Walking into the new space feels like stepping into the future of Label printing. Here, every piece of technology is designed to empower converters and brands to push boundaries, improve productivity, and achieve unmatched color accuracy and consistency.

“We wanted to create a space where technology meets creativity,” says Mr. Shaan Patel, Director of Arrow Systems, Inc. “Our goal was to give customers an environment where they can see real-world applications, test materials, and truly understand the challenges and how our digital printing solution can transform their business.”

Across the industry, converters are struggling with shorter production runs, higher material costs, and rising customer expectations. Brands are demanding faster prototyping, sustainable materials, and vibrant, durable prints, all while keeping costs in check. Traditional printing workflows often mean switching between multiple machines, dealing with long setup times, and managing unpredictable color results.

“We’ve seen how converters are pushed to deliver more variety in less time,” explains Mr. Shaan Patel,“Our water-based pigment ink systems help them stay ahead with Swiss-compliant formulations, vibrant output, and color consistency that holds true run after run. ”

At the heart of this Experience Center is Arrow’s renowned water-based pigment ink technology, engineered for both performance and responsibility. These Swiss-compliant inks offer vibrant, durable output with precise color consistency with a combination that’s increasingly important for industries like food, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics. With print resolutions up to 1600 x 1600 dpi, every label and package produced here reflects Arrow’s commitment to uncompromising quality.

Visitors can explore the entire range of ArrowJet solutions  from narrow web to wide web systems up to 25 inches. The lineup includes the ArrowJet Aqua 330R, a powerful workhorse for high-speed in-house digital label production; the ArrowJet Hybrid Pro, which integrates digital printing with inline Slitting; and the ArrowJet Aqua 800M, built for wide web flexible packaging applications. For converters seeking versatility, Arrow’s print-and-cut systems like the ArrowJet Nova 250R and ArrowJet Nova 330R Print, Cut & Deliver seamless, inline printing and laser cutting, helping businesses reduce setup times and eliminate costly tooling.

The Canada Experience Center is designed to support every stage of production  from prototyping to mid-run jobs, seasonal labels to variable data printing, and security features to compliance packaging. With its modular workflow, Arrow Systems helps converters expand capabilities without adding complexity.

“Brands today don’t just need printers; they need partners who understand their pressures,” adds Shaan Patel. “Whether it’s a food brand needing compliance-ready inks, or a cosmetic company requiring color accuracy across SKUs, our systems deliver both speed and quality.”

Arrow’s technology is already driving measurable improvements for converters  reducing waste by up to 40%, cutting lead times by 25%, and improving consistency across materials from film to paper. This means faster market launches, less rework, and more profitable production cycles.

“Our mission has always been to help brands produce better, faster, and more responsibly,” says Shaan Patel. “We’ve engineered these systems for industries that can’t afford inconsistency from food and pharma to cosmetics and nutraceuticals. Every solution we offer is built for long-term reliability and sustainability.”

The Experience Center isn’t just a showcase it’s a collaboration hub where innovation meets execution. It represents Arrow Systems’ broader vision: to empower the print industry with sustainable technology, consistent results, and accessible digital transformation.

If you’re a brand owner, converter, or packaging innovator, Arrow Systems invites you to see these solutions in action. Step inside, experiment with materials, and witness how Arrow’s ecosystem transforms print production from the ground up.

title.rendered: Arrow Launches Trade In Desktop Printers

content.rendered:
Table of Contents

Arrow Launches Trade In Program for Desktop Memjet Printers

Let’s be honest, your old Afinia, VIPColor, or Trojan printer has probably earned its keep. It’s printed thousands of labels, powered countless jobs, and maybe even helped you land your first big client. But here’s the truth no one likes to say out loud: what got you here won’t get you there.

The market is faster, sharper, and more demanding than ever. Now, the real question isn’t whether your printer still works, it’s whether it’s still working for you.

This blog will help you navigate:

  • The challenges faced with older/legacy inkjet label printers.
    Why a trade-in upgrade to a state-of-the-art system like the ArrowJet family makes sense.
  • How to structure a trade-in program that benefits you and your clients.
  • Key criteria to evaluate your upgrade decision, and how to maximise return on investment.
  • How Arrow Systems supports you through the process: trade-in value, upgrade path, implementation.

What’s Holding You Back?

Let’s identify the pain-points of staying with older inkjet label printing machines:

Slower throughput & productivity limits

The older style, desktop printers were designed for a different market than what we see today. As jobs shift to faster turnarounds, higher volumes, more variable data, and an increasing demand for eco-friendly solutions, the older style printers can become a problem.

The older, desktop Memjet printers just do not offer the same speeds, roll-handling, or finishing throughput as newer models. The ArrowJet uses a Siemens PLC to enable the machine to run up to 150’/min versus the slower 18-27’/min of the desktop styles.

Rising cost-of-ownership

  • Maintenance: older print heads, tougher to source parts, downtime risk
    • The ArrowJet uses the latest printheads which last significantly longer than the VersaPass heads
    • Parts are easy to find a locally available in most major markets

  • Ink cost: Desktop style Memjet printers utilize small, expensive ink tanks
    • The ArrowJet has options for 2L, 10L, and 55L bulk inks
    • This reduces your operating costs allowing you to keep more of the profits!

  • Waste: mis-feeds, roll misalignment, higher rejects translate into cost
    • The desktop style printers often used offline unwinders/rewinders leading to mis feeds and jamming
    • The ArrowJet features all Siemens based PLC design which allows for high-speed roll to roll feeding with no jamming or waste!

  • Compatibility: newer inks, new substrates, finishing expectations may not align with older machines
    • As your company grows you need to continue to reduce operating costs
    • Arrow has developed inline and offline primers to work with our print technology!

Quality & aesthetics expectations rising

Brand owners expect sharper print, richer color, more premium finishes, faster turnarounds. If you’re using a machine that struggles with newer substrates (say premium metallic films, flexible packaging, or specialty applications) or slower drying, you may lose premium jobs or face re-prints or outsourcing.

Risk of obsolescence / support issues

Technology evolves: manufacturers may stop support for older models, parts become scarce and more expensive, service becomes slower. Some trade-in programs highlight exactly this risk. For example, one vendor warns that outdated printers can pose network security risk and slow productivity.

If the device you own is nearing end-of-service, the risk of failure, compatibility issues, or inability to print new materials increases.

Competitive disadvantage

If your competitors have upgraded to newer machines with faster speed, better substrate compatibility, and lower running costs, you may find yourself losing jobs on price (to offset your higher cost) or losing jobs on inability to offer premium finishes.

Trade-In & Upgrade to ArrowJet

Here’s how a well-structured trade-in upgrade program solves those challenges:

Fresh technology, improved capability

By upgrading to a modern ArrowJet system, you gain:

  • Faster print speeds and higher throughput: meaning more jobs per day, shorter turnarounds, higher margin
  • Broader substrate compatibility: ability to run premium PP, PET, metallic, holographics and flexible packaging materials reliably
  • Better ink efficiency: newer machines often use more advanced inks, drying systems, and less waste
  • Enhanced finishing workflows: automated roll-handling, servo control, better web stability
  • Future-proofing: you’re ready for next-generation media, higher expectations, and emerging markets

Risk-reduction through trade-in credit

A trade-in program gives you value for your older assets and smooths transition cost. Many vendors run such program (for example, trade-in of old printers for cash rebates) to encourage customers to upgrade.
By doing so you reduce capital expenditure, maintain cash flow, and move to higher productivity quicker.

Better total cost of ownership (TCO)

While the upfront cost of a new machine may be higher, the operational savings, higher yield, less downtime, less waste, higher margin jobs combine to improve TCO. Plus you open doors to new premium jobs, which boosts revenue!

Competitive advantage & market positioning

With upgraded equipment you can market yourself as “high-speed digital label converter with premium inks” rather than “legacy-printer operator”. That helps you win new clients, higher value jobs, and clearly differentiate.

Here are actionable steps to design or engage with a trade-in program:

  1. Inventory your current machines
    • Model, age, hours run, maintenance history.
    • Are there known issues (roll feed, finishing problems, colour inconsistency)?
    • What substrates/media can you run and where are you constrained?


  2. Define your upgrade criteria
    • What minimum speed/throughput do you need?
    • What substrates do you want to run (premium metallic, holographic, PP, PET)?
    • What finishing workflows are you moving toward (e.g., full roll-to-roll, high speed, automated slitting)?
    • What budget or monthly cost can you allocate?


  3. Estimate the cost-savings/benefits
    • Calculate downtime costs, waste costs, opportunity losses on premium jobs
    • Estimate how many more jobs you could do with the new machine
    • Estimate the margin lift from being able to offer premium materials
    • Include the trade-in credit from the old machine to reduce cost


  4. Communicate with your vendor/partner
    • Ask about trade-in eligibility: what models are accepted (often older Afinia, Trojan, VIPColor etc)
    • Get clear terms: credit value, condition of machine, timeframe, how the transition works
    • Ensure you schedule installation, training, integration with your workflow


  5. Plan transition with minimal disruption
    • Ideally, you should run the old machine until the new is installed and validated
    • Plan substrate trials, print-test runs on new machine ahead of production ramp
    • Train operators, update workflows, ensure finishing processes work with new systems


  6. Leverage the upgrade as marketing
    • Announce to clients that you have upgraded equipment and can now offer premium substrates, faster turnaround, better quality
    • Use it as a differentiator in proposals: “we now run metallic gold PP inkjet-coated film on ArrowJet, giving you shelf-impact” etc

Why Arrow Systems is Your Ideal Partner for Trade Ins

At Arrow Systems, we understand the entire ecosystem: from printer hardware (trade-in for older Afinia, Trojan, VIPColor machines) to substrate (premium film) to finishing workflows. Here’s what we bring:

  • A track-record in label printing, offering and supporting digital inkjet systems and substrates.
  • A structured upgrade path: we help you evaluate your old printer, quantify trade-in value, and plan upgrade to ArrowJet.
  • Synchronized substrate and hardware strategy: your new machine + our premium material guarantee = optimal output.
  • Training & support: we get your team up and running, minimize ramp-up time.
  • We help you position yourself in the market as the premium converter with upgraded capability.
Explore Our Printers

FAQs

1. The old machine still works, why invest now?

While it may still print, you might be leaving productivity, substrate flexibility, margin on the table. The upgrade gives you new capabilities, new market opportunities, and better ROI. The trade-in credit also softens the cost.

2. We’re worried about transition downtime and costs.

With proper planning (old machine runs until new machine validated, trial runs on substrates, training ahead of production), transition can be smooth. The long-term gains in productivity justify the short-term planning.

3. We aren’t sure we need premium substrates yet, maybe wait.

Even if your current job mix is “standard”, the ability to handle premium jobs gives you optionality. The market is evolving; early adoption keeps you ahead rather than catching up. Plus the new machine will likely handle your existing jobs better, so you’re improving now even before premium jobs come.

Conclusion

Being “good enough” is no longer enough in digital Label printing. If you are still operating legacy inkjet label printers like Afinia L801/L901, VIPColor or Trojan T2-C, you’re likely facing hidden cost-leaks, substrate limitations, reduced ability to capture premium jobs and potential obsolescence.
A well-structured trade-in upgrade to an ArrowJet system gives you the speed, substrate flexibility, finishing capability, reduced waste and future-proofing you need  while the trade-in credit softens the investment.
At Arrow Systems we’re ready to partner with you, assess your current equipment, help you select the right upgrade, plan the transition, and support you with substrate and finishing ecosystems so you hit the ground running.

title.rendered: 5 Technological Advancements Driving Digital Printing in Packaging

content.rendered:

5 Technological Advancements Driving Digital Printing in Packaging

The world of packaging is moving at lightning speed, and at the center of this transformation is digital printing. Once considered a niche tool for short runs and labels, digital printing is now reshaping the packaging industry with faster production, smarter workflows, and eco-friendly innovations.

At the heart of this shift are five key technological advancements driving digital printing in packaging. From printhead innovations to eco-friendly ink systems and AI-powered automation, these breakthroughs are making it possible for brands to deliver packaging that’s not only faster and cheaper to produce but also more customized, sustainable, and engaging than ever before.

Let’s explore how these technologies are revolutionizing packaging in 2025 and beyond.

1. Printhead and Ink Innovations

Modern printhead technologies are at the foundation of digital printing’s rise in packaging. Today’s advanced printheads deliver high-resolution, durable, and vibrant output across a wide variety of substrates—from paper and board to flexible films and plastics.

Why it matters:

  • High-resolution graphics: Sharp text, vivid colors, and photo-quality imagery give brands a stronger presence on retail shelves.

  • Durable prints: Better adhesion ensures packaging withstands handling, shipping, and storage.

  • Versatility: Brands can now print on flexible films, pouches, cartons, and even rigid packaging substrates.

Water-Based Pigment Inks: A Game-Changer

Among the biggest innovations are water-based pigment inks, which are reshaping digital packaging. Unlike solvent-heavy alternatives, these inks are:

  • Food-safe and compliant (ideal for printed pouches and FMCG packaging).

  • Eco-friendly, reducing VOC emissions and supporting sustainable production.

  • Vibrant and fast-drying, ensuring packaging pops on the shelf without compromising turnaround speed.

By combining advanced printheads with sustainable ink formulations, brands achieve high-quality, eco-responsible packaging that also meets global safety standards.

2. AI and Press Automation

Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation are transforming digital printing into a smarter, leaner, and more reliable process.

How automation is driving packaging innovation:

  • Real-time adjustments: AI-driven systems detect and correct print variations instantly, ensuring consistent quality.

  • Predictive maintenance: Automated diagnostics predict when printheads or components need servicing, minimizing downtime.

  • Quick setup: Automated preflighting and calibration reduce operator workload and eliminate costly human errors.

  • Workflow automation: Switching between SKUs and short runs happens seamlessly, ideal for seasonal packaging and rapid product launches.

For brands, this means faster time-to-market, lower production risks, and packaging that keeps pace with consumer demands.

3. Sustainable Practices and Eco-Friendly Printing

Sustainability isn’t just a buzzword anymore—it’s a necessity. With growing consumer demand for greener products, digital printing in packaging has embraced eco-friendly innovations that benefit both brands and the planet.

Key sustainable practices include:

  • Water-based pigment inks: Safe for food-contact packaging and less harmful to the environment.

  • Recyclable and compostable substrates: Compatible with modern digital presses, helping reduce plastic waste.

  • Energy-efficient presses: Lower power consumption reduces both costs and environmental footprint.

  • On-demand production: Eliminates excess inventory and minimizes waste, since brands only print what they need.

For brands, this means they can proudly align their packaging with eco-friendly commitments while still enjoying the vibrancy and flexibility digital printing provides.

Explore More

4. Design and Customization Tools

Today’s packaging is no longer just about holding a product—it’s about engaging consumers and telling a story. Digital printing is empowering brands with powerful design and customization tools that allow for unprecedented creativity.

Major design innovations:

  • Variable data printing (VDP): Enables serialized packs, regional designs, multilingual packaging, and personalization.

  • AI-powered design platforms: Automate artwork creation and optimize graphics for maximum impact.

  • 3D previews and digital twins: Let brands visualize designs in real time before production, reducing errors.

  • Mass customization: Seasonal SKUs, limited editions, and personalized packaging are now affordable and scalable.

This level of flexibility allows brands to create printed pouches with unique designs for different audiences, seasonal promotions, or product launches—making packaging a marketing tool as much as a protective one.

5. Connectivity and Smart Packaging

One of the most exciting innovations in packaging is the rise of connectivity and Smart packaging, powered by digital printing and IoT.

What’s possible with smart packaging:

  • QR codes, NFC tags, and AR experiences: Add interactivity to packaging, linking consumers to promotions, loyalty programs, or product information.

     

  • Serialized designs for traceability: Support supply chain transparency and Anti-counterfeiting.

     

  • Dynamic content: Artwork or codes can change instantly from one pouch to the next.

     

  • Consumer engagement: Packaging becomes a two-way communication channel instead of a static surface.

For example, a coffee brand can print unique QR codes on short-run seasonal pouches that connect consumers to origin stories or brewing guides. This creates deeper engagement and brand loyalty.

The Bigger Picture: Why Printed Pouches Lead the Way

Among all packaging formats, printed pouches stand out as the best example of how these five innovations converge:

  • Loved by customers: Lightweight, resealable, and easy to carry.

  • Perfect for short runs: Ideal for startups, seasonal SKUs, and limited editions.

  • Highly customizable: Multiple flavors, versions, and promotions in one production cycle.

  • Lower production cost: No plates or cylinders; brands save money on setup and inventory.

  • Streamlined workflows: Quick artwork changes and on-demand production reduce lead times from weeks to days.

Whether it’s snacks, pet food, coffee, or personal care products, digitally printed pouches combine innovation, sustainability, and consumer appeal—making them the packaging format of the future.

Conclusion

The five technological advancements—printhead and ink innovations, AI-driven automation, sustainable practices, advanced design tools, and connectivity through smart packaging—are driving the next era of digital printing in packaging.

For brands, this means more than just efficiency. It means:

  • Faster speed to market with seasonal SKUs and short runs.

  • Lower costs and reduced waste through streamlined workflows.

  • Personalization and engagement via custom printed pouches.

  • Eco-responsibility with water-based pigment inks and recyclable substrates.

As we look ahead to 2025 and beyond, one thing is clear: Innovation in digital printing packaging isn’t optional—it’s essential. The brands that embrace these advancements will lead the way in creating packaging that is smarter, greener, and more engaging than ever.

title.rendered: Cosmetics Labels & Flexible Packaging

content.rendered:
Table of Contents

Cosmetics Labels & Flexible Packaging: The Role of High-Resolution, Sustainable Inks

In the dazzling world of cosmetics—where shelf appeal is almost as important as formulation—a label isn’t just a label. It’s a brand’s handshake, first impression, promise of quality. Beauty brands everywhere are under soaring pressure: crisp visuals, vibrant colors, luxe finishes and compliance with environmental, health, and safety standards.

Cosmetic labels must marry brand aesthetics (gloss, sharpness, color fidelity, tactile finish) with regulatory compliance (safety of inks, sustainability of materials, environmental footprint). In today’s market, anything less than excellence risks being lost in the sea of competitors—or worse, being flagged for non-compliance.

That’s where printers like the ArrowJet Nova 250R and ArrowJet Nova 330R step in. These aren’t just machines: they represent a solution—one that helps cosmetics brands deliver high-end visual branding and sustainable, safe, regulatory-friendly packaging.

What Cosmetic Brands Face Today

Here are the chief challenges in label/flex-pack printing for cosmetics:

  1. Visual differentiation & premium aesthetics. Gloss finishes, vivid color shifts, fine details like foil or embossing, metallics, gradients—labels must stand out on shelves or in competitor-heavy online photos.

  2. Speed & flexibility. Multiple SKUs, smaller runs (limited editions, seasonal packaging, bespoke products), frequent design tweaks. Traditional methods (analog printing, die-cutting separately, outsourcing) can be slow, rigid, expensive.

  3. Regulatory, health & safety compliance. Inks must be safe for contact (direct or indirect), particularly when packaging might touch skin; standards vary across regions. Migration of harmful substances must be controlled. Also, many brands want “green” credentials: sustainable inks, recyclable or compostable substrates, lower VOCs, lower carbon footprint.

  4. Cost & waste control. High print quality often means higher costs; inefficiencies in finishing (die cutting, trimming, slitting) lead to material waste. Brands need both ROI and responsible resource usage.

  5. Full supply chain traceability & environmental compliance. From sourcing of materials to ink composition, recyclability, sometimes even food or pharma grade regulatory compliance if multi-use environments.

So: cosmetic brands need a solution that lets them produce visually striking labels/flexible packaging in-house or on demand, with high resolution, sustainable ink options, inline finishing, minimal waste, and regulatory peace of mind.

Introducing the Solution: ArrowJet Nova 250R & ArrowJet Nova 330R

Explore More
Explore More

These two machines from Arrow Systems are designed precisely for these challenges. Let’s look at how they tackle the problem through their features, and why they’re particularly well suited for cosmetics brands.

ArrowJet Nova 250R: Features & Benefits for Cosmetic Labels

Key Specifications & Strengths

  • Max Media Width: ~250 mm (~9.84″) 

  • Resolution: Up to 1600 × 1600 dpi, delivering sharp, vivid full-color prints. 

  • Ink Type: Water-based pigment or dye based (depending), compliant with Nestlé Guidance. 

  • Print Speed: 3 m/min to 18 m/min (which is approx. 10 ft to 60 ft/min) depending on configuration and substrate. 

  • Inline Laser Cutter / Die-Cutter: Laser power up to ~125-150 W, capable of full-cut, half-cut, perforation, scribing, marking, etc. 

  • Additional Finishing Capabilities: Inline slitting, dual rewinders, “cut to part” for stickers, job changeover (optionally with barcode reader) to switch jobs dynamically. 

How It Addresses Cosmetic Brand Needs

  • Premium Visuals: 1600×1600 dpi enables fine detail (think filigree borders, thin lines, sheen gradients). Dye vs pigment inks provide flexibility—pigment gives more lightfastness; dyes often more vibrant (depending on substrate/treatment).

  • Flexible SKU Runs & Customization: With inline finishing and changeover, cosmetics brands can do small / seasonal runs, custom designs, limited editions efficiently. No need to outsource die cutting and then assemble separately.

  • Regulatory & Safety Compliance: Water-based (and some water-based pigment) inks reduce VOCs; Nestlé Guidance compliance means a higher chance of meeting food-contact or consumer product safety where relevant. For cosmetics, indirect contact with skin (labels touching jars, etc.) often requires such compliant inks. Pigment inks tend to migrate less. 

  • Waste & Cost Efficiency: Inline operations reduce handling, transport between print & finishing; slitting, dual rewinders manage material more efficiently; cut-to-part reduces scrap. Also lower substrate needs perhaps, because of higher resolution meaning less need for extra lamination or overprinting for color pop.

  • Sustainability Credentials: Water-based inks, efficient use of substrate, less waste, lower energy usage in finishing likely. For brands that need to show sustainability (for packaging that can be recycled, verifying ink safety) this helps.

ArrowJet Nova 330R: Features & Benefits

Key Specifications

  • Max Media Width: ~330 mm (~13″) 

  • Print Resolution: 1600 × 1600 dpi CMYK; high fidelity full-color. 

  • Print Speed: ~27 m/min (≈90 ft/min) printing; cutting speed up to ~45 m/min.

  • Ink Technology: Water-based pigment inks; Memjet DuraFlex® print engine. 

  • Laser Finishing System: Integrated with ArrowCut Nova 330R laser die-cutter; powerful single 250 W laser for crisp die cutting and finishing. 

  • Other Inline Features: Laminator, slitting, matrix removal, dual rewinding, job changeover, full/half cut, perforation, scoring, marking etc. 

How It Fits Cosmetics Brands

  • Scale & Versatility: Larger media width means ability to produce larger flexibles or wider labels (e.g. front/back panel labels, pouch packaging, flexible film wrap labels). This helps brands that want flexible packaging or bigger graphical assets.

  • High Speed with Quality: 27 m/min print speed with same high resolution means faster throughput without compromising detail. For brands needing to meet higher volumes or shorter lead times, Nova 330R accelerates delivery.

  • Full In-Line Production: With in-line finishing, laminating, die cutting, etc., the process becomes smoother, less labour, fewer handoffs. This reduces mis-registration, errors, and also helps maintain consistency across batches – important for brand identity.

  • Improved Ink & Substrate Efficiency: Pigment inks in Nova 330R require lower coating weights compared to water-based dye systems, meaning thinner or less coating layers on substrates. That reduces material usage and cost, and may also help recyclability or compostability if substrates/layers are more minimal. 

  • Regulatory & Safety Standards: Water-based pigment inks are more stable, often lower in harmful volatile compounds. If inks meet Nestlé Guidance or similar, brands get better assurance when it comes to consumer safety, indirect contact, potential allergen or irritant migration. Also better suited for food, pharma, or cosmetics that might be used around mouth/skin.

Environmental Compliance, Safety & Brand Aesthetic: How Nova 250R & 330R Help Balance All

A cosmetics brand typically has a wish-list:

  • Stunning visuals: vibrant, gloss, sharpness, maybe holographics or foils.

  • Safety: non-toxic inks, minimal migration, skin contact safety where needed.

  • Sustainability: eco-friendly materials, recyclable packaging, low VOC, minimized waste.

  • Regulatory compliance: various global standards (EU, FDA, ISO, etc.).

  • Cost & speed.

Here’s how the ArrowJet Nova pair addresses those trade-offs:

Aspect

What brands demand

How Nova 250R / 330R address it

Print Quality

High resolution, sharp detail, vibrant color, consistency across batches

Both machines offer 1600×1600 dpi resolution. Nova 330R uses Memjet DuraFlex engine for stable, high fidelity color. Nova 250R’s inline Memjet inkjet + laser die-cutting ensures clean edges.

Finishing & Shape Complexity

Unique die-cut shapes, perforations, half cuts, sticker/cut-outs, custom geometries

Inline laser die-cutting (full, half, perforation, marking, scribing) built in. Cut-to-part for stickers on Nova 250R; Nova 330R with laser finishing system.

Ink Safety / Regulatory Compliance

Safe for skin contact or proximity, compliant with regional/global safety systems, low VOCs, minimal migration

Water-based inks, pigment options, Nestlé Guidance compliance, cartridges or bulk ink systems reducing potential contamination, better control over chemistry.

Material / Substrate Versatility

Want to use paper, PE, PP, PET, maybe bio-materials, laminates, foils, films; also ability to apply coatings / lamination

Nova 330R supports laminator, treatments; Nova 250R has overprinting systems. Both support varied substrates. Novas accept thinner or thicker substrates depending on configuration.

Eco / Sustainability

Reduce waste, use renewable/recyclable materials, lower environmental impact of inks & coatings

Less coating weight needed (Nova 330R), water-based inks (lower VOCs, safer disposal), inline finishing reduces waste, dual rewinders, efficient job changeover reducing scrap.

Turnaround & Flexibility

Short runs, custom jobs, seasonal packaging, frequent design changes, minimal lead time

Inline systems; job-changeover, barcode reader options; cut to part; ability to print + cut in one pass. Nova 250R: smaller width so more nimble for smaller jobs; Nova 330R: higher capacity for larger runs but still flexible.

 

In-Depth: How High Resolution & Sustainable Inks Matter for Cosmetics Labels

To appreciate why “1600×1600 dpi + water-based / pigment inks + inline finishing” is more than marketing speak, here are some technical & practical elements brands must get right.

1. Resolution, Finish & Brand Perception

  • Fine texts (ingredient lists, small print), micro lines, cosmetic packaging often uses foils or raised effects. Low resolution or coarse halftones will reveal banding, jagged edges, especially in gradients or spot colors.

  • Texture matters: gloss vs matte; finishes like soft touch or velvet require coatings; transparent films demand ink clarity. The sharper the print, the less you need heavy coatings to “smooth over” roughness.

2. Ink Type: Pigment vs Dye, Water-Based vs Solvent / UV

  • Pigment inks: more stable (lightfast, fade resistant), less migration risk, more durable. Good for color longevity and regulatory safety.

  • Water-based inks: lower VOC, safer for workers and the environment, easier to dispose of; often more acceptable for substrates intended for skin contact or food-adjacent products.

  • Dye inks: can be vibrant but may bleed, fade, or have migration issues; may require coatings or laminates to seal.

  • Solvent and UV inks: strong durability, but often higher VOC, curing agents, safety / environmental concerns.

So machines like Nova 250R / 330R using water-based pigment / water-based inks (with responsible compliance, e.g. Nestlé Guidance) are better suited for cosmetics labels that need safety + aesthetics.

3. Substrate, Coating, Laminates & Flexibility

  • Many cosmetics labels use films (PET, PP), metallic laminates, foils, transparent windows. Some are pressure sensitive adhesives, others heat seals, flexible pouches etc.

  • The printing machine must be able to handle these materials: varied thicknesses, finishes, whether adhesives or liners; also must match lamination, post-print treatments.

  • Inline finishing (laser cutting, slitting, laminating, matrix removal) is a big plus: less handling, less chance of misalignment or damage, less shipping or external finishing (thus lower carbon / cost).

4. Safety, Environment & Regulatory Standards

  • Cosmetics packaging may indirectly contact skin—think labels that wrap around bottles, tubes that are squeezed, or even lip balms. The inks, adhesives, substrates must pass safety standards (e.g. EU’s Cosmetics Regulation, ISO safety for packaging, allergen/migration tests).

  • Environmental regulations are tightening: bans or restrictions on certain chemicals, stricter VOC limits, expectations of recyclable/compostable materials.

  • Certifications (Nestlé Guidance is referenced in the specs for Nova machines) help; water-based pigment inks are an asset; lower coating weights = less material / energy.

Comparative Use Case: When to Use Nova 250R vs Nova 330R

To show how cosmetics brands might choose between them:

Brand Scenario

Which Machine Fits Best

Indie brand with 10-20 SKUs: bottles, small labels, seasonal labels, frequent design changes, smaller runs

Nova 250R. Narrower width, more agile. Cut-to-part stickers, quicker job changeovers; cost of machine lower; inline finishing helps avoid outsourcing.

Mid-sized brand launching new flexible pouches, outer packaging, wanting more art coverage, larger labels, higher volumes, multiple SKUs with consistent high volume

Nova 330R. Larger media width, faster print & cut, supports laminating etc.; better suited when scale & speed are needed.

However, many brands will use both in their ecosystem: the 250R for prototyping, limited editions, or small-batch specialty items; the 330R for mainline runs or flexible packaging where size / volume matter.

Tips for Cosmetics Brands Using Nova 250R / 330R to Maximize Impact

Here are actionable recommendations for brands:

Design for the Equipment.

    • Ensure your artwork accounts for bleed, cut lines, half-cuts (if applicable), and laser precision.
    • Proof colors well; high resolution means subtle flaws will be visible—good substrates and color profiles matter.

Choose Substrates Carefully.

    • Decide: transparent vs opaque, film vs paper, matte vs gloss vs metallic finish. Test adhesion of inks, finishing effects (lamination, varnish).
    • If sustainability is a goal, consider recyclable films or bio-films, compostable liners, or materials that accept water-based inks well.

Finish Strategically.

      • Use lamination or varnish where needed (for protection, gloss, tactile feel), but avoid overcoating just to hide print imperfections—Nova machines’ resolution minimizes need for hiding flaws.
      • Use laser finishing for custom cuts / more premium tactile effects.

Ink Management & Compliance.

    • Validate the ink chemistry for your end-use: contact with skin, FDA / EU regulation, allergen considerations.
    • Keep records and certificates if required.

Optimize Waste & Cost.

    • Use job changeover, barcode reader options to reduce waste.
    • Dual rewinders, matrix removal options help reduce unused liner or scrap.
    • Monitor coating weight and reduce where possible; thinner coatings/lighter materials reduce costs and environmental impact.

Sustainability Messaging.

    • Once your process uses water-based / pigment inks and recyclable or bio-compatible materials, feature that in branding and marketing. It’s increasingly important for consumers.
    • Be transparent: e.g., “Labels printed with water-based pigment inks, compliant with Nestlé Guidance; materials recyclable / FSC certified (if applicable).”

Potential Limitations / Things to Watch Out For

While Nova 250R and 330R are powerful tools, brands should be aware of:

  • Upfront investment & operating costs. The hardware, ink, substrate costs, maintenance, operator training are non-trivial. Brands need to ensure volume/use frequency justifies it.

  • Substrate Compatibility Limits. Some exotic or specialty materials (very thick laminates, highly metallic foils, extremely thin films) may still pose challenges in terms of feed, finishing, or ink absorption.

  • Finish Durability. While ink resolution is high, inks themselves may need protective laminates or varnishes to resist rubbing, water, UV, etc. Even pigment inks have limits.

  • Regulatory Differences by Region. “Nestlé Guidance compliant” is good, but doesn’t automatically equal compliance with all local / national cosmetics / packaging laws. Testing, migration studies may still be needed.

  • Workflow and Prepress Considerations. Good color management, RIP software, artwork setup, proofing, finishing calibration are essential; otherwise the “high resolution” feature is wasted.

Conclusion: Why Nova 250R & 330R Are Ideal for Cosmetics Brand Labels & Flexible Packaging

In sum: for cosmetics brands striving to look premium, stay safe, and be sustainable, the combination of:

  • High resolution printing (1600×1600 dpi)

     

  • Water-based / pigment-based ink chemistry with compliance credentials

     

  • Inline finishing (laser cutting, slitting, matrix removal, laminating)

     

  • Faster job changeovers & flexible SKU handling

     

  • Lower waste and material efficiency

…makes the ArrowJet Nova 250R and Nova 330R strong contenders.

  • For smaller, boutique, artisanal or seasonal product lines, Nova 250R offers agility, sharpness, finishing, without excess scale overhead.

     

  • For brands with larger output, needing flexible packaging, larger media, or wanting to scale up premium finishes, Nova 330R delivers throughput without compromising aesthetics or safety.

When done thoughtfully—selecting substrate, managing inks, proofing, finishing—cosmetics labels produced on these machines can reinforce brand identity, meet regulatory/environmental demands, and even become a marketing point themselves.

Top 4 Food & Beverage Packaging Trends: Low-VOC Inks, Lightweighting & Refillable Design

The food and beverages packaging industry is undergoing a massive transformation. Consumer demand for safer, more sustainable products, combined with stringent regulatory frameworks, is pushing brands to rethink how they package, print, and deliver. From low-VOC inks to lightweight flexible packaging and refillable design systems, the trends shaping this space are redefining not only environmental standards but also performance expectations.

In this blog, we’ll explore the latest food and beverages packaging innovations, the critical role of water-based pigment inkjet solutions, and how cutting-edge technologies like the ArrowJet Bolt and ArrowJet 800M are helping businesses meet regulatory, sustainability, and performance challenges head-on.

ArrowJet Bolt

Explore More

ArrowJet Aqua 800M

Explore More

The New Age of Food and Beverages Packaging

The packaging industry has always evolved in response to consumer needs. Today, sustainability is the most powerful driver. Shoppers want packaging that not only protects freshness but also reflects their values: eco-consciousness, safety, and transparency.

Key trends include:

  • Low-VOC inks that minimize harmful emissions.

  • Lightweight packaging materials that reduce transportation costs and carbon footprint.

  • Refillable and reusable designs that extend packaging life cycles.

  • Paper-based pouches replacing plastics for improved recyclability.

These trends are not just voluntary—they’re backed by regulations like EU Packaging Waste Directives, U.S. FDA guidelines for indirect food contact, and Switzerland’s strict ink compliance frameworks. For converters and brands, the challenge is finding solutions that align with both market demand and legal compliance without compromising print quality or operational efficiency.

Why Low-VOC Inks Matter in Food & Beverage Packaging

Traditionally, solvent-based inks dominated packaging because of their durability. But they come with a heavy trade-off: volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions that contribute to air pollution and potential food safety concerns.

Low-VOC and water-based inks are now the preferred choice for food and beverages packaging because they:

  • Comply with global safety standards such as Swiss Ordinance and Nestlé Guidance.

     

  • Reduce harmful emissions, supporting brand sustainability goals.

     

  • Ensure safer migration levels, critical for flexible packaging in direct or indirect food contact.

Water-based pigment inks, in particular, stand out for their high color vibrancy, durability, and broad media compatibility—from flexible films to paper-based pouches.

Lightweighting: Efficiency Meets Sustainability

Another megatrend reshaping the packaging landscape is lightweighting—designing packaging with less material without sacrificing performance.

For the food and beverage sector, lightweighting offers:

  • Lower transportation costs due to reduced weight.

  • Smaller carbon footprint, aligning with corporate ESG commitments.

  • Improved shelf efficiency, as thinner films or pouches allow more units per shipment.

However, lightweight substrates can be more challenging to print on, requiring precise ink adhesion and durability. This is where water-based pigment inkjet solutions shine, delivering strong bonding and resistance while maintaining vibrant, high-resolution prints.

Refillable Design: Closing the Loop

The shift toward refillable packaging is not a fad—it’s a movement. Consumers increasingly expect brands to offer refill options for beverages, sauces, snacks, and even dry goods. Retailers and governments are also incentivizing refill stations and reusable packaging systems.

For converters, this introduces new requirements:

  • Durable packaging capable of multiple refill cycles.

     

  • Print durability that withstands handling, washing, or long shelf life.

     

  • Eco-friendly inks that won’t compromise recyclability.

Water-based inks play a crucial role here. Unlike solvent-based inks that can complicate recycling streams, water-based pigment inks enable cleaner, safer recycling while still providing long-lasting print quality.

The Regulatory Pressure: Why Brands Can’t Afford to Ignore Ink Compliance

Food and beverages packaging is one of the most tightly regulated sectors. With consumer health at stake, global bodies are constantly revising rules around inks, coatings, and substrates.

Key challenges include:

  • Migration limits: Inks must not transfer harmful substances into food.

  • Swiss Ordinance compliance: One of the strictest frameworks for packaging inks.

  • Regional differences: What’s approved in the EU may face different restrictions in the U.S. or Asia.

Failure to comply can lead to recalls, fines, and long-term reputational damage. This makes ink selection not just a technical choice but a strategic decision.

Water-Based Pigment Inkjet: The Key to Modern Food & Beverage Packaging

So, how do brands align with eco-trends, regulatory compliance, and consumer expectations—all while keeping production efficient? The answer lies in water-based pigment inkjet solutions.

Advantages include:

  • Eco-compliance: No hazardous VOC emissions, Swiss-compliant ink formulations.

     

  • Durability: Scratch, light, and water resistance suitable for flexible packaging.

     

  • High-resolution print quality: 1600 x 1600 dpi for vibrant, brand-consistent graphics.

     

  • Media versatility: Compatible with films, papers, foils, and pouches.

     

  • Operational efficiency: Reduced manual interventions and easy integration with digital workflows.

This is where ArrowJet solutions become game-changers for the industry.

Criteria

Fully compliant with Swiss Ordinance, Nestlé Guidance, and global food packaging standards. Low-migration, safe for direct/indirect contact.

VOC Emissions

Print Durability

Print Quality

Substrate Compatibility

Sustainability

Operational Efficiency

Consumer Safety & Brand Trust

ArrowJet Solutions: Redefining Food and Beverages Packaging

ArrowJet Bolt

Designed for high-speed, high-volume digital label and flexible packaging printing, the ArrowJet Bolt is built for converters looking for maximum throughput with uncompromised quality.

  • Speed: Industry-leading throughput for short and long runs.

  • Resolution: 1600 x 1600 dpi ensures packaging pops with color vibrancy.

  • Ink: Water-based pigment inks, fully compliant with food safety standards.

  • Application: Ideal for snack packaging, beverage labels, and flexible pouches.

ArrowJet 800M

Engineered specifically for flexible packaging converters, the ArrowJet 800M combines rugged mechanics with advanced inkjet technology.

  • Media handling: Supports flexible substrates like PET, PE, and paper-based pouches.

     

  • Sustainability: Perfect for lightweight and recyclable packaging.

     

  • Compliance: Meets Swiss Ordinance and EU food packaging standards.

     

  • Use cases: From frozen food pouches to refillable beverage sachets.

Both models empower brands to move away from solvent-heavy processes toward eco-friendly digital packaging solutions without compromising efficiency or quality.

Challenges and How ArrowJet Solves Them

1. Regulatory Complexity

  • Challenge: Brands struggle to navigate regional ink regulations.

  • Solution: ArrowJet’s water-based pigment inks are developed to meet the strictest global standards, ensuring compliance across markets.

2. Substrate Compatibility

  • Challenge: Lightweight and recyclable films are difficult to print on.

  • Solution: The ArrowJet 800M is optimized for flexible packaging materials, ensuring excellent ink adhesion and durability.

3. Cost Pressure

  • Challenge: Balancing sustainability with profitability.

  • Solution: Digital inkjet reduces waste, setup time, and manual intervention—helping converters lower costs while meeting eco-goals.

4. Consumer Demand for Vibrancy

  • Challenge: Eco-friendly packaging shouldn’t mean dull prints.

  • Solution: ArrowJet’s high-resolution systems deliver rich, vibrant colors that elevate shelf presence.

The Future of Food & Beverages Packaging

Looking ahead, the intersection of sustainability and technology will continue to drive innovation in packaging. Brands that embrace water-based pigment Inkjet printing will have the edge in meeting both consumer and regulatory demands.

We can expect to see:

  • Wider adoption of paper-based flexible packaging as plastics face stricter bans.

     

  • Growth of on-demand digital printing for seasonal and localized products.

     

  • Expansion of refillable ecosystems requiring durable, eco-friendly print solutions.

Conclusion: Why Water-Based Inkjet is the Future

The global shift in food and beverages packaging is clear: low-VOC inks, lightweight designs, and refillable packaging are no longer optional—they are imperatives. At the heart of these trends lies a single enabler: water-based pigment inkjet solutions.

With innovations like the ArrowJet Bolt and ArrowJet 800M, converters and brands can:

  • Stay ahead of evolving regulations.

  • Deliver sustainable, consumer-friendly packaging.

  • Reduce costs while boosting print quality and efficiency.

For businesses ready to future-proof their packaging operations, the path is clear: embrace digital, embrace sustainability, and embrace the power of water-based inks.

Top 10 Innovations in Multilayer Flexible Packaging: Sustainable Barrier Solutions & Printable Layers

Multilayer flexible packaging has become the backbone of modern packaging. From snacks and coffee to cosmetics and pharmaceuticals, industries rely on it to deliver shelf life, barrier protection, and eye-catching branding. But the old ways of building these packages—stacking different plastics, aluminium foils, and coatings—have created problems: recyclability issues, higher costs, and challenges in achieving vibrant, durable printing.

Today, a wave of innovations is transforming how multilayer packaging is designed and printed. Let’s explore the top 10 innovations that are shaping the future, and see how ArrowJet’s water-based pigment inkjet technology is helping solve one of the toughest challenges: printability on sustainable substrates.

1. Functional Barrier Paper

One of the most exciting shifts is the rise of functional barrier paper. Traditionally, paper has been used as an outer wrap, but new coatings and barrier treatments allow paper to act as a true alternative to plastic-heavy laminates. With resistance to oxygen, moisture, and grease, these papers provide excellent protection while maintaining a recyclable, lightweight profile. For food and beverage packaging in particular, functional paper answers consumer demand for eco-friendly, natural-feeling packs without sacrificing performance.

2. Mono-Material Films with Specialty Coatings

Historically, multilayer packaging relied on combining incompatible polymers, which created recycling headaches. The new generation of packaging favors mono-material films—all polyethylene (PE) or all polypropylene (PP)—that are made functional with advanced coatings. These coatings deliver oxygen and moisture resistance, making the pack perform like a complex laminate but recycle like a single material. For brand owners, this means sustainability without compromising shelf life or machinability.

3. Advanced EVOH Structures

Ethylene vinyl alcohol (EVOH) has long been prized as a barrier layer against oxygen. Recent innovations in EVOH blends have improved machinability, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness. Manufacturers can now use thinner EVOH layers while maintaining protection, which means lighter structures, lower material use, and easier incorporation into recyclable designs. EVOH remains essential in packaging for sensitive foods, coffee, and pharmaceutical products.

4. Aluminium-Free High Barrier Films

While aluminium foil laminates have been a gold standard for blocking oxygen, moisture, and light, they pose recyclability and weight issues. The industry is now turning to aluminium-free high barrier films that mimic foil’s protection without its drawbacks. These films make packs lighter, more sustainable, and easier to process while still meeting stringent requirements for shelf life—ideal for snacks, dairy, and ready-to-eat meals.

5. Biopolymer Multilayers

With sustainability top of mind, biopolymer-based multilayers are entering the spotlight. Materials like polylactic acid (PLA), PHA, and cellulose are being laminated with coatings to create compostable solutions. While they still face challenges around moisture sensitivity and cost, biopolymers are carving out a space in industries that want renewable, plant-based options—especially organic foods, sustainable cosmetics, and eco-conscious consumer goods.

6. Functional Nano-Coatings

Nanotechnology is enabling ultra-thin coatings that provide barrier performance once only achievable with heavy laminates. Nanocomposite and metal-oxide coatings can drastically reduce oxygen and moisture transmission while keeping materials lightweight and flexible. These coatings are especially promising for pharmaceutical and medical packaging, where protection must be uncompromising but material efficiency is critical.

7. Printable Sustainable Films

One of the overlooked hurdles in packaging is printability. Many sustainable films and barrier substrates have low surface energy, making it difficult for inks to adhere. Recent innovations in printable barrier films are solving this by engineering higher surface energy or adding coatings designed to work seamlessly with modern inks. This means converters can deliver both sustainability and shelf appeal without additional complex treatments.

8. Water-Based Pigment Inks: ArrowJet’s Solution

Even with better substrates, printing technology has had to evolve. Solvent and UV inks often add complications, from VOC emissions to recyclability concerns. That’s why water-based pigment inks have become a game-changer. They are eco-friendly, low-VOC, food-safe, and deliver vibrant, durable colors across a wide range of substrates.

ArrowJet leads this movement with presses like the ArrowJet Bolt and Aqua Series, which pair advanced water-based pigment inks with 1600 x 1600 dpi resolution. These systems ensure bright, durable branding that meets Nestlé and Swiss food packaging compliance, while still being compatible with sustainable barrier films and papers. In short, ArrowJet makes sustainable packaging print as beautifully as traditional substrates—without compromising safety or recyclability.

Explore More

9. Recyclable Barrier Pouches

Stand-up pouches remain one of the fastest-growing packaging formats thanks to their convenience and visual impact. The latest innovation is recyclable barrier pouches made with mono-material laminates that deliver shelf stability while being accepted into recycling streams. From pet food to coffee, these pouches are quickly becoming the standard, giving consumers eco-friendly options without sacrificing usability or aesthetics.

10. Smart Packaging Layers

Finally, multilayer packaging is becoming smart. Digital watermarks, QR codes, and embedded traceability features are now being integrated into layers themselves. This makes recycling sortation more efficient, ensures supply chain transparency, and enables brands to engage directly with consumers through their packaging. Smart multilayer structures aren’t just about protection—they’re becoming a channel for information and interaction.

Industries Leading Adoption

The innovations in multilayer flexible packaging are already shaping industries:

  • Food & Beverages rely on high barrier pouches, recyclable laminates, and functional paper.

  • Pharmaceutical & Medical packaging demands uncompromising oxygen and moisture protection.

  • Cosmetics & Personal Care require both barrier performance and striking aesthetics.

  • Pet Food & Agriculture need durability, long shelf life, and sustainable formats.

Conclusion: The Future of Multilayer Flexible Packaging

The packaging industry is proving that sustainability doesn’t have to mean compromise. With functional barrier papers, mono-material laminates, advanced coatings, and smart designs, multilayer flexible packaging is evolving into a sustainable, recyclable, and highly printable solution.

And with ArrowJet’s water-based pigment inkjet technology, brands and converters can finally bridge the gap between eco-friendly substrates and world-class printing. High-quality, compliant, and sustainable packaging is no longer a distant goal—it’s here.
