10 Step Guide For the best Frozen Food Pouches with Water-Based Inks

The Frozen Food Aisle is Booming

Take a walk down any supermarket freezer aisle and you’ll see it: a blizzard of vibrant, glossy pouches competing for your attention. From frozen berries and ready-to-eat meals to meatless burgers and exotic smoothie blends, the frozen food segment is growing rapidly. In fact, the global frozen food Market is projected to reach over $400 billion by 2030. That’s not just growth; it’s an avalanche of opportunity.

Packaging That Can’t Keep Up

While brands are racing to innovate with product offerings, their packaging often lags behind. For many new and emerging food brands, packaging is either too expensive, too generic, or just not robust enough to survive harsh freezer conditions. Worse yet, when it comes to custom printing, many fear the high costs, long lead times, or environmental impact of traditional ink and plate technologies.

So how do you create standout, freezer-safe packaging without breaking the bank or compromising on quality and sustainability?

Digitally Printed Pouches with ArrowJet Water-Based Pigment Inks

In this guide, we’ll walk you through everything you need to know about custom-printed frozen food pouches—from beginner basics to advanced considerations—with a special focus on digital printing using ArrowJet’s single-pass water-based pigment ink technology. Whether you’re a startup exploring your first frozen product or a seasoned brand looking to scale up sustainably, this blog is for you.

 

Factor

Moisture Resistance

Freezer Compatibility

Must test at -18°C or lower

Ink Adhesion

Food Safety

Durability

Test for smudging, abrasion, frost exposure

 

1. Why Frozen Food Brands Are Betting Big on Pouches

Flexible pouches are dominating freezer shelves for a few simple reasons:

  • Space-saving: They take up less space than rigid containers.
  • Lightweight: Lower shipping costs and less waste.
  • Highly customizable: Ideal for eye-catching designs and storytelling.
  • Consumer-friendly: Easy to open, reseal, and store.

Brands like Daily Harvest, Tattooed Chef, and Amy’s Kitchen use high-quality, custom-printed pouches to stand out in a highly competitive market. They’re not just protecting the food—they’re telling a story.

2. What Makes Frozen Food Packaging Unique?

Frozen food packaging has to do more than just look good. It must:

  • Withstand temperatures as low as -20°C
  • Resist moisture, frost, and condensation
  • Retain structural integrity when stacked or dropped
  • Maintain print quality through shipping, storage, and use

Choosing the wrong materials or printing method can result in cracking, fading, or even food spoilage. That’s why this isn’t just about looking good—it’s about preserving product quality and consumer trust.

3. Why Digital Printing is a Game-Changer

Traditionally, printing on flexible packaging required long setup times, high MOQ (minimum order quantities), and expensive printing plates. Digital printing eliminates these bottlenecks by offering:

  • Short runs and fast turnarounds
  • High-resolution, full-color graphics
  • Variable data printing (VDP) for batch codes, languages, promotions
  • On-demand scalability as you grow your product line

But here’s where it gets better.

4. Enter ArrowJet: Water-Based Inks Made for the Freezer

Explore More

Arrow Systems Inc. has introduced a revolutionary solution with its ArrowJet product line, powered by single-pass water-based pigment ink technology. Here’s why this matters for frozen food packaging:

a. Eco-Friendly and Food Safe

ArrowJet inks are water-based and meet stringent food-packaging compliance requirements, making them ideal for indirect food contact.

b. Moisture and Cold Resistant

Unlike dye-based or solvent inks, ArrowJet’s pigment inks are naturally resistant to moisture and UV degradation, making them perfect for cold chain environments.

c. High Durability and Print Quality

These inks bond well with freezer-grade films and produce vivid, long-lasting prints that won’t smear or fade—even in frosty, wet conditions.

d. No Need for Plates

Short-run? No problem. You can print different SKUs, promotional designs, or languages without needing to invest in multiple plates.

5. Choosing the Right Pouch Material

Material choice is crucial for print compatibility and freezer performance. Recommended structures include:

  • PET/PE or PET/LLDPE: Great for general frozen foods
  • Nylon-based laminates: Ideal for puncture resistance (e.g., meat or dense foods)
  • Mono-materials: For brands focused on recyclability

ArrowJet printing systems work seamlessly with pre-treated films optimized for ink adhesion and lamination.

6. Lamination: The Unsung Hero

Even the best water-based pigment ink needs protection in cold, moist environments. Lamination adds:

  • Moisture and abrasion resistance
  • A premium matte or gloss finish
  • Structural support for sealing and stacking

Ask your converter about lamination options that are compatible with water-based ink systems.

7. Design Tips for Frozen Food Pouches

  • Use bold, high-contrast colors for visibility in fogged freezer doors
  • Keep text legible at small sizes
  • Include cooking instructions, QR codes, and certifications
  • Highlight sustainability claims with icons or infographics
  • Opt for resealable zippers if your product is multi-serve

8. Common Pitfalls to Avoid

  • Using untreated film: Can cause ink adhesion failures
  • Skipping lamination: Leads to smudging and fading
  • Overdesigning: Can confuse consumers; keep it simple and strong
  • Ignoring real-world testing: Always do a freeze/thaw test before scaling

9. Industry Insights: What the Leaders Are Doing

Big brands are investing in sustainable, small-batch, and direct-to-consumer packaging strategies. Many are turning to digital printing to support:

  • Localized versions of products (language, region-specific branding)
  • Seasonal campaigns without long lead times
  • Market testing for new SKUs or flavors

ArrowJet technology allows you to tap into this trend without massive investment.

10. How to Get Started with ArrowJet Digital Printing

Here’s a simple roadmap:

  1. Define your pouch format and size
  2. Choose a suitable substrate (consult with Arrow Systems or your converter)
  3. Create high-resolution artwork in CMYK
  4. Request print samples with ArrowJet water-based inks
  5. Run freezer simulations and QA tests
  6. Launch with confidence!

Future-Proof Your Frozen Food Packaging

The frozen food industry is only getting colder—but your brand can heat up with the right packaging strategy. Digitally printed, water-based pigment ink pouches are no longer a luxury—they’re a smart, scalable solution that meets modern expectations for quality, sustainability, and speed.

With ArrowJet single-pass water-based pigment ink technology, you get it all: brilliant color, freezer-safe durability, and the flexibility to grow.

Choosing the Right Supplement Packaging: Top 6 Types You Must Know in 2025

Introduction: The First Impression Can Make or Break Your Brand

Let’s be honest—when someone picks up a supplement bottle, they’re not just looking at the ingredient list. They’re absorbing everything—the design, the feel, the trustworthiness it exudes. In an industry where competition is fierce and consumer skepticism is high, your packaging becomes more than a container. It’s the first impression, your brand’s handshake, and often, the deciding factor in a purchase.

If you’re in the health and wellness space, whether launching a new product or scaling an existing line, packaging deserves your full attention. In this blog, we’ll explore six proven packaging formats that are dominating the supplement market in 2025—and help you decide which one fits your brand best.

1. Plastic Bottles: A Timeless Classic That Still Works

Plastic bottles—specifically HDPE and PET—remain a staple in the supplement world. And for good reason. They’re sturdy, cost-effective, and easy to customize. Whether you’re packaging capsules, tablets, softgels, or chewable gummies, plastic bottles provide a secure, tamper-evident format that consumers trust.

They’re also ideal for high-volume production and shelf storage. If you’re just starting out or aiming for mass retail distribution, plastic bottles offer that balance between functionality and affordability. You can add features like child-resistant caps or UV-protective finishes depending on your target audience.

2. Glass Bottles: Elevating Your Brand with a Premium Touch

There’s something about glass that communicates purity and quality. If your supplement contains oil-based ingredients, herbal extracts, or sensitive compounds, glass is not only elegant—it’s functional. Amber and cobalt glass provide UV protection, preserving potency and shelf life.

Beyond function, glass packaging taps into the growing demand for eco-conscious branding. Customers who care about sustainability often perceive glass as more environmentally responsible than plastic. For brands in the premium or organic space, glass bottles make a strong statement.

3. Stand-Up Pouches: The Future of Flexible Packaging

As e-commerce continues to boom, more supplement brands are turning to flexible packaging like stand-up pouches. They’re lightweight, space-saving, and resealable—perfect for powdered supplements, gummies, and superfoods.

Not only do they perform well during shipping, but they also provide ample space for bold branding and regulatory labeling. Custom finishes such as matte laminates or soft-touch textures can elevate the tactile experience. For startups and direct-to-consumer brands, stand-up pouches strike a balance between innovation and practicality.

4. Blister Packs: Clinical Precision with Added Convenience

Blister packs are widely used in pharmaceuticals, and they’re making waves in the supplement industry too—especially for daily-use tablets or travel-sized formats. They’re hygienic, tamper-evident, and offer a clear visual cue for dosage tracking.

This format is particularly effective when you want to reinforce structure and consistency. For example, vitamin regimens, probiotic courses, or multiday supplement packs benefit from the daily-slot style that blister packs provide. They’re compact, portable, and ideal for both sample kits and full-size offerings.

5. Stick Packs and Sachets: Designed for Life on the Go

In today’s fast-paced world, convenience often drives customer loyalty. Stick packs and sachets are single-serve powerhouses, perfect for powdered supplements, hydration mixes, and vitamin-infused drink powders.

Consumers love the ease of tearing one open, pouring it into water, and getting their dose—no scooping, no measuring, no mess. From a branding standpoint, they also double as excellent samples or trial formats to introduce new customers to your product. If your brand caters to athletes, travelers, or busy professionals, this is one format you can’t overlook.

6. Dropper Bottles: Small, Powerful, and Precise

For liquid supplements like tinctures, herbal drops, and CBD oils, dropper bottles offer control and class. They’re typically made of glass and come with a dropper cap that makes dosing easy and consistent.

This format appeals to a growing segment of users who prefer sublingual delivery or liquid alternatives to pills. It’s also a favorite in the holistic health and natural wellness space, where minimalism and perceived purity go hand in hand. Dropper bottles may not hold much, but they deliver a strong brand message when done right.

Bonus: Things to Consider Before You Choose

The perfect packaging format depends on more than just the product itself. Consider your customer’s lifestyle, your brand identity, and your supply chain. Ask yourself:

  • Is this packaging travel-friendly and tamper-proof?
  • Does it align with my sustainability goals?
  • Will it preserve the product’s shelf life and potency?
  • Is there enough space for mandatory labeling and branding?
  • How will it perform during shipping and storage?

Packaging is where design meets science—and getting it right means more loyal customers and fewer returns.

Final Thoughts: Let Your Packaging Speak Before You Do

In 2025, supplement packaging is more than a vessel. It’s a brand experience, a promise of quality, and a reflection of your mission. The right packaging not only protects your product but also builds trust with the people who use it.

So, take the time to choose packaging that reflects your values and meets your customer’s expectations. Because when your supplement looks as good as it works, you don’t just sell—you inspire confidence.

In the evolving landscape of dietary supplements, packaging plays a pivotal role in product success. For supplement manufacturers, understanding market dynamics and consumer preferences is essential. Here are some key data points and statistics to guide strategic packaging decisions:

Market Growth and Trends:

  • Expanding Market: The global dietary supplement packaging market was valued at USD 12.7 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach USD 23.1 billion by 2034, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 6.1% from 2025 to 2034.
  • Nutraceutical Packaging Surge: The nutraceutical packaging market is anticipated to grow from USD 3.73 billion in 2024 to USD 6.09 billion by 2034, reflecting a CAGR of 5.1%.

Consumer Preferences:

Why Water-Based Pigment Inks Are the Future of Sustainable Packaging

Introduction: The Ink Behind the Impact

When we talk about sustainable packaging, we often focus on materials—biodegradable films, recyclable cartons, or compostable pouches. But there’s an equally important element hiding in plain sight: the ink.

Inks are not just colors on a label. They influence recyclability, food safety, and even regulatory compliance. As more brands move toward eco-conscious packaging, the spotlight is now turning to water-based pigment inks—a technology quickly gaining ground for its environmental, functional, and commercial benefits.

In this article, we’ll explore why water-based pigment inks are being hailed as the future of sustainable packaging, how they compare to traditional inks, and why packaging converters and brands should care.

What Are Water-Based Pigment Inks?

Water-based pigment inks use water as the primary solvent instead of petroleum-based solvents or reactive chemicals. They contain color pigments suspended in water and stabilizers, and are known for their excellent durability and colorfastness.

Unlike dye-based inks that soak into the substrate, pigment inks sit on the surface, making them more resistant to light, moisture, and chemicals—ideal for packaging that needs to last through shipping, shelving, and handling.

Why Sustainability Leaders Are Switching to Water-Based Inks

1. Low Environmental Impact

Solvent and UV inks release Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) during curing or drying, which contribute to air pollution and pose health risks in production environments. Water-based inks drastically reduce VOC emissions and eliminate the need for UV curing systems that consume high energy.

According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), water-based inks can reduce VOC emissions by up to 90% compared to solvent-based inks.

2. Safe for Food and Pharma Applications

In industries like food, beverage, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals, ink safety is critical. Water-based pigment inks are often formulated to comply with Nestlé and Swiss Ordinance packaging standards, making them ideal for indirect food contact and primary packaging in regulated industries.

Brands looking to meet FDA, EU, or REACH regulations are increasingly turning to compliant water-based solutions that align with health and safety expectations.

3. Better for Recyclability

Traditional inks can contaminate recyclable packaging, especially when they contain heavy metals or solvent residues. Water-based pigment inks contain no hazardous air pollutants (HAPs) and are designed to minimize ink migration, making them far more compatible with paper, board, and film recycling streams.

As Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations continue to gain momentum globally, using inks that don’t compromise recyclability is becoming essential.

Performance Matters: Do Water-Based Pigment Inks Hold Up?

The biggest concern with water-based inks used to be print quality and durability—especially on non-porous surfaces. But those days are long gone.

Thanks to advancements in printhead technology and ink chemistry, modern water-based pigment inks deliver:

  • High-resolution print quality (up to 1600 x 1600 dpi)
  • Excellent rub and water resistance
  • Fade-resistant colors suitable for retail packaging
  • Compatibility with various substrates, including flexible films and synthetic materials

Leading digital presses like the ArrowJet Aqua 330R and ArrowJet Bolt now feature water-based pigment ink systems that meet the rigorous demands of short-run label and flexible packaging production—without compromising on performance.

Explore More
Explore More

Cost Efficiency and Operational Benefits

Switching to water-based pigment inks can also lower operational costs:

  • No need for UV curing units, reducing energy bills
  • Lower health and safety risks, which cuts insurance and compliance costs
  • Simplified clean-up and maintenance, thanks to non-toxic formulations

And with growing pressure from consumers and retailers alike, sustainability is no longer a “nice-to-have”—it’s a market requirement. Brands that adopt greener ink solutions gain a competitive edge in bidding for eco-conscious product lines.

Real-World Adoption: Who’s Making the Switch?

Global brands like Nestlé, Unilever, and P&G have committed to making all packaging recyclable or reusable by 2025. Ink selection is part of that equation. According to a 2023 report by Future Market Insights, the Global market for water-based inks is projected to grow at a CAGR of 6.3% from 2024 to 2030, outpacing other ink technologies.

In addition, small and mid-sized brands in the DTC and organic product space are actively seeking sustainable partners. Offering water-based ink solutions isn’t just an environmental decision—it’s a business one.

Why ArrowJet Solutions Lead the Way

At the forefront of this transformation is ArrowJet’s water-based pigment ink technology. Designed for high-performance label and flexible packaging applications, ArrowJet presses offer:

  • ArrowJet Bolt: A blazing-fast, single-pass inkjet press with speeds up to 150 m/min, delivering vibrant, high-resolution prints using Nestlé-compliant water-based pigment inks.
  • ArrowJet Aqua Series: Includes the Aqua 330R and Aqua 800M—ideal for flexible packaging, pouch printing, and short-run jobs with no compromise on compliance or quality.
  • Full modularity: Options for inline priming, varnishing, and finishing allow converters to create end-to-end sustainable workflows.

ArrowJet systems empower packaging converters to meet sustainability goals without sacrificing speed, color, or versatility—a true win-win in a demanding marketplace.

Explore More

Conclusion: It’s Time to Rethink What’s in Your Ink

As brands race toward sustainability and governments tighten regulations, it’s clear: the ink you use matters.

Water-based pigment inks represent the next chapter in responsible packaging. They’re safer, cleaner, and ready for high-performance applications across food, pharma, personal care, and beyond. Combined with cutting-edge digital printers like the ArrowJet Bolt, they offer a smarter way to future-proof your packaging business.

If you’re serious about sustainability, it’s time to look past the substrate and rethink what’s in your ink.

title.rendered: How to Automate Label Production in 2025 Without Breaking the Bank

Table of Contents

How to Automate Label Production in 2025 Without Breaking the Bank

Still relying on manual label production in 2025? You might be losing more money than you think.

With rising demand for short-run, customized labels and flexible packaging, brands and converters alike are feeling the pressure to deliver faster and cheaper—without compromising on quality. But automation often sounds expensive.

Here’s the good news: label production automation in 2025 doesn’t have to cost a fortune. With smarter tech, modular digital systems, and streamlined workflows, even small businesses can scale operations without burning through capital.

In this post, we’ll explore affordable ways to automate label production, whether you’re a growing brand or a print service provider looking to boost efficiency.

Why Automate Label Production in the First Place?

Before diving into the how, let’s quickly talk about the why. Traditional Label production is often slow, wasteful, and limited in flexibility. Whether it’s setting up plates, managing changeovers, or dealing with inventory storage, the process eats up valuable time and resources.

By contrast, automating your label workflow allows you to:

  • Deliver labels faster with consistent quality
  • Minimize human error and reduce labor costs
  • Handle short runs and customized jobs with ease
  • Improve profitability on every label you print

And perhaps most importantly, it gives you complete control over your production timeline—a game-changer in industries where speed and responsiveness are critical.

1. Choose the Right Digital Label Printer (Affordability Meets Performance)

One of the biggest myths in print production is that digital printers are too expensive to justify unless you’re running massive volumes. That may have been true years ago, but not in 2025.

Today’s digital label printers are compact, efficient, and surprisingly affordable—especially for brands or converters dealing with short runs or frequent design changes.

When selecting a digital label printer that won’t break the bank, look for these key features:

  • High resolution (ideally 1600 x 1600 dpi) for sharp, vibrant labels
  • Water-based pigment inks that are safe for food, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals
  • Low setup time and no plate costs, perfect for on-demand and custom printing
  • Media flexibility, allowing you to print on different types of substrates

One standout option is the ArrowJet Aqua 330R, a compact single-pass digital inkjet printer built for businesses that want to bring production in-house. It offers exceptional print quality, uses Nestlé-compliant water-based inks, and supports a wide range of label applications—all at a fraction of the cost of traditional label presses.

Explore More

2. Add a Modular Digital Finisher to Complete the Workflow

Printing is just the beginning. To fully automate, you’ll need a finishing system that can laminate, cut, slit, and rewind your labels efficiently.

Gone are the days when finishing equipment required large capital investment and complex die-cut setups. Modern digital finishers are modular, compact, and designed to work seamlessly with digital printers—meaning no tooling, no dies, and minimal waste.

Here’s what to look for in a digital label finisher:

  • Ability to perform lamination, slitting, and die-less cutting
  • Compatibility with multiple media types and roll sizes
  • Barcode scanning for automatic job recognition and switching
  • Integration with your printer for a smoother workflow

A great budget-conscious option is the Arrow EZCut 350R. It’s user-friendly, compact, and includes everything you need for finishing labels after printing—making it an ideal step toward full automation.

Explore More

3. Explore Inline Print-and-Cut Solutions for Maximum Efficiency

If you’re aiming for peak productivity with minimal touchpoints, inline print-and-cut systems are your best bet. These all-in-one machines combine printing and finishing into a single pass, allowing you to produce labels that are printed, cut, and ready to apply without manual intervention between stages.

These systems dramatically reduce production time, eliminate the need for separate operators or machines, and reduce errors. They’re also ideal for handling multiple SKUs or versions of the same product packaging—common scenarios in food, beverage, and health industries.

The ArrowJet Nova 250R, for example, is a compact inline system that offers high-resolution CMYK printing and laser die-cutting all in one unit. It’s designed for converters and businesses looking to streamline operations, cut waste, and speed up turnaround—all while maintaining top-tier print quality.

Explore More

4. Don’t Overlook Workflow Automation Software

While hardware handles the physical side of automation, software takes care of the digital flow—and the two should work hand-in-hand.

Modern workflow software lets you:

  • Accept online orders via web-to-print portals
  • Manage and track job tickets automatically
  • Batch similar jobs to reduce downtime
  • Control color consistency and RIP files efficiently

Many new digital label printers and finishers come with integrated workflow solutions, reducing the need for expensive third-party systems. Make sure the software is scalable, user-friendly, and capable of integrating with your sales and inventory systems.

In short, software acts as the brain behind your automated production—saving time, avoiding confusion, and improving accuracy from file to finish.

5. Take a Phased Approach: Start Small and Scale Wisely

It’s tempting to think automation requires a complete overhaul. The truth is, most successful businesses take a modular approach, starting with their most pressing pain points and building from there.

Here’s a smart automation roadmap:

  • Phase 1: Invest in a cost-effective digital label printer to bring printing in-house.
  • Phase 2: Add a modular digital finisher for lamination, slitting, and cutting.
  • Phase 3: Upgrade to an inline print-and-cut solution as volumes increase.
  • Phase 4: Integrate automation software to tie everything together.

you avoid large upfront costs while still moving steadily toward full automation.

6. Reduce Inventory and Waste with On-Demand Printing

One of the often-overlooked benefits of label automation is the ability to print exactly what you need, when you need it. On-demand printing eliminates the need to stockpile pre-printed labels, which can expire, become outdated, or take up valuable warehouse space.

Instead of ordering thousands of labels per SKU, you can produce short runs based on real-time demand. This is especially valuable for seasonal products, limited editions, or brands with frequently changing artwork and compliance requirements.

Final Thoughts: Affordable Automation is Within Reach

In 2025, automating your label production doesn’t require massive budgets or industrial-scale operations. With the right digital printer, modular finishing solutions, and workflow software, any business can improve productivity, reduce costs, and deliver better labels faster.

Whether you’re a brand looking to bring printing in-house or a print shop wanting to expand your capabilities, it’s time to take advantage of the technology that makes automation affordable, scalable, and incredibly efficient.

We help businesses of all sizes find the perfect digital printing and finishing solutions. If you’re ready to streamline your label production and reduce your overhead, let’s talk.

Sustainable Inks & Packaging: What the Food & Pharma Industry Must Know

The Cost of Progress? Not Anymore.

Every product label, every blister pack, every flexible pouch—has a story. But behind the eye-catching colors and tamper-proof packaging lies a hidden truth: traditional printing and packaging materials are damaging our planet.

In an era where climate change, consumer awareness, and strict global regulations dominate industry headlines, the food and pharmaceutical sectors face a pivotal choice. Do they continue with legacy packaging systems that are wasteful and hazardous—or pivot toward a more responsible, future-proof solution?

If you’re in the food or pharma business, this blog will unpack the urgent need for sustainable inks and packaging, the technologies leading the change, and how this shift isn’t just better for the environment—but better for your bottom line, too.

Why Sustainability Matters More Than Ever

From farm to fork, and lab to label—sustainability isn’t a buzzword anymore. It’s a requirement.

Today’s consumers are hyper-aware. They scan QR codes. They read the fine print. They care about carbon footprints, recyclability, and health compliance. And regulators? They’re tightening the screws. Governments across the globe, especially in Europe and North America, are enforcing sustainability standards around food safety, pharmaceutical compliance, and environmental impact.

Failing to comply isn’t just a bad look—it can mean fines, product recalls, and damaged brand trust.

The Real Impact of Conventional Inks & Packaging

Let’s be clear—most conventional inks are chemical-heavy, containing volatile organic compounds (VOCs), heavy metals, and petroleum derivatives. These toxins don’t just pollute air and water—they linger in packaging, potentially leaching into food or medicine if the barrier is compromised.

Likewise, plastic-based multilayer packaging is rarely recyclable and contributes significantly to landfill and marine waste. Worse, improper disposal in developing markets amplifies global ecological imbalance.

The question isn’t “Should we switch?”—it’s “How soon can we?”

Enter: Sustainable Inks – The Game Changer

What Are Sustainable Inks?

Sustainable inks are formulated with bio-based, renewable or non-toxic ingredients, reducing environmental harm and supporting circular production processes. Some of the most common include:

  • Water-based pigment inks
  • Vegetable or soy-based inks
  • UV-curable inks (low migration)
  • Compostable and biodegradable ink systems

But not all sustainable inks are created equal. For food and pharma sectors, compliance is non-negotiable.

What Makes Inks “Food & Pharma Safe”?

To be compliant, inks must meet strict international standards such as:

  • Nestlé Guidance Note on Packaging Inks
  • Swiss Ordinance on Materials and Articles (SR 817.023.21)
  • EU Framework Regulation (EC) No. 1935/2004
  • FDA 21 CFR Regulations

One standout option is water-based pigment ink technology, such as Memjet’s DuraFlex® systems, which comply with these health and safety guidelines. These inks offer vibrant color, high durability, and safety for indirect food contact packaging—making them ideal for flexible films, blister foils, cartons, and pouches.

The Shift to Eco-Friendly Packaging Materials

Switching to sustainable inks is just half the solution. Your packaging material matters just as much.

What Defines Sustainable Packaging?

To be considered sustainable, packaging should be:

  • Recyclable or compostable
  • Made from renewable sources
  • Lightweight yet protective
  • Compatible with sustainable ink systems

Common sustainable substrates include:

  • Recyclable films (PET, PP) with mono-material structure
  • Compostable cellulose-based films
  • Sugarcane paper or bagasse-based packaging
  • Bio-PE and PLA laminates

These digitally printable substrates that work seamlessly with water-based pigment inks, brands can reduce their carbon footprint without compromising print quality or compliance.

The Business Benefits Are Just as Big

Lower Inventory. Higher Customization.

Sustainable digital printing allows food and pharma brands to print short runs with no minimum order quantities. That means less waste, faster turnaround, and localized packaging.

Variable Data & Security Printing

From lot numbers to expiry dates to anti-counterfeiting QR codes—digital systems with sustainable inks can print variable data in a single pass. For the pharma industry, that’s a huge plus for compliance and patient safety.

Reduced Downtime and Faster Time-to-Market

With digital sustainable print systems, brands no longer need to wait weeks for offset plate setups or massive print runs. Instead, new SKUs, seasonal designs, and multilingual packs can be launched within days.

What Brands Should Look for in a Printing System

Making the switch to sustainable printing isn’t just about swapping out inks. It’s about choosing the right printing ecosystem.

Here’s a checklist:

Food- and Pharma-Safe Inks: Make sure they meet global compliance standards.
High Resolution: Look for systems offering 1600 x 1600 dpi for premium shelf appeal.
Speed & Versatility: At least 90 ft/min or higher for industrial-scale short-run jobs.
Modular & Scalable Design: So you can integrate inline varnishers, laminators, and slitters.
Compatible with Eco-Substrates: To ensure full packaging sustainability.

One such solution is the ArrowJet Aqua 330R, a sustainable digital pigment inkjet printer built specifically for food and pharma applications. It prints with Nestlé-compliant inks at blazing speeds and handles flexible packaging, cartons, and even blister foils.

Explore More

Real-World Use Cases: Food & Pharma Going Green

Pharma Example: Blister Foil Printing with Compliance

A leading nutraceutical brand recently transitioned from solvent-based gravure printing to a digital water-based pigment ink system. The result?

  • Reduced production waste by 45%
  • Eliminated VOC emissions from the line
  • Achieved faster launches of new SKUs and formulations

Food Example: Flexible Pouches for Health Snacks

An organic snack company embraced sustainable inks and packaging for its on-the-go pouches. With short-run digital production, they now offer:

  • Custom labels per region and language
  • Seasonal limited-edition packs
  • 100% recyclable packaging without compromising on vibrant print quality

The Future is Circular—and You Should Be, Too

The linear model—take, make, waste—is obsolete.

The food and pharmaceutical industries are moving toward a circular economy. That means materials stay in use longer, waste becomes a resource, and consumers become co-creators in sustainability.

Brands adopting sustainable inks and digital packaging systems, does more than meet regulations—you build trust, credibility, and long-term resilience.

Final Thoughts: It’s Not Just Ink on Paper Anymore

Choosing the right ink and packaging material is no longer just a design or cost decision. It’s a strategic one.

For the food and pharma industries, sustainability is about more than optics. It’s about compliance, innovation, and responsibility. And with new-generation printing solutions now readily available, there are no more excuses.

If you’re still printing with VOC-laden inks or sitting on piles of outdated pre-printed packaging—it’s time for a change.

Print smarter. Pack greener. And future-proof your brand—one label at a time.

Table of Contents

7 Questions to Ask Before Investing in a New Label Printer

Did you know that 67% of converters say short-run jobs now make up over half of their label business?
 With SKU proliferation, seasonal promotions, and consumer personalization, investing in the right label printer isn’t just smart—it’s essential.

Whether you’re a growing label converter, a food and beverage brand, or a pharma manufacturer, choosing the right label printing solution can make or break your operational efficiency, profit margins, and product presentation.

We help brands and converters make informed, future-ready choices in Digital printing. If you’re exploring new technology, here are 7 key questions you must ask before making the investment.

1. What Are Your Labeling Requirements—Today and Tomorrow?

Before even looking at models, define your label output:

  • Are you printing product labels, compliance labels, or luxury labels?
  • How many SKUs are in your portfolio? Is your product line expanding?
  • Do you need short-run, variable data, or just-in-time printing capabilities?
  • Are your labels used in harsh environments (e.g., chemicals, outdoor, frozen goods)?

For example, pharmaceutical brands require precision, traceability, and microtext for anti-counterfeiting, while food and beverage brands need inks that are food-safe and compliant with regulations like Nestlé Guidance or Swiss Ordinance.

This is where water-based pigment inks shine. Not only do they offer high resolution for microtext and fine detailing, but when they’re Swiss-compliant, they also meet global safety standards—essential for packaging that comes in direct or indirect contact with consumables.

Tip: If your answer includes “high customization,” “short runs,” or “regulatory compliance,” you’re in digital label territory—and ArrowJet’s aqueous pigment printers are built for just that.

2. What Printing Technology Best Aligns With Your Use Case?

There are several technologies available—each with pros and trade-offs:

  • Inkjet (Aqueous Pigment): Vibrant colors, safe for food and pharma, and great for micro-detailing like batch coding, QR codes, and microtext security printing.
  • Thermal Transfer: Durable but often slower and better for basic black text labels.
  • Laser and LED: Sharp output, but may struggle with certain substrates or higher operational costs.

Our water-based pigment inkjet technology isn’t just about image quality—it’s about compliance, safety, and versatility. Our systems utilize Nestlé-compliant and Swiss Ordinance-compliant inks, ideal for highly regulated industries such as pharmaceuticals, nutraceuticals, infant nutrition, and ready-to-eat foods.

Recommended: If you operate in food, pharma, cosmetics, or supplements, ArrowJet Aqua 330R or ArrowJet Aqua 800M ensure your print meets both regulatory standards and commercial appeal.

Explore More
Explore More

3. What Is the True Cost of Ownership?

Don’t let a low upfront cost fool you.

Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) includes:

  • Ink or ribbon costs
  • Maintenance and downtime
  • Waste and media loss during job changeovers
  • Energy efficiency
  • Software licenses

Let’s say you’re printing 500,000 labels/month—ink savings alone can amount to thousands over a year. Printers with bulk ink systems, like the ArrowJet Nova 250R, drastically lower cost-per-label compared to cartridge-based systems.

Ask your supplier for a cost-per-label comparison, including consumables and service contracts.

4. Is It Compatible With Your Current Workflow?

This is where many investments fall short.

Ask:

  • Does it integrate with your label design software (e.g., BarTender, NiceLabel)?
  • Can it connect with your ERP, MIS, or WMS systems?
  • Does it support automated job queues, variable data, or inline finishing?

Converters love our modular print-and-cut solutions, such as the ArrowJet Nova 330R, which can seamlessly sync with existing production lines—while brands benefit from web-to-print and SKU versioning tools.

Scalability and automation are key. A good printer should adapt to your growth, not restrict it.

5. Are You Getting the Right Speed & Resolution for Your Business?

Don’t compromise here.

  • High-resolution (up to 1600 x 1600 dpi) is critical for beauty, wine, or nutraceutical products where visual branding impacts purchase.
  • High-speed (e.g., 27-45 m/min or more) is non-negotiable if you’re dealing with 1000s of labels per SKU.

ArrowJet Hybrid Pro M and ArrowJet Bolt are built to deliver both: blazing speed and precision for high-volume jobs and vivid branding.

Match speed to your daily output and resolution to your brand image. Don’t settle for less.

6. Can It Handle the Media and Label Types You Use?

Today’s packaging is complex: gloss, matte, synthetics, foils, laminates. Your printer must:

  • Handle a wide media range (e.g., PET, PP, paper, eco-friendly films)
  • Print on flexible packaging substrates
  • Offer unlimited label length and width flexibility
  • Support inline lamination, varnish, or die-cutting if needed

Arrow’s solutions like the EZCut 350R and Aqua 330R are built for adaptability. With modular design, you can add finishing, slitting, or drying modules as your needs evolve.

If you’re limited by SKUs or packaging formats today, choose a printer that frees you—not one that boxes you in.

Explore More
Explore More

7. What Support and Warranty Options Are in Place?

This is your safety net. Consider:

  • On-site or remote tech support availability
  • Access to local service technicians
  • Training programs for your team
  • Warranty length and coverage for critical components

Arrow Systems doesn’t just sell hardware—we partner with you. Our USA-based support and global service network ensures you’ll never be left hanging during a production crisis.

Remember: Downtime is cost. The right service support = peace of mind + consistent output.

Final Thoughts: The Right Label Printer Is a Growth Engine

Investing in a digital label printer is more than a capital expenditure—it’s a strategic move toward:

  • Lower operating costs
  • Reduced lead times
  • Unlimited SKU flexibility
  • Sustainable, compliant packaging
  • Higher brand value through print quality

We’ve helped converters and brands across the globe—from startups to Fortune 500s—transform their operations with our ArrowJet Series, EZCut Finishers and Limitronics

Ready to Take the Next Step?

Whether you’re looking for a short-run digital label printer, a modular print-and-cut solution, or a full-fledged flexible packaging printer, our team is here to help you evaluate what’s right for your goals.

Contact Arrow Systems, Inc. today and let’s find the printer that matches your future—not just your present.

Arrow EZCut 350R vs Arrow EZCut 330R: Why You Should Upgrade Today

Introduction: Choosing the Right Label Finisher for Your Business

When it comes to digital label finishing, efficiency, accuracy, and automation are the three pillars that determine success. The right finishing solution can make all the difference in reducing production time, minimizing waste, and improving quality.

For years, the Arrow EZCut 330R has been a trusted solution in the label finishing industry, offering reliable performance. But as the demand for faster, more precise, and automated solutions grows, the Arrow EZCut 350R has emerged as the next-generation digital label finisher, built to tackle modern production challenges.

This in-depth comparison highlights how the EZCut 350R outperforms the EZCut 330R and why upgrading is a smart investment for businesses looking to streamline operations and boost productivity.

Key Differences Between the Arrow EZCut 350R and EZCut 330R

Let’s break down the major differences between these two models and understand what makes the EZCut 350R the superior choice.

Speed: 50% Faster for Maximum Efficiency

Speed is crucial in label finishing. The EZCut 330R operates at standard speeds, which may work well for moderate production volumes. However, as demand increases, slow speeds can create bottlenecks.

The EZCut 350R is designed for high-speed performance, offering a 50% increase in speed compared to the 330R. This upgrade enables businesses to handle more jobs in less time, resulting in higher efficiency, lower costs, and improved turnaround times.

If your goal is to increase daily production without compromising quality, the EZCut 350R is the perfect solution.

Automatic Job Change: No More Manual Adjustments

The EZCut 330R requires manual job changes, meaning operators have to stop production, adjust settings, and restart the process for each new job. This is not only time-consuming but also increases the risk of errors.

With the EZCut 350R, job changes are fully automated. This means your machine can transition from one job to the next seamlessly, reducing downtime and allowing for a smoother, more efficient workflow.

Automation also reduces operator dependency, making it easier to scale operations without needing additional manpower.

Auto Knife Placement: Precision Without Hassle

Manually adjusting knives for different cutting needs can be a tedious process. The EZCut 330R requires manual knife placement, which is time-intensive and prone to alignment issues.

The EZCut 350R eliminates this hassle with an automatic knife placement system. This ensures that each job is executed with pinpoint accuracy, minimizing material waste and reducing human error.

For businesses handling intricate designs and complex label shapes, this feature alone makes the EZCut 350R a must-have upgrade.

Inline Web Guide: Perfect Alignment Every Time

One common challenge in label finishing is maintaining perfect alignment, especially for long runs or complex designs.

The EZCut 330R does not come with an inline web guide, which means any misalignment can lead to wasted materials and inconsistent results.

The EZCut 350R, however, features an inline web guide that ensures perfect alignment throughout the finishing process. This upgrade improves cutting precision, enhances print registration, and reduces material waste, saving businesses both time and money.

Upgraded Cutting Software: Advanced Control and Customization

The EZCut 330R runs on basic cutting software, which gets the job done but may lack the flexibility needed for intricate or high-volume production.

The EZCut 350R is equipped with upgraded cutting software that offers better optimization, enhanced control, and more customization options.

With this advanced software, users can:

  • Fine-tune cutting parameters for different materials
  • Create custom cutting profiles for repeated jobs
  • Improve efficiency with automated adjustments

These features allow businesses to handle diverse label-finishing projects with greater precision and less effort.

Built-in CPU: Smarter, Faster Processing

A major difference between the two models is their processing capabilities.

The EZCut 330R relies on an external control unit, which can limit processing speed and create delays in execution.

In contrast, the EZCut 350R comes with a built-in CPU, allowing for faster processing, real-time job management, and better system reliability.

This improvement results in a smoother, more efficient workflow, making high-speed label finishing more reliable than ever.

Rotary Slitting Knives: A Game-Changer for Finishing

For businesses looking to enhance their label finishing capabilities, the rotary slitting knives in the EZCut 350R offer a significant advantage.

The EZCut 330R does not include rotary slitting knives, which limits its ability to handle certain cutting applications.

The EZCut 350R is designed with rotary slitting knives, improving cutting efficiency and accuracy while expanding the range of finishing options.

This feature is particularly beneficial for businesses working with high-volume label production, variable designs, and complex materials.

Why Should You Upgrade to the EZCut 350R?

The EZCut 330R is a solid entry-level digital finisher, but the EZCut 350R takes performance, efficiency, and automation to the next level.

Here’s why businesses should consider upgrading:

  1. Increased Productivity: Faster speeds mean more jobs completed in less time.
  2. Enhanced Automation: Automatic job change and knife placement reduce manual effort.
  3. Better Cutting Accuracy: The inline web guide ensures precise alignment.
  4. Smarter Operation: The built-in CPU processes jobs faster and more reliably.
  5. Expanded Finishing Capabilities: Rotary slitting knives allow for more complex cutting options.

For businesses focused on scaling operations, reducing waste, and improving workflow efficiency, the EZCut 350R is the ultimate investment.

Final Verdict: Is the EZCut 350R Worth It?

Without a doubt! The Arrow EZCut 350R is a significant upgrade over the EZCut 330R, offering faster speeds, automation, advanced cutting technology, and more efficient processing.

If your business is growing and you need a reliable, high-performance finishing solution, the EZCut 350R is the best choice.

Cost-Effective Solution for Industrial Label Printer

Are Your Labels Slowing Down Your Business? Here’s the Solution

Imagine this: You’re running a high-speed production line, fulfilling orders at full throttle, but then—everything slows to a crawl. The culprit? Your outdated or inefficient labeling system. Misprints, smudged barcodes, peeling labels, or slow output can disrupt the entire supply chain, leading to lost time, compliance issues, and frustrated customers.

If your labeling process isn’t as fast and reliable as the rest of your operations, you’re leaving money on the table.

In today’s fast-paced industrial world, precision and efficiency are everything. And that’s exactly why having the right industrial label printer isn’t just an option—it’s a necessity.

This blog will help you:

  • Understand the importance of industrial label printers in streamlining operations.
  • Discover key features to look for in a high-performance label printer.
  • Learn about the ArrowJet Line—a game-changer in digital label printing.
  • Explore industry trends, stats, and expert insights to stay ahead of the competition.

Let’s dive in and find out how upgrading your labeling process can save you time, reduce errors, and boost your bottom line!

The Backbone of Modern Industries: Industrial Label Printers

Imagine a bustling warehouse where thousands of products move in and out daily. Without proper labeling, chaos would ensue, leading to misplaced items, delayed shipments, and dissatisfied customers. Industrial label printers are the unsung heroes that prevent such scenarios. They produce durable labels that withstand harsh environments, ensuring seamless operations across various sectors, including manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, and retail.

Why Invest in an Industrial Label Printer?

  • Durability: Industrial environments can be harsh, with exposure to chemicals, moisture, and extreme temperatures. Industrial label printers produce labels that can withstand these conditions, ensuring longevity and readability.​
  • Efficiency: High-speed printing capabilities mean large volumes of labels can be produced quickly, keeping up with the demands of fast-paced operations
  • Accuracy: Advanced printing technologies ensure that barcodes, QR codes, and other critical information are printed clearly, reducing errors in scanning and tracking.​

title.rendered: The Power of Personalized Labels

content.rendered:
Table of Contents

The Power of Personalized Labels

Introduction to Personalized Labels

What Are Personalized Labels?

Personalized labels are custom-designed tags, stickers, or packaging elements tailored to represent a brand, product, or message. These labels often include unique designs, customer names, or specific details that resonate with the target audience.

Why Personalized Labels Matter in Branding

In today’s saturated Market, personalization is king. By leveraging custom labels, brands can create a stronger connection with consumers, making their products more memorable and desirable.

Benefits of Personalized Labels

Boosting Brand Recognition

A well-designed personalized label immediately grabs attention. Think of iconic brands whose labels you recognize instantly. That’s the power of personalization—it turns a product into a statement.

Enhancing Customer Experience

Personalized labels create a sense of exclusivity. When customers see their name or a unique message, it sparks joy and fosters loyalty.

Standing Out in a Competitive Market

Competition is fierce. Unique, visually appealing labels can be the deciding factor in whether a customer picks your product off the shelf or clicks “Add to Cart.”

Industries Leveraging Personalized Labels

Food and Beverage

Custom Wine and Beer Labels: Breweries and wineries often use personalized labels for limited editions or events, giving their products a premium feel.

Health and Beauty

Skincare and Cosmetic Packaging: Custom labels add a touch of luxury to beauty products, aligning with consumer demand for bespoke items.

E-Commerce and Retail

Subscription Boxes and Gift Wraps: Personalized labels elevate unboxing experiences, turning ordinary packaging into a delightful surprise.

Elements of Effective Personalized Labels

High-Quality Printing and Design

The visual and tactile quality of your label speaks volumes about your brand. Invest in professional printing to ensure your labels leave a lasting impression.

Choosing the Right Material

From glossy finishes to eco-friendly kraft paper, the material sets the tone for your product’s presentation.

Incorporating Branding Elements

Your logo, brand colors, and typography should be seamlessly integrated to maintain consistency and reinforce identity.

Technology Behind Personalized Labels

Digital Printing Innovations

Advanced digital printing technologies enable small-batch production of custom labels, reducing waste and costs.

Variable Data Printing (VDP)

This technology allows businesses to print different designs, names, or messages on each label, perfect for personalized campaigns.

Eco-Friendly Printing Options

Sustainability is crucial. Many brands now use biodegradable or recyclable materials for their labels.

Tips for Creating Personalized Labels

Understand Your Target Audience

Tailor your labels to your customers’ preferences. What appeals to them? What problems can your product solve?

Experiment with Colors and Fonts

Colors evoke emotions, and fonts set the tone. Choose wisely to create the desired impact.

Add a Touch of Interactivity

Consider QR codes, NFC tags, or AR elements to engage your customers in an innovative way.

Real-World Examples of Personalized Labels

Coca-Cola’s “Share a Coke” Campaign

This campaign replaced traditional labels with popular names, driving customer engagement and boosting sales worldwide.

Nutella’s Name Labels

Nutella allowed customers to order jars with their names on them, creating a buzz and increasing brand loyalty.

Etsy Sellers Creating Unique Packaging

Small businesses on Etsy use personalized labels to make their handmade products even more special.

Challenges in Implementing Personalized Labels

Cost and Resource Management

Custom labels can be expensive, especially for small businesses. Balancing quality with budget is key.

Maintaining Consistency Across Products

Consistency ensures your brand remains recognizable, even with diverse designs.

Avoiding Over-Complexity

Simplicity often works best. Overcomplicated designs can confuse or overwhelm customers.

The Future of Personalized Labels

AI-Driven Label Customization

AI tools are making it easier to create hyper-personalized labels based on consumer data.

Augmented Reality Integration

AR can turn a simple label into an immersive experience, connecting the physical product with the digital world.

Sustainable Innovations

The future of labels lies in eco-friendly materials and processes that cater to environmentally conscious consumers.

Conclusion

Personalized labels are more than just a decorative touch—they’re a powerful branding tool. By tapping into the emotional and practical needs of consumers, they can elevate your product and set you apart in a crowded market. Whether you’re a small business or a large corporation, personalized labels are worth the investment.

FAQs About Personalized Labels

1. What are personalized labels?

Personalized labels are custom-designed packaging elements tailored to reflect a brand’s identity and connect with its audience.

2. How can personalized labels benefit my small business?

They help increase brand visibility, foster customer loyalty, and differentiate your product in the market.

3. Are there eco-friendly options for personalized labels?

Yes, many printers offer biodegradable or recyclable materials and sustainable ink options.

4. What industries benefit most from personalized labels?

Industries like food and beverage, beauty, e-commerce, and retail see significant benefits from custom labels.

5. How do I start creating personalized labels for my brand?

Start by understanding your target audience, investing in quality design and materials, and leveraging digital printing technologies.

Trends in Food Label Printing: From Digital to Sustainable Solutions

Why Food Labels Matter More Than Ever

Food labels are no longer just a regulatory necessity; they have become a powerful branding tool that helps companies build trust and connect with consumers. In today’s competitive food industry, the right label design and material can make a significant impact on purchasing decisions. 

A well-crafted food label not only provides essential product information but also tells a brand’s story, highlighting its values, quality, and sustainability efforts. From minimalistic transparent labels to eco-friendly biodegradable options, food label printing is evolving rapidly to meet consumer demands for both aesthetics and responsibility.

As the demand for visually compelling and environmentally conscious packaging grows, brands are seeking innovative printing solutions that align with modern trends. The shift towards digital and sustainable food label printing is reshaping the market, allowing businesses to produce high-quality labels that cater to changing consumer expectations.

Let’s explore the latest developments in food label printing, the materials leading the way, and how cutting-edge technology is revolutionizing the industry.

Emerging Trends in Food Label Printing

The Rise of Eco-Friendly Food Labels

Sustainability has become a top priority for brands and consumers alike. More companies are investing in eco-friendly food labels, incorporating biodegradable and recyclable materials to reduce their environmental impact. 

According to industry reports, the sustainable packaging market is projected to grow by 7.6% annually through 2030, indicating a strong shift towards greener solutions. Consumers are becoming more conscious of their purchases, preferring brands that adopt sustainable practices. 

Using recyclable label materials and water-based inks not only reduces waste but also strengthens a brand’s commitment to responsible production.

Digital Printing for Food Labels

The Digital label printing market is experiencing rapid growth, with an estimated increase of $2.32 billion between 2023 and 2028. Digital printing allows brands to produce food labels with greater flexibility, enabling quick turnarounds, cost-effective short runs, and high-quality printing. 

Unlike traditional printing methods, digital printing makes it easy to customize labels for multiple SKUs without the need for expensive plates or extensive setup times. It also supports variable data printing, allowing brands to add batch numbers, expiration dates, and QR codes seamlessly. 

As more food brands require on-demand label printing, digital printing is becoming the go-to solution for efficiency and precision.

Smart Labels and Connected Packaging

With transparency becoming a key factor in consumer decision-making, brands are integrating smart food labels that provide interactive experiences. Labels featuring QR codes, NFC, and RFID technology allow consumers to access real-time product information, including ingredient sourcing, sustainability efforts, and nutritional details. A recent study by Accenture found that 72% of consumers are more likely to trust a brand that offers transparent product information through digital means. This trend is driving brands to use smart labels as a tool to enhance consumer engagement and supply chain visibility.

Minimalist and Transparent Food Labels

The “less is more” approach is becoming increasingly popular in food label design. Many brands are opting for transparent food labels, which create a sleek, modern look while allowing consumers to see the product inside. This style aligns with the clean-label movement, where transparency in both ingredients and packaging is valued. Transparent labels work exceptionally well for premium food and beverage products, enhancing their authenticity while providing an elegant, minimalist aesthetic.

Best Materials for Food Labels

Food label materials play a crucial role in ensuring both durability and sustainability. Stickers remain a widely used option, thanks to advancements in adhesive technology that allow them to withstand moisture and refrigeration. 

Transparent labels continue to be a favorite for beverages, glass jars, and organic food products, giving them a high-end appearance while maintaining product visibility.

For products with uniquely shaped bottles or containers, shrink sleeves offer a 360-degree branding solution, allowing brands to maximize space for vibrant graphics and essential product information. 

Additionally, as sustainability becomes a priority, more brands are turning to biodegradable and recycled food labels. These materials reduce environmental impact while meeting consumer demand for eco-friendly packaging solutions. 

When you select the right label material, your brand can enhance its packaging appeal while aligning with its sustainability goals.

The Future of Food Labels: Sustainability and Innovation

Sustainability is no longer just a marketing trend—it has become a business imperative. As environmental concerns continue to shape consumer behavior, brands that prioritize eco-friendly food labels will gain a competitive advantage. 

From using biodegradable materials to incorporating water-based, non-toxic inks, companies are adopting practices that support both product safety and environmental responsibility.

The rapid evolution of digital printing technology is also enabling food brands to stay agile in a dynamic market. Digital printing allows for personalization, cost-effective short runs, and high-speed production, giving brands the flexibility they need to respond to changing trends and consumer preferences. 

Moreover, innovations like smart labels and connected packaging are transforming food labels into interactive marketing tools that engage and educate consumers.

As the industry moves forward, the focus will remain on sustainability, digital transformation, and high-quality, visually appealing food labels. By adopting the latest printing technologies and eco-conscious materials, brands can ensure their labels stand out while meeting regulatory and consumer expectations. 

The future of food label printing is about more than just compliance—it’s about creating labels that inspire trust, enhance brand identity, and support a greener planet.

ArrowJet Line: Revolutionizing Food Label Printing

Arrow Systems, Inc. has introduced the ArrowJet Line, a series of digital label printers designed to meet the evolving needs of the food industry. Key features include:

  • High Resolution: Delivering up to 1600 x 1600 dpi for exceptional image quality.
  • Eco-Friendly Inks: Utilizing water-based pigment inks that comply with Nestlé guidelines, ensuring safety for food packaging applications.
  • Versatility: Compatible with a wide range of label materials, including biodegradable substrates and transparent films.
  • Efficiency: Achieving print speeds up to 150 meters per minute, facilitating high-volume production without compromising quality.

Key Takeaways:

✅ Eco-friendly labels are in demand, with brands shifting to biodegradable and recycled materials.

✅ Digital printing is transforming the industry, making food label production faster and more flexible.

✅ Smart labels enhance consumer trust through real-time product transparency. 

✅ Minimalist and transparent food labels appeal to modern, eco-conscious buyers.

✅ ArrowJet Line offers high-resolution, sustainable food label printing solutions tailored to market needs.

Final Thoughts

Food label printing is undergoing a transformation, driven by sustainability, digital advancements, and consumer demand for transparency. Whether brands opt for eco-friendly biodegradable labels, sleek transparent designs, or high-tech smart labels, they have an array of options to create impactful packaging. 

With the rise of digital printing, food brands can now produce high-quality labels with greater efficiency, customization, and cost-effectiveness with ArrowJet Solutions

If you’re looking to elevate your food label printing, now is the time to explore innovative solutions that align with market demands. 

Contact us today to discover how advanced printing technologies can transform your packaging and help your brand make a lasting impression.

The Role of Digital Printing in Personalizing Cookie Bags for Small Businesses

Introduction: Why Custom Cookie Bags Matter

In today’s competitive market, small businesses are constantly looking for ways to stand out. Custom cookie bags not only protect the product but also serve as a powerful marketing tool. Arrow Systems, Inc. is revolutionizing digital printing with our ArrowJet product line, offering small businesses the ability to print vibrant, custom designs on demand. Let’s explore how digital printing is transforming the cookie packaging industry and why small businesses should embrace it.

The Shift to Digital Printing in Cookie Packaging

Traditional Printing Challenges

For years, small businesses relied on flexographic and offset printing for their cookie packaging needs. While effective for large-scale production, these methods come with significant drawbacks, including:

  • High setup costs for plates and tooling
  • Long lead times that delay product launches
  • Lack of flexibility for small-batch orders
  • Limited customization for different designs or seasonal packaging

These challenges make it difficult for small bakeries and startups to scale and adapt to market trends. That’s where digital printing comes in.

Advantages of Digital Printing for Cookie Bags

Digital printing eliminates the need for plates and allows for short-run, on-demand printing, making it an ideal solution for small businesses. Here are some of the key benefits:

1. Unlimited Customization

With ArrowJet digital printers, businesses can print unique designs for each batch without additional setup costs. This means:

  • Seasonal and holiday-themed packaging
  • Limited-edition cookie bags
  • Custom packaging for corporate orders or events

2. No Minimum Order Quantities

Unlike traditional printing, where high order volumes are required to justify costs, digital printing allows businesses to print exactly what they need—whether it’s 50 bags or 5,000. This is especially useful for small businesses that want to test different designs or flavors.

3. Fast Turnaround Times

Since there’s no need for plate-making or long setup processes, digital printing delivers quick and efficient results. Small businesses can print new packaging designs in-house with ArrowJet’s high-speed printing solutions, reducing lead times and keeping up with market demand.

title.rendered: How to Choose the Right Material for Transparent Labels

content.rendered:
Table of Contents

How to Choose the Right Material for Transparent Labels

In today’s competitive marketplace, transparent labels have become a powerful tool for enhancing product appeal. They provide a sleek, modern look that allows the product to shine through while maintaining a clean design. However, choosing the right material for these labels is crucial, as it directly affects their durability, functionality, and overall impact. Selecting the appropriate material ensures that your product not only looks great but also withstands environmental factors, adhering securely to the packaging.

In this blog, we will explore different materials for transparent labels, discuss how to select the best option and dive into why choosing the right material is essential for both branding and product longevity.

Why Choosing the Right Material for Transparent Labels Matters

Choosing the right material for your transparent label is more than just about looks. It affects the label’s ability to stick to different surfaces, survive in various environments, and maintain a premium appearance throughout the product’s lifecycle. The right material can prevent fading, peeling, or damage, ensuring that your product looks its best from the factory to the consumer’s hands.

Types of Materials for Transparent Labels

Transparent labels can be made from various materials, each suited for different products and packaging needs. Here are five of the most commonly used materials and their benefits:

1. BOPP (Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene)

BOPP is a durable, water-resistant material commonly used in food, beverage, and cosmetic industries. Its resistance to moisture and oils makes it an ideal choice for products exposed to harsh environments. BOPP offers excellent clarity and a smooth finish, ensuring that your product maintains a premium look throughout its shelf life.

Key Benefits:

  • Water and oil resistance
  • Long-lasting durability
  • Ideal for food and beauty products

2. PET (Polyethylene Terephthalate)

PET is known for its exceptional clarity and durability, making it perfect for premium products like glass bottles and luxury packaging. It is tear-resistant and can withstand extreme temperatures, ensuring the Label remains intact and visually appealing, even in challenging conditions. PET is ideal for high-end, transparent labeling.

Key Benefits:

  • Excellent transparency
  • Tear-resistant
  • Great for luxury items

3. Vinyl

Vinyl is highly durable and suitable for outdoor or industrial applications due to its resistance to weather and environmental factors. It is often used for products that require labels to withstand extreme conditions, such as outdoor signage or equipment. Vinyl labels ensure longevity and are a top choice for products exposed to the elements.

Key Benefits:

  • Extreme durability
  • Weatherproof
  • Perfect for outdoor and industrial uses

4. Polypropylene

Polypropylene labels are flexible, water-resistant, and chemically resistant, making them suitable for products like squeezable containers or flexible packaging. This material offers a premium finish while maintaining its durability under harsh conditions. Polypropylene is a versatile option, combining both flexibility and resistance in various packaging scenarios.

Key Benefits:

 

  • High flexibility

  • Chemical resistance

  • Suitable for squeezable packaging

5. PVC (Polyvinyl Chloride)

PVC labels are strong, cost-effective, and can withstand environmental stress, making them versatile across multiple industries. They are particularly useful for heavy-duty applications and provide a sturdy option for products requiring extra durability. PVC’s affordability and strength make it a popular choice for a range of packaging types.

Key Benefits:

  • Strong and durable

     

  • Cost-effective

     

  • Suitable for various packaging types

How Transparent Labels Contribute to Product Appeal

Transparent labels are not just about function; they also contribute to a product’s visual appeal. Here are five ways transparent labels enhance a product’s overall look:

  • Minimalist Aesthetic
    Transparent labels allow the product’s packaging to take center stage. The label blends with the packaging, offering a clean, modern design that appeals to consumers looking for minimalism.

  • Versatility Across Industries
    Whether you’re in food, beauty, or electronics, transparent labels work across different packaging types, from glass to plastic, ensuring consistency in branding.

  • Highlighting Product Quality
    By using transparent labels, brands can showcase the product inside the packaging, which is particularly beneficial for food and beverages, allowing the consumer to see the quality upfront.

  • Customizable Designs
    Transparent labels offer flexibility in design. You can incorporate logos, text, and images without overwhelming the packaging, creating a premium look that’s easily customizable.

  • Creating a Premium Look
    The seamless appearance of transparent labels makes the packaging feel luxurious, elevating the overall perception of the product.

How Transparent Labels Appeal to Design-Conscious Consumers

Consumers today are more design-conscious than ever. They are drawn to products that not only meet their needs but also offer an aesthetically pleasing experience. Here’s how transparent labels appeal to such consumers:

  • Seamless Integration with Packaging
    Transparent labels create a smooth transition between the product and the label, allowing the packaging design to remain the focus.

  • Focus on Product Over Branding
    With a transparent label, the product is at the forefront, giving consumers the confidence to trust what they’re buying.

  • Enhances Unboxing Experience
    The transparency of the label gives a sleek finish, enhancing the consumer’s unboxing experience and making it more enjoyable.

  • Simplistic Elegance
    The minimalist design of transparent labels provides a clean and sophisticated look, which is favored by consumers who value simplicity in design.

  • Environmental Appeal
    Transparent labels, particularly those made from recyclable materials, resonate with eco-conscious consumers looking for sustainable products.

Versatility Across Packaging Types

Transparent labels are versatile and can be applied to various packaging types, ensuring flexibility and adaptability for brands. Here’s how they work across different packaging options:

  • Glass Bottles
    PET and vinyl labels offer superior clarity, making them ideal for glass bottles, ensuring the label does not detract from the product.

  • Plastic Containers
    BOPP and polypropylene labels adhere well to plastic, making them perfect for cosmetics, food, and household products.

  • Metal Cans
    PET is ideal for metal surfaces, providing a high-quality, seamless finish without compromising durability.

  • Flexible Packaging
    Polypropylene labels are flexible and resistant to water and chemicals, making them suitable for flexible packaging such as pouches and squeezable containers.

  • Outdoor Products
    Vinyl labels, with their weather-resistant properties, are ideal for outdoor products and industrial goods exposed to extreme conditions.

Cost-Effectiveness of Transparent Labels

Transparent labels are not only visually appealing but also cost-effective, offering brands a solution that combines aesthetics with practicality. Here’s how:

  • Lower Material Costs
    Materials like BOPP and polypropylene are relatively inexpensive compared to other premium label materials, making them affordable without sacrificing quality.

  • Durable and Long-Lasting
    The durability of transparent labels reduces the need for replacements or maintenance, saving brands money in the long run.

  • Reduced Packaging Costs
    Transparent labels often allow brands to use simpler packaging designs, reducing the need for additional design elements, which cuts down packaging costs.

  • Versatile Use Across Multiple Products
    Brands can use the same transparent label material across various product lines, streamlining the manufacturing process and reducing costs.

  • Minimal Waste
    Many transparent label materials, like PET, are recyclable, contributing to a more eco-friendly packaging solution and reducing waste management costs.

Conclusion: Trust Arrow Systems Inc. for Your Transparent Label Needs

Choosing the right material for transparent labels can make all the difference in product presentation and performance. Whether you’re looking for the durability of BOPP, the clarity of PET, or the flexibility of vinyl, selecting the right material ensures that your label enhances the product while standing up to environmental factors.

At Arrow Systems Inc we offer a wide range of transparent label materials tailored to meet your brand’s needs. Our experts can guide you through the selection process to ensure your labels not only look great but also perform under various conditions. Trust Arrow Systems Inc. to help you create the perfect transparent labels that elevate your brand’s aesthetics and ensure long-lasting success.
